definition_zh: 网络安全；保护计算机系统、网络与数据免受攻击、破坏或未经授权访问的实践与领域
definition_en: the practice and field of protecting computer systems, networks and data from attack, damage or unauthorised access
core_image: 银行内网的一块告警面板上，红色标记逐条亮起，值班人员一条条核对来源
scene: 银行内网每天收到大量试探登录，安全团队盯着告警面板逐个处置。 Strong cybersecurity kept the bank's customer records out of the breach.
sceneCN: 这里指保护系统与网络免受攻击的整体工作（第 1 个义项：保护计算机系统与网络免受攻击）；句意为有力的网络安全防护让银行客户记录没有落入泄露事件。图中可辨识物件：告警面板、登录窗口、锁形图标、值班表。

pos.zh: 网络安全；网络空间安全

senses.title: Protecting systems and networks
senses.definition: the work of defending computers, networks and data against unauthorised access, disruption or theft
senses.definitionCN: 保护计算机、网络与数据，防止未经授权的访问、破坏或窃取
senses.example: Strong cybersecurity kept the bank's customer records out of the breach.
senses.exampleCN: 有力的网络安全防护让银行客户记录没有落入泄露事件。
senses.why: Cyber names the networked space and security names freedom from harm, so the word is protection inside that space.
senses.whyCN: 前缀命名联网空间，后一词命名免于伤害，因此这个词就是那个空间内部的保护。

senses.title: The industry and profession
senses.definition: the companies, teams and careers built around defending networks
senses.definitionCN: 围绕网络防御建立的公司、团队与职业
senses.example: The firm hired a cybersecurity team before the product launch.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在产品发布前雇了一支网络安全团队。
senses.why: A defensive practice becomes a trade once the threat is constant enough to pay for.
senses.whyCN: 当威胁持续到值得付费，防御做法就变成一门行业。

senses.title: Defensive measures
senses.definition: the specific controls used to protect a system, such as firewalls, patches and access rules
senses.definitionCN: 用于保护系统的具体控制手段，如防火墙、补丁与访问规则
senses.example: Poor cybersecurity left an old password on the server.
senses.exampleCN: 糟糕的网络安全措施让服务器上留着一个旧密码。
senses.why: The abstract field is made of concrete measures, and the same word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的领域由具体措施组成，同一个词兼指两者。

senses.title: Defence of an organization
senses.definition: the arrangements by which an institution protects its records, money and services
senses.definitionCN: 机构保护其记录、资金与服务的一整套安排
senses.example: The audit found gaps in the ministry's cybersecurity.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现该部门的网络安全存在缺口。
senses.why: When the protected thing is an institution, the word names a management duty, not only a technology.
senses.whyCN: 当被保护的对象是机构，这个词命名的是一项管理职责，而不只是技术。

senses.title: National policy
senses.definition: the laws, agencies and strategies by which a state protects its networks and infrastructure
senses.definitionCN: 国家保护其网络与基础设施的法律、机构与战略
senses.example: The new law treats cybersecurity as part of public safety.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律把网络安全视为公共安全的一部分。
senses.why: Networks cross borders and carry public services, so defence rises from the firm to the state.
senses.whyCN: 网络跨越边界并承载公共服务，防御因此从企业上升到国家。

senses.title: Personal hygiene
senses.definition: the everyday habits by which an individual protects accounts, devices and data
senses.definitionCN: 个人保护账户、设备与数据的日常习惯
senses.example: Good cybersecurity starts with changing a reused password.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的网络安全从改掉重复使用的密码开始。
senses.why: The same defence shrinks to one person's habits, where most breaches actually begin.
senses.whyCN: 同一套防御缩到一个人的习惯上，而多数泄露正是从这里开始。

senses.title: An academic discipline
senses.definition: the study of attacks, defences and risk, taught as a subject with its own methods
senses.definitionCN: 研究攻击、防御与风险的学问，作为一门有自身方法的学科来教授
senses.example: The university added a degree in cybersecurity last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学去年增设了网络安全学位。
senses.why: Once defence has methods and evidence, it can be taught and researched like any other field.
senses.whyCN: 当防御有了方法与证据，它就能像其他领域一样被教授与研究。

senses.title: The threat landscape
senses.definition: the changing set of attackers, methods and vulnerabilities that defenders must track
senses.definitionCN: 防御者必须跟踪的攻击者、手法与漏洞的变动集合
senses.example: Ransomware changed the cybersecurity picture for small clinics.
senses.exampleCN: 勒索软件改变了小诊所的网络安全格局。
senses.why: The word also names the problem, not only the answer, because defence is defined by what it faces.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也命名问题而不只是答案，因为防御由它所面对的东西来定义。

intro.en: Cybersecurity joins cyber-, from cybernetics, coined by Norbert Wiener in 1948 from Greek kybernetes 'steersman', with security, from Latin securitas and securus 'free from care'. The compound became common in the 1990s; the exact first use is source uncertain.
intro.cn: cybersecurity 由 cyber-（源自维纳一九四八年据希腊 kybernetes「舵手」造出的 cybernetics）与 security（拉丁 securitas、securus「无忧」）组合。该复合词在二十世纪九十年代普及；最早用例来源不确定。

items.en: Greek kybernetes meant a steersman or governor, the person who steers a ship and keeps it on course.
items.cn: 希腊 kybernetes 指舵手或掌舵者，即驾驶船只并使其保持航向的人。

items.en: Norbert Wiener used cybernetics for the study of control and communication in animals and machines, taking the Greek steering word.
items.cn: 维纳用 cybernetics 指对动物与机器中控制与通信的研究，取自那个希腊「掌舵」词。

items.en: From the 1960s cyber- was attached to spaces and activities that were networked, giving cyberspace, cybercrime and later cyberattack.
items.cn: 二十世纪六十年代起，cyber- 被加到联网的空间与活动上，造出网络空间、网络犯罪，后来又造出网络攻击。

items.en: Latin securus meant free from care, built from se- 'without' and cura 'care', and English secure and security come from it.
items.cn: 拉丁 securus 指无忧，由 se-「无」与 cura「忧虑」构成，英语 secure 与 security 由此而来。

items.en: Latin securitas named freedom from danger or care, and English security widened it to protection, guarantees and financial instruments.
items.cn: 拉丁 securitas 指免于危险或忧虑，英语 security 把它扩展到保护、担保与金融工具。

items.en: The two parts were joined in the 1990s as networks became central to business and government; the earliest written use is source uncertain.
items.cn: 两部分在二十世纪九十年代网络成为商业与政府核心时被连起来；最早书面用例来源不确定。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like cybersecurity; the second group names neighbouring ideas in the same field.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「cybersecurity」相近；第二组是同一领域里意思相邻的其他说法。

entries.definition: A prefix or adjective meaning networked or computer-based.
entries.definitionCN: 表示联网或计算机化的前缀或形容词。

entries.definition: The imagined space of networks, built with the same steering prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 由网络构成的想象空间，同用那个「掌舵」前缀。

entries.definition: The study of control and communication, the source of the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 研究控制与通信的学问，是该前缀的来源。

entries.definition: Protection from danger, the second element of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 免于危险的保护，是复合词的第二部分。

entries.definition: Crime carried out through networks, the thing this field defends against.
entries.definitionCN: 经网络实施的犯罪，正是这一领域要防御的对象。

entries.definition: Protection of information wherever it is held, whether or not networked.
entries.definitionCN: 保护无论存于何处的信息，不论是否联网。

entries.definition: Protection of the links and traffic between machines.
entries.definitionCN: 保护机器之间的链路与流量。

entries.definition: The ability to keep working and recover after an attack, rather than only to prevent it.
entries.definitionCN: 遭攻击后仍能运作并恢复的能力，而不只是预防。

entries.definition: Active measures to detect and respond to attacks, often in a military or national setting.
entries.definitionCN: 侦测并回应攻击的主动措施，常用于军事或国家语境。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek steering word, the real Latin care word and real policy phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实希腊「掌舵」词、真实拉丁「忧虑」词与真实政策搭配。

normal.en: Cybernetics comes from Greek kybernetes, a steersman, and Norbert Wiener coined it in 1948.
normal.cn: cybernetics 来自希腊 kybernetes「舵手」，由维纳于一九四八年造出。

normal.en: Security comes from Latin securus, free from care, built from se- 'without' and cura 'care'.
normal.cn: security 来自拉丁 securus「无忧」，由 se-「无」与 cura「忧虑」构成。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: cybersecurity threat, policy, firm, awareness, framework.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各支：网络安全威胁、政策、公司、意识、框架。

normal.en: A firewall, a patch and an access rule are all concrete members of the field.
normal.cn: 防火墙、补丁与访问规则都是这一领域的具体成员。

normal.en: The field is defined by what it defends against, so the threat landscape is part of it.
normal.cn: 这一领域由它所防御的东西来定义，因此威胁格局也是它的一部分。

abstract.en: Cybersecurity is a lock on a door that opens onto the whole world.
abstract.cn: 网络安全是装在一扇通向全世界的门上的锁。

abstract.en: The defenders must be right every day; the attacker needs one good night.
abstract.cn: 防御者每天都要做对，攻击者只需要一个好夜晚。

abstract.en: Most breaches begin with one small habit, which is why the field reaches down to individuals.
abstract.cn: 多数泄露始于一个小习惯，这就是这一领域延伸到个人的原因。

examples.en: The hospital increased its cybersecurity budget after a phishing attack.
examples.cn: 在一次钓鱼攻击后，医院增加了网络安全预算。

examples.en: Cybersecurity is now taught in schools as part of digital literacy.
examples.cn: 网络安全如今作为数字素养的一部分在学校教授。

examples.en: A single weak password can defeat years of cybersecurity.
examples.cn: 一个弱密码就能击穿多年的网络安全防护。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赛博 + 安全」——网络那片空间里的门锁与巡逻

root: cyber- 源自 cybernetics（维纳一九四八年据希腊 kybernetes「舵手」造出）；security 源自拉丁 securus「无忧」= se- 无 + cura 忧虑。复合词二十世纪九十年代普及，最早用例来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one defence inside a network: protecting systems, an industry, concrete measures, an institution's duty, national policy, personal habits, a discipline, and the threat landscape itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一场网络空间里的防御：保护系统、一个产业、具体措施、机构职责、国家政策、个人习惯、一门学科，以及威胁格局本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bank's warning panel lighting up row by row while an analyst checks each source.
core.cn: 核心意象：银行告警面板逐条亮起，分析员核对每一个来源。

branches.en: THE DEFENCE AND ITS MEASURES: abstract protection is made of firewalls, patches and rules.
branches.cn: 防御与措施：抽象的保护由防火墙、补丁与规则组成。

branches.en: THE TRADE AND THE SCHOOL: constant threat turns defence into a career and then into a taught discipline.
branches.cn: 行业与学堂：持续的威胁把防御变成职业，再变成被教授的学科。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION AND THE STATE: a firm protects its records, and a state protects networks that carry public services.
branches.cn: 机构与国家：企业保护记录，国家保护承载公共服务的网络。

branches.en: THE PERSON: most breaches start with one habit, so the field reaches down to the individual.
branches.cn: 个人：多数泄露始于一个习惯，因此这一领域延伸到个人。

branches.en: THE PROBLEM: the changing set of attackers and weaknesses half-defines the defence.
branches.cn: 问题：不断变化的攻击者与弱点，反过来定义了防御的一半。

intro.en: Cybersecurity joins the Greek steering prefix cyber- with the Latin care word behind security.
intro.cn: cybersecurity 把希腊「掌舵」前缀 cyber- 与 security 背后的拉丁「忧虑」词连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Greek kybernetes gives cybernetics and the prefix cyber-; Latin securus gives secure and security; English joins them into cybersecurity.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 kybernetes 衍生 cybernetics 与前缀 cyber-；拉丁 securus 衍生 secure 与 security；英语把它们连成 cybersecurity。

items.exampleCN: 维纳一九四八年的造词。

items.example: The prefix names the space being defended.
items.exampleCN: 前缀命名被防御的空间。

definition_zh: 使现代化；更新设备与技术；改革制度；使（语言、拼写、建筑）现代化；现代化（不及物，少用）
definition_en: to make something modern in style, equipment, method or organization
core_image: 磨坊的旧皮带轮已经磨得发滑，账本上的维修费一年比一年高
scene: 磨坊的皮带轮已经磨得发滑，账本上的维修费一年比一年高， The old mill must modernize its equipment or close.
sceneCN: 这里 modernize 指「更新设备与技术」（第 2 个义项：技术设备更新）；句意为这座老磨坊必须更新设备，否则就得关门。图中可辨识物件：磨滑的皮带轮、维修账本、待换的新齿轮、关门的木牌。

pos.zh: 使现代化；更新设备；改革制度；使现代化（不及物，少用）

senses.title: Make modern in style or design
senses.titleCN: 在风格或设计上使现代化
senses.definition: to change the appearance or design of something so that it looks contemporary
senses.definitionCN: 改变某物的外观或设计，使其看起来属于当代
senses.example: They modernized the lobby with glass and steel.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用玻璃与钢材使大堂现代化。
senses.why: The verb starts with the visible: what looks old is made to look new.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词从可见处开始：看起来旧的东西被弄得看起来新。

senses.title: Update equipment and technology
senses.definition: to replace old machines or systems with newer and more efficient ones
senses.definitionCN: 用更新、更高效的机器或系统替换旧的
senses.example: The old mill must modernize its equipment or close.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老磨坊必须更新设备，否则就得关门。
senses.why: Here the verb has a hard test: if the old machine still turns, it can wait; if it slips, modernization becomes urgent.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词有一道硬检验：旧机器还能转就还能等；一旦打滑，现代化就变得紧迫。

senses.title: Reform institutions and laws
senses.definition: to bring government, law or administration into a modern form
senses.definitionCN: 使政府、法律或行政进入现代形式
senses.example: The new state modernized its courts before it built its railways.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新国家先改革了法院，再修铁路。
senses.why: The verb can act on abstractions: a code, a ministry or a tax system can be brought up to date.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以对抽象物起作用：一部法典、一个部门或一套税制都可以被更新。

senses.title: Bring a society to modern industry
senses.definition: to transform an economy or society by introducing industry, wage labour and modern infrastructure
senses.definitionCN: 通过引入工业、雇佣劳动与现代基础设施来改造经济或社会
senses.example: The plan aimed to modernize the whole province within twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划打算在二十年内使全省现代化。
senses.why: The verb can take a whole society as its object, and then it means the entire package of industry, cities and administration.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以拿整个社会作宾语，此时它指工业、城市与行政的整套组合。

senses.title: Modernize language or spelling
senses.definition: to change spelling, vocabulary or usage to match current practice
senses.definitionCN: 改变拼写、词汇或用法，以符合当前惯例
senses.example: The editors modernized the spelling but kept the punctuation.
senses.exampleCN: 编者把拼写现代化了，却保留了原来的标点。
senses.why: Language is inherited too, so the same verb can be applied to orthography: old letters are replaced by current ones.
senses.whyCN: 语言也是继承来的，因此同一个动词可以用在正字法上：旧字母被当下的字母替换。

senses.title: Renovate a building or facility
senses.definition: to repair and update a building so that it meets current standards
senses.definitionCN: 修缮并更新一栋建筑，使其符合当前标准
senses.example: The library was modernized without losing its reading room.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆被现代化了，却没有丢掉它的阅览室。
senses.why: A building can be modernized inside while its shell stays old, which shows that the verb changes systems rather than age.
senses.whyCN: 一栋建筑可以内部现代化、外壳仍旧，这说明动词改的是系统，而不是年岁。

senses.title: Adopt modern methods
senses.definition: to switch to current techniques in farming, industry or administration
senses.definitionCN: 在农业、工业或行政中改用当前技术
senses.example: The cooperative modernized its irrigation and doubled the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 合作社使灌溉现代化，收成翻了一倍。
senses.why: The object can be a method rather than a thing: what is modernized is the way work is done.
senses.whyCN: 宾语可以是方法而非物件：被现代化的是做事的方式。

senses.title: Become modern (intransitive, rare)
senses.definition: to become modern without an explicit object, used mainly in older or technical writing
senses.definitionCN: 不带明确宾语地变得现代，主要用于较早或专业写作
senses.example: The town modernized slowly, one street at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇慢慢地现代化，一次一条街。
senses.why: Most uses are transitive, but the verb can stand alone when the subject is the thing changing itself.
senses.whyCN: 多数用法是及物的，但当主语就是自行变化之物时，这个动词也可以单独使用。

intro.en: Modernize is modern plus the verb ending -ize, which reached English through Latin from Greek -izein. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: modernize 是 modern 加动词词尾 -ize 构成，后者经拉丁语从希腊语 -izein 进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Modo meant just now; it is usually derived from modus, measure or manner, though that link is a standard account rather than a certainty.
items.cn: modo 意为「刚刚」；通行说法认为它来自 modus「尺度、方式」，但这一联系只是标准解释，并非确证。

items.en: Late Latin modernus, of the present time, was built from the time word plus -nus and reached English through French.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 modernus 意为「当下的」，由这个时间词加 -nus 构成，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: The ending -ize came through Latin -izare from Greek -izein, meaning to make, practise or become.
items.cn: 词尾 -ize 经拉丁语 -izare 来自希腊语 -izein，意为「使、从事或成为」。

items.en: French moderniser appeared in the eighteenth century, and English modernize followed the same pattern.
items.cn: 法语 moderniser 在十八世纪出现，英语 modernize 沿用了同一构词方式。

items.en: English modernize first meant to give a modern form to language or design, and later extended to industry and institutions.
items.cn: 英语 modernize 最初指给语言或设计以现代形式，后来扩展到工业与制度。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of modernize is not securely dated, and the pre-Latin origin of modo and modus remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：modernize 在英语中的最早使用没有确切年代；modo 与 modus 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds members of the same modern- family; the second holds verbs of improvement that are often used in its place.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 modern- 词族的成员；第二组是常被用来替代它的「改进」类动词。

entries.definition: The process of making modern; modernize is the verb that names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 使现代化的过程；modernize 是命名该动作的动词。

entries.definition: Belonging to the present age; the adjective describes the result, while the verb describes the act of producing it.
entries.definitionCN: 属于当下时代的；形容词描述结果，动词描述产生结果的动作。

entries.definition: The state of being modern; the verb cannot be replaced by this noun without losing the action.
entries.definitionCN: 现代的状态；这个名词不能替代动词，否则动作就丢了。

entries.definition: The cultural movement that broke with inherited forms; it is a programme, not an act of upgrading.
entries.definitionCN: 打破继承形式的文化运动；它是一套纲领，不是升级动作。

entries.definition: To add the latest information or changes; narrower than modernize, which can mean a whole social process.
entries.definitionCN: 加入最新信息或改动；比 modernize 窄，后者可指整个社会过程。

entries.definition: To replace something with a better version; it usually applies to one item, while modernize can apply to a system.
entries.definitionCN: 用更好的版本替换；通常用于单件物品，而 modernize 可用于整个系统。

entries.definition: To restore a building to good condition; it may keep the old style, while modernize changes the style or system.
entries.definitionCN: 把建筑修复到良好状态；它可能保留旧风格，而 modernize 会改变风格或系统。

entries.definition: To change an institution for the better; it stresses improvement, while modernize stresses becoming current.
entries.definitionCN: 为改善而改变制度；它强调改善，而 modernize 强调变得合乎当下。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real modern stem, the real make-verb ending and the phrases the verb actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 modern 词干、表示「使……」的真实动词词尾，以及这个动词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: modern plus the make-verb ending: the word means to make modern, as activate means to make active.
normal.cn: modern 加表示「使……」的动词词尾：这个词意为「使现代」，就像 activate 意为「使活动」。

normal.en: The family runs modern, modernize, modernization, modernizer, modernity and modernism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 modern（现代的）、modernize（使现代化）、modernization（现代化）、modernizer（推动现代化的人）、modernity（现代性）、modernism（现代主义）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: modernize equipment, modernize the economy, modernize spelling.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：更新设备、使经济现代化、使拼写现代化。

normal.en: The verb is transitive most of the time: someone modernizes something.
normal.cn: 这个动词多数时候是及物的：某人使某物现代化。

normal.en: A useful contrast: renovate repairs, upgrade improves one item, modernize brings a whole system up to date.
normal.cn: 有用的对照：renovate 是修复，upgrade 是改进单件，modernize 是把整套系统更新到当下。

abstract.en: Picture a worn belt being cut and a new one fitted while the wheels keep turning.
abstract.cn: 想象一条磨坏的皮带被剪下，新皮带装上，而轮子还在转。

abstract.en: Picture an old courtroom with new record books and the same wooden bench.
abstract.cn: 想象一间旧法庭，换了新记录册，木凳还是原来那张。

abstract.en: Picture a page of old spelling with every long s crossed out.
abstract.cn: 想象一页旧拼写，每个长 s 都被划掉。

examples.en: The city modernized its water system before the old pipes burst.
examples.cn: 这座城市在旧管道爆裂之前更新了供水系统。

examples.en: She modernized the workshop without firing a single carpenter.
examples.cn: 她把作坊现代化了，却没有辞退一名木匠。

examples.en: The publisher modernized the text but refused to modernize its jokes.
examples.cn: 出版社把文本现代化了，却拒绝改动其中的笑话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩登」加「使……」——把旧东西弄成摩登样子，就是使现代化。

root: 由 modern 加动词词尾 -ize 构成。modern 来自晚期拉丁语 modernus「当下的」，通行说法追溯至 modo「刚刚」，modo 又常被解释为来自 modus「尺度、方式」；-ize 经拉丁语 -izare 源自希腊语 -izein「使、成为」。modo 与 modus 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of making current: a look, a machine, a court, a society, a spelling, a building, a method and finally a town changing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「使合乎当下」的动作展开：外观、机器、法院、社会、拼写、建筑、方法，最后是一座自行变化的小镇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn belt replaced while the wheels keep turning.
core.cn: 核心意象：磨坏的皮带被替换，而轮子仍在转。

branches.en: SURFACE AND SHELL: a lobby and a library can be made current without changing what they are.
branches.cn: 表面与外壳：大堂与图书馆都可以被更新，而不改变它们是什么。

branches.en: MACHINE AND METHOD: equipment and technique are two ways of doing work differently.
branches.cn: 机器与方法：设备与技术是改变做事方式的两条路。

branches.en: LAW: courts and codes are brought up to date before the railways arrive.
branches.cn: 法律：法院与法典在铁路到来之前就先更新。

branches.en: SOCIETY: the verb can take a whole province as its object.
branches.cn: 社会：这个动词可以拿整个省作宾语。

branches.en: LANGUAGE AND SELF-CHANGE: spelling can be modernized, and a town can modernize itself.
branches.cn: 语言与自行变化：拼写可以被现代化，一座小镇也可以自行现代化。

intro.en: Modernize is a time adjective plus a make-verb ending, and the inflections are perfectly regular.
intro.cn: modernize 是一个时间形容词加一个表示「使……」的动词词尾，其屈折变化完全规则。

latinIntro.en: Latin modo and modernus supply modern, and Greek -izein through Latin -izare supplies the verb ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modo 与 modernus 提供 modern，希腊语 -izein 经拉丁语 -izare 提供动词词尾。

items.example: The adverb is usually linked to modus, measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词通常被联系到 modus「尺度」。

items.example: The adjective entered English through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词经法语进入英语。

items.example: The ending builds modernize and organize.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 modernize（使现代化）与 organize（组织）。

items.example: The harbour was modernized last year.
items.exampleCN: 这座港口去年完成了现代化。

items.meaning: in the act of making modern
items.exampleCN: 现代化委员会每周开会。
这位现代化推动者订购了新织机。

definition_zh: v. 使着迷，吸引住；使倾心
definition_en: to hold someone attention completely; to win someone affection strongly
core_image: 木偶一举手，孩子的眼睛就再没离开过
scene: 木偶戏让孩子一动不动，连糖都忘了吃。 The puppet show captivated the child for a full hour.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：captivate 指完全吸引住注意力；句意是木偶戏让孩子一动不动看了整整一小时。

pos.zh: 使着迷；吸引住

senses.title: To hold attention completely
senses.definition: to take and keep all of someone attention, so that nothing else matters
senses.definitionCN: 占据并保持某人全部注意力，使别的事情都不重要
senses.example: The lecture captivated the whole room.
senses.exampleCN: 那场讲座让全场入迷。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to take captive, and attention can be taken the same way.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词原意为「使成俘虏」，注意力也可以这样被夺走。

senses.title: To win affection
senses.definition: to attract someone so strongly that they feel drawn to you
senses.definitionCN: 强烈吸引某人，使其心向你
senses.example: Her honesty captivated him long before her wit.
senses.exampleCN: 早在她展现机智之前，她的坦诚就让他倾心。
senses.why: The word moves from holding the mind to holding the heart.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从占据头脑转向占据人心。

intro.en: Captivate comes from Latin captivare, to take captive.
intro.cn: captivate 源自拉丁语 captivare，意为使成俘虏。

items.en: Capere means to seize.
items.cn: capere 意为抓取。

items.en: Captivus means a prisoner.
items.cn: captivus 意为俘虏。

items.en: Captivare means to take captive.
items.cn: captivare 意为使成俘虏。

items.en: Captivate means to make a prisoner.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语意为使成俘虏。

items.en: Captivate comes to mean to charm.
items.cn: 十七世纪转指使人着迷。

items.en: Captivate means to hold attention.
items.cn: 现代指牢牢吸引注意力。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the capt- root; the near-meaning group ranks attraction from simple interest to something close to a spell.
note.cn: 形近组共享 capt- 词根；近义组把吸引力从单纯有兴趣排到近乎施咒。

entries.definition: Kept as a prisoner.
entries.definitionCN: 被俘的；俘虏。

entries.definition: To catch or record.
entries.definitionCN: 捕获；捕捉。

entries.definition: Quick to find small faults.
entries.definitionCN: 吹毛求疵的。

entries.definition: To please and attract people easily.
entries.definitionCN: 使人喜爱。

entries.definition: To fill someone with wonder and hold them.
entries.definitionCN: 使入迷。

entries.definition: To hold attention as if by hypnosis.
entries.definitionCN: 使着迷。

entries.definition: To charm completely.
entries.definitionCN: 施魔法于；使着迷。

normalIntro.en: To captivate is to capture someone without touching them.
normalIntro.cn: captivate 就是不碰对方地「抓住」他。

normal.en: Captivus is a prisoner.
normal.cn: captivus 是俘虏。

normal.en: To captivate is to make one.
normal.cn: to captivate 就是使人成为俘虏。

normal.en: Attention is what gets captured.
normal.cn: 被俘获的是注意力。

normal.en: A good story does it quietly.
normal.cn: 好故事悄无声息地做到这点。

normal.en: The heart can be captured too.
normal.cn: 心也能被俘获。

abstract.en: A room that forgets its clock.
abstract.cn: 忘了看钟的一个房间。

abstract.en: Attention held without a hand.
abstract.cn: 不用手就按住的注意力。

abstract.en: A spell made of sentences.
abstract.cn: 由句子构成的咒语。

examples.en: The dancer captivated everyone in the hall.
examples.cn: 那位舞者让全场人着迷。

examples.en: He was captivated by her quiet confidence.
examples.cn: 他被她安静的自信吸引住了。

examples.en: It is a captivating account of a difficult year.
examples.cn: 那是对艰难一年的精彩叙述。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开普提维特」——一开口就把人提摄住，动弹不得。

root: 拉丁 capere（抓取）→ captivare（使成俘虏）→ 使着迷

sensesIntro.en: The prisoner and the enchanted listener share one condition: they cannot leave.
sensesIntro.cn: 俘虏与入迷的听众共享一种状态：他们走不开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child frozen in front of a puppet stage
core.cn: 核心意象：站在木偶台前一动不动的小孩

branches.en: A hall that stops talking.
branches.cn: 忽然安静下来的礼堂。

branches.en: A story that outlasts the clock.
branches.cn: 长过钟表的一场故事。

branches.en: A heart won by honesty.
branches.cn: 被坦诚赢得的心。

branches.en: Someone drawn back again and again.
branches.cn: 一再被吸引回来的人。

branches.en: A hold that feels pleasant.
branches.cn: 令人愉快的掌控。

intro.en: Captivate is captive turned into a verb; the list below covers its endings and the vocabulary of charm.
intro.cn: captivate 是由 captive 转化来的动词；下面列出其词尾以及「魅力」词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin captivare is to take captive, capere is to seize, and fascinum is a spell.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 captivare 意为使成俘虏，capere 意为抓取，fascinum 意为咒语。

latinEntries.exampleCN: capere 产生 capture 与 captive。

definition_zh: 归纳的；由个别到一般的；感应的；诱导的
definition_en: relating to reasoning that moves from particular cases to a general rule, or to effects produced without direct contact
core_image: 七个样本按颜色排成一列，一条细线从最左端拉到最右端，线的另一端写着一条通则
scene: 地质课上，学生把七块岩石样本按颗粒大小排成一列，然后写下一条适用于整层的判断。 Her inductive method turned seven samples into a single working rule.
sceneCN: 这里 inductive 指「由个别样本推向一般规则的」（第 2 个义项：由个别到一般）；句意为她的归纳方法把七块样本变成了一条可用的规则。

pos.zh: 归纳的；由个别到一般的；感应的；可被诱导的

collocations.zh: 归纳偏置（机器学习术语）

derivatives.zh: 归纳；感应（形容词背后的名词，指该过程或该现象）
以归纳方式（形容词加副词后缀）
归纳的性质（形容词加名词后缀）
电感器（拉丁动词加表器具的后缀，指利用感应的元件）

senses.title: Of inductive reasoning
senses.definition: belonging to the kind of inference that generalizes from observed cases
senses.definitionCN: 属于从被观察事例进行概括的那类推理
senses.example: Inductive reasoning cannot prove a rule, only support it.
senses.exampleCN: 归纳推理无法证明一条规则，只能支持它。
senses.why: The adjective simply labels the process named by the noun behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是给它背后那个名词所指的过程贴上标签。

senses.title: Proceeding from particulars to a general
senses.definition: describing a method that starts with individual facts and ends with a wider statement
senses.definitionCN: 形容从个别事实开始、以较宽陈述结束的方法
senses.example: Her inductive method turned seven samples into a single working rule.
senses.exampleCN: 她的归纳方法把七块样本变成了一条可用的规则。
senses.why: Direction is the whole point: the same facts read upward give a rule, read downward give instances.
senses.whyCN: 方向就是全部要点：同样的事实往上读得到规则，往下读得到实例。

senses.title: Of electrical induction
senses.definition: describing effects produced in a conductor by a changing magnetic field
senses.definitionCN: 形容由变化磁场在导体中产生的效应
senses.example: Inductive coupling charges the smaller coil without a wire.
senses.exampleCN: 电感耦合不用导线就给较小的线圈充电。
senses.why: Here nothing is led in physically; a state appears in a nearby body, which is the old image at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有东西被实际引入；一种状态出现在邻近物体上，这是那个古老意象的远距离版本。

senses.title: Of an inductor
senses.definition: in electronics, describing a component that stores energy in a magnetic field
senses.definitionCN: 在电子学中，形容以磁场储存能量的元件
senses.example: The inductive load made the switch arc.
senses.exampleCN: 电感负载使开关产生了电弧。
senses.why: A component is named for the effect it exploits, so the adjective attaches to hardware.
senses.whyCN: 元件因它所利用的效应而得名，于是这个形容词附着到硬件上。

senses.title: Capable of being induced
senses.definition: able to be brought about or brought on by an outside agent
senses.definitionCN: 能够被外部因素引起或触发的
senses.example: Some genes are inductive only under stress.
senses.exampleCN: 有些基因只在应激时才可被诱导。
senses.why: The passive possibility is expressed by the same ending that marks other capacities.
senses.whyCN: 被动的可能性由标记其他「能力」的同一词尾表达。

senses.title: Introductory or leading on
senses.definition: in older usage, describing remarks that lead the hearer into a subject
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧的用法中，形容把听者引入某个话题的开场话
senses.example: His inductive remarks prepared the audience for the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 他那段开场话为听众进入论证做了铺垫。
senses.why: The literal sense of leading someone in survives in this mild rhetorical use.
senses.whyCN: 「把某人领进来」的字面义在这种温和的修辞用法中留存。

senses.title: Empirical, based on observation
senses.definition: resting on what has been observed rather than on principles fixed in advance
senses.definitionCN: 依据已被观察到的内容，而非事先固定的原则
senses.example: The study took an inductive route, gathering cases before framing a theory.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究走归纳路线，先收集案例，再提出理论。
senses.why: When no framework is given, the only way forward is to look first and generalize later.
senses.whyCN: 在没有现成框架时，唯一的前进方式就是先看、后概括。

senses.title: A built-in assumption in learning systems
senses.definition: in machine learning, describing the assumptions a model makes in order to generalize from limited data
senses.definitionCN: 在机器学习中，形容模型为了从有限数据泛化而作出的假设
senses.example: Every model carries an inductive bias of some kind.
senses.exampleCN: 每个模型都带着某种归纳偏置。
senses.why: A machine that generalizes must be tilted toward some patterns, and the older word supplies the label.
senses.whyCN: 要泛化的机器必须偏向某些模式，这个古老的词为此提供了标签。

intro.en: Inductive is the adjective built on induction, with a Latin ending meaning 'having the nature of'. Its history is the history of the noun.
intro.cn: inductive 是建立在 induction 之上的形容词，带一个意为「具有……性质」的拉丁词尾。它的历史就是那个名词的历史。

items.en: The verb meant 'to lead'; the whole family is about direction of movement, literal or mental.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「引领」；整个词族都关乎运动的方向，无论是实际还是心智上的。

items.en: The compound meant 'to lead in', and its participle supplied the stem that English adjectives use.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为「引入」，它的分词提供了英语形容词所用的词干。

items.en: Late Latin formed an adjective on the participle, meaning 'of a bringing in'; it passed into the modern languages as a label for a kind of argument.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语在这个分词上造出形容词，意为「属于引入的」；它作为某类论证的标签传入近代语言。

items.en: English adopted the adjective in the sixteenth century, at first for rhetorical and then for logical use.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪接受了这个形容词，先用于修辞，后用于逻辑。

items.en: Physics gave the word its electrical sense, and engineering extended it to components that exploit the effect.
items.cn: 物理学给了它「电」这一义，工程学又把它扩展到利用该效应的元件上。

items.en: Learning theory and machine learning reused the word for the assumptions that allow generalization from limited data. Source uncertain: the deeper origin of the leading verb is not settled.
items.cn: 学习理论与机器学习再次使用这个词，指使有限数据得以泛化的那些假设。来源不确定：那个「引领」动词的更早来源没有定论。

note.en: The first group holds words that differ from inductive by a prefix or an ending; the second holds near neighbours in method.
note.cn: 第一组是与 inductive 只差一个前缀或词尾的词；第二组是方法上的近义词。

entries.definition: The same adjective pattern with a prefix meaning 'down from': it starts from general rules and works toward cases.
entries.definitionCN: 同样的形容词模式，前缀却意为「由……而下」：从通则出发走向个别情形。

entries.definition: The process or event itself; the adjective is used to modify a method, a step or a reasoning type.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程或事件本身；形容词用来修饰方法、步骤或推理类型。

entries.definition: The past participle: it says that something was brought about, not that a method generalizes.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词：说的是某事被引起，而不是某种方法在做概括。

entries.definition: A device, not a method; the ending marks a thing rather than a property.
entries.definitionCN: 指器件而非方法；词尾标记的是物，而不是性质。

entries.definition: It stresses reliance on observed data, which inductive methods usually need but do not define.
entries.definitionCN: 强调依赖观察数据；归纳方法通常需要它，但并不等于它。

entries.definition: A philosophical label for knowledge that comes after experience, wider than any one method.
entries.definitionCN: 哲学术语，指经验之后获得的知识，比任何一种方法都宽。

entries.definition: It describes work set up to produce observations, whereas inductive describes how conclusions are drawn from them.
entries.definitionCN: 形容为产生观察而安排的工作，而 inductive 形容如何从中得出结论。

entries.definition: It names a mathematical apparatus for generalizing from samples, one modern form of inductive work.
entries.definitionCN: 指从样本概括的一套数学工具，是归纳工作的现代形态之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'in' and the verb means 'lead': inductive work leads the mind inward from cases to a rule.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「向内」，动词意为「引领」：归纳工作把心智从事例领向一条规则。

normal.en: The family runs induce, induction, inductive, inductively, inductiveness, inductor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 induce、induction、inductive、inductively、inductiveness、inductor。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: inductive reasoning, inductive method, inductive coupling.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：归纳推理、归纳方法、电感耦合。

normal.en: The opposite adjective is deductive, which travels the other way with the other prefix.
normal.cn: 反义的形容词是 deductive，用另一个前缀走相反方向。

normal.en: Machine learning speaks of an inductive bias, the tilt that lets a model generalize.
normal.cn: 机器学习讲「归纳偏置」，即让模型得以泛化的那种偏向。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled from many small pegs into one knot.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳从许多小木桩上收拢成一个结。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder whose rungs are separate facts.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，每一级横档都是一个单独的事实。

abstract.en: Picture a magnet that makes a nearby needle turn before it is touched.
abstract.cn: 想象一块磁铁让旁边的针在被碰之前就转了方向。

examples.en: Inductive reasoning is powerful in discovery and weak in proof.
examples.cn: 归纳推理在发现上很有力，在证明上很弱。

examples.en: The team took an inductive approach, coding interviews before forming categories.
examples.cn: 团队采取归纳进路，先编码访谈，再形成类别。

examples.en: Inductive charging heats the phone less than a cable does.
examples.cn: 感应充电比线缆充电让手机发热更少。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（向内）+ duct（引领）+ ive（具有……性质的）＝ 把心智从个别事例领向通则的 → 归纳的。

root: 拉丁 inductivus「属于引入的」，来自 inducere「领进来」，由 in-「向内」+ ducere「引领」构成；更早来源不确定。同族有 induction、induce、deductive、inductor。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective's reach. It can label a kind of inference, a direction of method, an electrical effect, a component, a capacity to be brought about, an introductory remark, an empirical stance, or an assumption built into a model.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个形容词的覆盖范围展开。它可以标记一类推理、一种方法的方向、一种电效应、一个元件、一种可被引起的性质、一段开场话、一种经验立场，或一个被装进模型里的假设。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn from many separate dots up to a single knot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条线从许多分散的点拉向一个结。

chain: A TILT BUILT INTO THE MODEL

branches.en: THE LABEL AND THE DIRECTION: what kind of inference it is, and which way it travels.
branches.cn: 标签与方向：它是哪一类推理，以及它朝哪边行进。

branches.en: LOOK FIRST: when no framework exists, observation must come before the rule.
branches.cn: 先看：没有框架时，观察必须走在规则之前。

branches.en: ACROSS A GAP: the effect arrives without contact, and then the hardware is named for it.
branches.cn: 越过空隙：效应不接触就到达，随后硬件因它得名。

branches.en: BROUGHT ABOUT, OR LED IN: what can be caused, and the older habit of leading a listener in.
branches.cn: 被引起，或被领入：可被引起的东西，以及把听者领进来的旧习惯。

branches.en: THE MACHINE'S OWN TILT: generalization needs an assumption chosen in advance.
branches.cn: 机器自身的偏向：泛化需要一个事先选定的假设。

intro.en: Inductive is a Latin participle stem plus an adjective ending, so it is built from three recognisable pieces.
intro.cn: inductive 是拉丁分词词干加形容词词尾，因此由三块可辨认的成分构成。

latinIntro.en: The same leading verb underlies the noun and the verb, while the ending marks a property rather than an action.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个「引领」动词支撑着名词与动词，而词尾标记的是性质而非动作。

definition_zh: 另一方面；不过话说回来（用于对比前文，或补充第二项考虑）
definition_en: used to introduce a contrasting point, or a second consideration after the first
core_image: 同一枚硬币翻到背面，图案与正面完全不同
scene: 买房的人算完价格又算通勤，价格低的那套每天要多花两个小时。 The flat is cheap; on the other hand, the commute would wear anyone down.
sceneCN: 这里取「另一方面」（第 1 个义项：引出与前文相对的第二项考虑）；句意为这套房便宜，另一方面通勤会让人吃不消。

pos.zh: 副词短语：另一方面；不过话说回来

forms.label: 配对形式
forms.form: on the one hand ... on the other hand

senses.title: The second consideration
senses.titleCN: 对比义：引出第二项考虑
senses.definition: used to add a point that weighs against or differs from the one just made
senses.definitionCN: 用来补上一个与刚才那点相抗衡或不同的看法
senses.example: The job pays well; on the other hand, it leaves no time for family.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作报酬不错；另一方面，它让人没时间陪家人。
senses.why: Two hands hold two sides of one object, so the image naturally sets a second view beside the first.
senses.whyCN: 两只手各持一物的一面，这个意象自然把第二种看法摆在第一种旁边。

senses.title: The paired frame
senses.definition: it answers a first phrase that has already opened one side of the comparison
senses.definitionCN: 用来回应前文已经打开比较一侧的那个短语
senses.example: On the one hand the offer is generous; on the other hand the terms are strict.
senses.exampleCN: 一方面这份报价很慷慨；另一方面条款却很严。
senses.why: A hand needs its partner, and the pair keeps the reader oriented in a two-sided account.
senses.whyCN: 一只手需要另一只手配，这对短语让读者在双面叙述中不迷失方向。

senses.title: Not the contrast phrase
senses.titleCN: 辨义：不同于强对比说法
senses.definition: it adds a second side, while the phrase with contrast sets two things sharply against each other
senses.definitionCN: 它补上第二面，而表强对比的短语把两物尖锐对立起来
senses.example: The first plan is cheaper; on the other hand, the second is faster.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个方案更便宜；另一方面，第二个更快。
senses.why: Adding a side is gentler than staging a clash, which is why business prose prefers this frame.
senses.whyCN: 补上一面比制造冲突温和，因此商务文字偏爱这个框架。

senses.title: Not the opposite
senses.definition: it introduces a different consideration, not a denial of what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 它引出另一项考虑，而不是否认刚才所说的话
senses.example: The weather was bad; on the other hand, the hotel was excellent.
senses.exampleCN: 天气很糟；另一方面，旅馆却很好。
senses.why: A contrary phrase says the previous claim is false, while this one merely adds weight elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 表相反的说法断言前一主张为假，而这个短语只是把分量加到别处。

senses.title: Concession after admission
senses.definition: after an admitted weakness it brings in a compensating strength, or the reverse
senses.definitionCN: 在承认某一弱点之后，引入可补偿的长处，或反之
senses.example: The evidence is thin. On the other hand, no one has offered a better account.
senses.exampleCN: 证据确实单薄。不过另一方面，也没有人提出更好的解释。
senses.why: Balancing is the everyday work of the phrase, and it often repairs a concession.
senses.whyCN: 权衡是这个短语的日常功能，它常把一次让步修补回来。

senses.title: Two sides of an argument
senses.definition: in discussion it marks the second camp, keeping both positions visible without judging them
senses.definitionCN: 在讨论中标出第二方，让两种立场都可见而不作评判
senses.example: Supporters stress growth; on the other hand, critics point to the debt.
senses.exampleCN: 支持者强调增长；另一方面，批评者指向债务。
senses.why: A neutral connector lets a writer report a debate without taking a side.
senses.whyCN: 中性衔接语让作者报道争论而不选边。

senses.title: The spoken turn-back
senses.definition: in conversation it softens a reversal, as if the speaker has just thought of the other side
senses.definitionCN: 在对话中软化一次转折，仿佛说话人刚想到另一面
senses.example: It is a long journey. On the other hand, the scenery is worth it.
senses.exampleCN: 路程是远。不过话说回来，风景值得。
senses.why: A spoken reversal needs a cushion, and the phrase supplies one.
senses.whyCN: 口语中的转折需要缓冲，这个短语正好提供。

senses.title: Not a second hand
senses.definition: the phrase contrasts arguments and never describes a second physical hand
senses.definitionCN: 这个短语对比的是论点，从不描述另一只实际的手
senses.example: On the other hand introduces a contrast, not a second physical hand.
senses.exampleCN: 另一方面引出的是对比，不是另一只实实在在的手。
senses.why: The body-part image faded into a metaphor of two sides long ago.
senses.whyCN: 身体部位的意象早已淡化为两面的比喻。

intro.en: Hand is Old English, from a reconstructed Germanic form, with no Latin etymon; other is also native. The phrase grew from the image of holding two sides of one thing.
intro.cn: hand 属古英语，源自日耳曼语系的重构形式，无拉丁语词源；other 亦为本族词。短语由「一手各持一面」的意象发展而来。

items.en: Hand named the body part and also possession, control and a side of a bargain.
items.cn: 这个词指身体部位，也指持有、掌控与交易的一方。

items.en: The earlier Germanic noun is reconstructed rather than recorded, so its exact shape is not attested.
items.cn: 更早的日耳曼语名词是重构形式而非有记录的，确切形态无实证。

items.en: The word for the second of two is native and supplies the contrasting element.
items.cn: 表两者中另一个的词是本族词，提供对比成分。

items.en: One hand and the other hand picture two sides of one matter held at once.
items.cn: 一只手与另一只手，描绘同一件事的两面被同时持握。

items.en: The fixed adverbial phrase belongs to modern argument and correspondence; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 这个固定副词短语属于近代论证与书信，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the hand image or the contrast job but differs in strength; the second group are connectors of contrast and reversal.
note.cn: 第一组共用手的意象或对比功能，但力度不同；第二组是表对比与转折的衔接语。

entries.definition: It opens the first side and expects this phrase to follow.
entries.definitionCN: 它打开第一面，并期待本短语随后出现。

entries.definition: It asserts that the previous statement is wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 它断言前一陈述是错的。

entries.definition: It often refers to a physical side or an opposing party.
entries.definitionCN: 常指实际一侧或对立一方。

entries.definition: It introduces a compensating advantage in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中引出可补偿的好处。

entries.definition: A single adverb for a contrast, usable in mid-sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 单词副词表转折，可用于句中。

entries.definition: It sets two things against each other explicitly.
entries.definitionCN: 明确把两物对立起来。

entries.definition: It marks the reversed version of the same relation.
entries.definitionCN: 标出同一关系的反向表述。

entries.definition: It means on second thought, in conversation.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中表示转念一想。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the native origin, the paired-hand image and the real difference from contrary and contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用本族词来源、双手配对的意象，以及与相反、强对比的真实差别。

normal.en: Two hands hold two sides of one thing, so the phrase adds a side rather than denies one.
normal.cn: 两只手各持一面，因此短语是补上一面，而非否认一面。

normal.en: It expects its partner to have opened the other side earlier.
normal.cn: 它期待搭档已在前文打开另一面。

normal.en: A contrary word calls the first claim false; this one only adds weight elsewhere.
normal.cn: 表相反的词说前一主张为假；这个只把分量加到别处。

normal.en: In conversation it cushions a reversal.
normal.cn: 在对话中它为转折提供缓冲。

normal.en: The body-part image is long dead; no actual hand is meant.
normal.cn: 身体部位的意象早已消亡，并不指实际的手。

abstract.en: Like a coin turned over: the same object, a different face.
abstract.cn: 像硬币翻面：同一枚，另一张脸。

abstract.en: Like a balance held in two hands, one pan rising as the other falls.
abstract.cn: 像两手托着天平，一盘升另一盘落。

abstract.en: Like a debate table with speakers seated on opposite sides.
abstract.cn: 像辩论桌，发言者分坐两侧。

examples.en: The train is faster; on the other hand, the bus is cheaper.
examples.cn: 火车更快；另一方面，公共汽车更便宜。

examples.en: On the other hand, the second candidate has more experience.
examples.cn: 另一方面，第二位候选人经验更丰富。

examples.en: The work is hard. On the other hand, it pays well.
examples.cn: 这活很辛苦。不过话说回来，报酬不错。

root: 核心名词意为手，来自古英语 hand，源自日耳曼语系的 handuz（重构形式），无拉丁语同源；该短语由一手与另一手的对称意象发展而来，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses separate the second consideration, the paired frame, the contrast with sharper connectors, the contrast with denial, concession after admission, two camps in a debate, the spoken reversal and the exclusion of a literal hand.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项区分：第二项考虑、配对框架、与更强对比语的差别、与否认的差别、承认后的让步、辩论中的两方、口语转折，以及排除字面上的手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same coin turned over, the reverse face showing a different pattern.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一枚硬币翻过来，背面显出不同的图案。

branches.en: THE SECOND SIDE: another consideration is added beside the first.
branches.cn: 第二面：在第一项旁边补上另一项考虑。

branches.en: THE PAIR: the frame answers an opening phrase that has already taken one side.
branches.cn: 配对：这个框架回应已经取了一面的前文短语。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: adding a side is not denying the previous claim.
branches.cn: 对照：补一面不等于否认前一主张。

branches.en: THE BALANCE: a weakness is repaired by a strength, in writing or in speech.
branches.cn: 权衡：无论书面还是口语，弱点由长处补回。

branches.en: THE TWO CAMPS AND THE LIMIT: a debate shows both sides, and no body part is meant.
branches.cn: 两方与边界：辩论呈现双方，且不指身体部位。

intro.en: The phrase is wholly native in its nouns, so its affix section records Germanic forms rather than Latin roots.
intro.cn: 这个短语的两个名词都是本族词，因此词缀部分记录日耳曼语形式而非拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin etymon for either noun: hand and other are native Germanic words, and the earlier forms are reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 两个名词都没有拉丁语词源：它们都是日耳曼语本族词，更早的形式为重构形式。

items.example: English keeps the limb and the possession senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语兼留肢体与持有两义。

items.example: The word supplies the contrasting half.
items.exampleCN: 这个词提供对比的另一半。

items.example: The verb pictures taking something in hand.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描绘把东西拿在手里。

items.example: The adjective keeps the idea of being within reach.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词保留伸手可及的意思。

items.meaning: as much as one hand holds
items.example: The suffix measures a quantity by the hand.
items.exampleCN: 后缀以手为单位量取分量。

items.example: The compound contrasts with machine production.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词与机器生产相对。

items.example: The adverb marks ease of handling.
The frame is standard in balanced argument.
items.exampleCN: 这个框架在平衡论证中是标准用法。

definition_zh: 灭绝的；绝种的；（火山）熄灭的；（语言、习俗）已消亡的
definition_en: no longer existing as a living species, or no longer active, spoken or in use
core_image: 一座火山口安静地积着雨水，山坡长满树，看不出这里曾经喷发
scene: 这里指「灭绝的」。 The volcano has been extinct for ten thousand years, its crater now a lake.
sceneCN: 这里 extinct 指「火山已停止活动、不会再喷发」（第 2 个义项：火山进入休眠终止状态）；句意为这座火山已熄灭一万年，火山口如今成了湖。图中可辨识物件：积水火山口、覆满植被的山坡、岩层剖面、远处无烟的天际。

pos.zh: 灭绝的；绝种的；（火山）熄灭的；（语言、习俗）已消亡的

forms.label: 现在分词作定语（正在消失的）

senses.title: No longer living as a species
senses.definition: no longer existing as a living species anywhere on earth
senses.definitionCN: 地球上不再有任何活着的个体
senses.example: The passenger pigeon is extinct, though its skins fill museum drawers.
senses.exampleCN: 旅鸽已经灭绝，尽管它的皮毛还塞满博物馆的抽屉。
senses.why: extinct is the past participle of a verb meaning to put out, so a species described this way is one whose flame has gone out.
senses.whyCN: extinct 是「弄灭」这个动词的过去分词，因此被这样描述的物种，就是火已熄灭的那一个。

senses.title: A volcano that will not erupt again
senses.titleCN: 死火山：不再活动的火山
senses.definition: no longer capable of erupting, said of a volcano whose magma supply is cut off
senses.definitionCN: 指火山不再喷发，岩浆供给已切断
senses.example: The volcano has been extinct for ten thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座火山已熄灭一万年。
senses.why: the image of a quenched fire fits a volcano exactly: the fire is out and the mountain is only a shape.
senses.whyCN: 「火被弄灭」的意象正合火山：火已熄，山只剩下一个形状。

senses.title: A language with no native speakers
senses.definition: no longer spoken as a mother tongue by any community
senses.definitionCN: 不再有任何社群把它当作母语使用
senses.example: The language went extinct when its last fluent speaker died in 1987.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一位流利使用者于 1987 年离世后，这门语言就消亡了。
senses.why: a language is kept alive by its speakers, so when the last one goes the word for a quenched flame applies.
senses.whyCN: 语言靠使用者维持生命，最后一人离去，便可以用「火已熄灭」来形容。

senses.title: A family line that has died out
senses.definition: having no living descendants, said of a family or lineage
senses.definitionCN: 指家族或世系已无在世后代
senses.example: The male line became extinct in the fifteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 这一支男系在 15 世纪断绝。
senses.why: Latin used the verb of a family whose last member died, and English kept that figurative use intact.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语就用这个动词指家族最后一人死去，英语完整保留了这一比喻用法。

senses.title: A fire or light put out
senses.definition: no longer burning or shining, used in literary and older prose
senses.definitionCN: 不再燃烧或发光，用于文学与较早的书面语
senses.example: By midnight every lamp in the hall was extinct.
senses.exampleCN: 到午夜，大厅里每一盏灯都熄了。
senses.why: this is the literal sense from which all the others were cut, and it survives in elevated writing.
senses.whyCN: 这是所有其他义项所由切出的字面义，仍存活于较庄重的文字中。

senses.title: A custom no longer practised
senses.definition: no longer existing in practice, said of a custom, craft or usage
senses.definitionCN: 指习俗、手艺或用法已不再实际存在
senses.example: The craft of hand-setting type is nearly extinct.
senses.exampleCN: 手工排字这门手艺已近乎消亡。
senses.why: a practice lives only while people perform it, so it goes out like a flame when the last practitioners stop.
senses.whyCN: 一种做法只在人们实践时存在，最后一批人停手，它便像火一样熄灭。

senses.title: A right no longer in force
senses.definition: no longer legally valid, said of a right, claim or obligation
senses.definitionCN: 指权利、主张或义务在法律上已失效
senses.example: The easement is extinct once the dominant estate is sold.
senses.exampleCN: 需役地被出售后，这项地役权即归消灭。
senses.why: law borrows the word for anything that has ceased to exist in law, keeping the sense of being put out.
senses.whyCN: 法律借这个词指在法律上不复存在之物，保留「被弄灭」的意思。

senses.title: Gone from the wild, kept in captivity
senses.titleCN: 野外灭绝：仅存于人工饲养
senses.definition: no longer surviving in the wild but still kept in zoos or collections
senses.definitionCN: 野外已无存活个体，但动物园或收藏机构仍有饲养
senses.example: The antelope is extinct in the wild but breeds in captivity.
senses.exampleCN: 这种羚羊在野外已灭绝，但在人工饲养下仍能繁殖。
senses.why: conservation needed a label in between living and lost, and the fixed phrase extinct in the wild supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 保护工作需要「既未全活也未全失」的状态标签，固定说法「野外灭绝」正好补上这个位置。

intro.en: Extinct is the past participle of Latin exstinguere 'to put out, quench', used in English as an adjective from the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: extinct 是拉丁 exstinguere「熄灭、扑灭」的过去分词，自 16 世纪起在英语中作形容词使用。年代均为约数。

items.en: Exstinguere combined ex- 'out' with stinguere 'to prick, quench'; its past participle exstinctus meant 'put out, quenched'.
items.cn: exstinguere 把 ex-「向外」与 stinguere「刺、熄灭」结合，其过去分词 exstinctus 意为「已熄灭的」。

items.en: English adopted exstinctus as extinct in the sixteenth century, first of fires, lights and family lines.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪把 exstinctus 吸收为 extinct，最初用于火、光与家族世系。

items.en: The geological use for a volcano that will not erupt again is recorded from the seventeenth century, as naturalists classified mountains as active or quiet.
items.cn: 指不会再喷发的火山这一地质用法在 17 世纪有记录，当时博物学家把山分为活动与安静两类。

items.en: The sense of a species having died out spread in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries with the fossil record and with Cuvier's work on vanished animals.
items.cn: 物种已灭绝的意思在 18 至 19 世纪随化石记录与居维叶对消失动物的研究而扩散。

items.en: The fixed phrase extinct in the wild was adopted in the twentieth century to mark species surviving only in captivity.
items.cn: 固定说法「野外灭绝」于 20 世纪被采用，用来标记仅存于人工饲养的物种。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): early citations for the volcano and species senses are not precisely fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of stinguere remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：火山义与物种义的最早书证没有精确定论；stinguere 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words of the same stinguere stock that look almost identical; group two holds adjectives for things no longer present.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 stinguere 词干、外形几乎相同的词；第二组表示「已不存在」的形容词。

entries.definition: The event or process of dying out; extinct describes the resulting state.
entries.definitionCN: 指灭绝的事件或过程；extinct 描述由此形成的状态。

entries.definition: To put out a fire or wipe out something; extinct is what remains after the act.
entries.definitionCN: 扑灭火或抹去某物；extinct 是行为之后留下的状态。

entries.definition: Dis- 'apart' plus stinguere: marked off, hence clear and separate. It has no trace of dying out.
entries.definitionCN: dis-「分开」加 stinguere：被划分开，因此指清楚、分明。毫无「消亡」之意。

entries.definition: In- 'in' plus stinguere, 'pricked from within': the word names an inborn impulse, not an ending.
entries.definitionCN: in-「在内」加 stinguere，「被内在刺动」：指天生冲动，不指终结。

entries.definition: Gone from view or existence, often used loosely; a vanished custom may return, an extinct species cannot.
entries.definitionCN: 指从视野或存在中消失，用法较宽；消失的习俗可能回来，灭绝的物种不能。

entries.definition: Said of organizations, laws or machines that have stopped working; it is not used of species.
entries.definitionCN: 用于停止运作的机构、法律或机器；不用于物种。

entries.definition: Inactive but able to revive, as a dormant volcano or seed; extinct means there is no revival.
entries.definitionCN: 指暂不活动但仍可能复活，如休眠火山或种子；extinct 指再无复活可能。

entries.definition: No longer used because something better replaced it, said of words or tools; it implies replacement, not death.
entries.definitionCN: 因被更好的东西取代而不再使用，用于词或工具；含「被取代」而非「死亡」之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + stinguere 'quench': the flame has been put out.
normal.cn: ex-「向外」+ stinguere「熄灭」：火已被弄灭。

normal.en: The family runs extinct, extinction, extinguish, extinguisher, extinctive.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 extinct、extinction、extinguish、extinguisher、extinctive。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: extinct species, extinct volcano, extinct language, extinct in the wild.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：已灭绝物种、死火山、消亡语言、野外灭绝。

normal.en: It is an absolute adjective, so grammar prefers go extinct to more extinct.
normal.cn: 它是绝对形容词，因此语法上更常说 go extinct 而不是 more extinct。

normal.en: The same root appears in distinct and instinct with different prefixes.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 distinct 与 instinct 中，前缀不同。

abstract.en: Picture a crater full of rainwater where fire used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象一个积满雨水的火山口，那里曾经是火。

abstract.en: Picture a museum drawer of skins that are the last of their kind.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆抽屉里的皮毛，是它们那类最后的遗存。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp with no oil left, however polished the brass.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏没有油可点的灯，黄铜再亮也无用。

examples.en: The species was declared extinct after three years without a sighting.
examples.cn: 连续三年没有观测记录后，该物种被宣布灭绝。

examples.en: An extinct volcano can still host hot springs.
examples.cn: 死火山仍可能有温泉。

examples.en: The dialect is not extinct yet, but no children speak it.
examples.cn: 这种方言尚未消亡，但已没有孩子会说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）+ tinct（熄灭）」——火灭得干干净净 → 灭绝的、熄灭的

root: 拉丁 exstinctus（exstinguere「熄灭」的过去分词）= ex-「向外」+ stinguere「刺、熄灭」；英语 extinct。与 extinction、extinguish 同族，与 distinct、instinct 同根不同前缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one state: a fire is out, and that outness is then read as a species, a volcano, a language, a lineage, a lamp, a craft, a legal right and a species that survives only in cages.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个状态展开：火已灭，这个「灭」再被读成物种、火山、语言、世系、灯、手艺、法律权利，以及只活在笼中的物种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crater holding rainwater where fire once was.
core.cn: 核心意象：火山口积着雨水，那里曾经是火。

branches.en: LIVING LINE ENDED: species and family lines both reach a last member.
branches.cn: 活的世系终止：物种与家族都走到最后一位成员。

branches.en: MOUNTAIN QUIET: a quenched fire explains an unerupting volcano.
branches.cn: 山的安静：熄灭的火解释了不再喷发的火山。

branches.en: CARRIERS SILENT: a language and a craft last only while someone performs them.
branches.cn: 承载者沉默：语言与手艺只在有人实践时存在。

branches.en: LITERAL LAMP: the oldest sense, kept for elevated prose.
branches.cn: 字面的灯：最古老的义项，保留在庄重文字里。

branches.en: LEGAL AND CAPTIVE ENDS: a right can be extinguished, and a species can be extinct in the wild only.
branches.cn: 法律与圈养两端：权利可被消灭，物种也可只在野外灭绝。

intro.en: Extinct is a Latin participle used as an adjective; ex- supplies 'out' and stinguere supplies the quenching, both visible across its word family.
intro.cn: extinct 是作形容词用的拉丁分词；ex- 提供「向外」，stinguere 提供「熄灭」，两者在整个词族中都看得见。

latinIntro.en: Exstinguere yields extinct, extinction and extinguish; the same root with other prefixes yields distinct, instinct and distinguish.
latinIntro.cn: exstinguere 衍生 extinct、extinction 与 extinguish；同一词根换前缀则得 distinct、instinct 与 distinguish。

items.example: The prefix marks the driving out of the flame.
The root carries the quenching image.

items.meaning: the state or event of dying out
items.example: Extinction followed the draining of the marsh.
items.exampleCN: 沼泽排干之后出现了灭绝。
他们扑灭了最后的余烬。

items.example: An extinctive condition ended the licence.
items.exampleCN: 一条消灭条件终止了许可。

items.example: Two distinct calls mark the two species.
items.exampleCN: 两种不同的鸣声标记着两个物种。

definition_zh: 比较起来；与……相比（用于衡量两者的相似或差距）
definition_en: when judged against something else; used to weigh two or more things on the same scale
core_image: 两把新旧尺子并排贴在桌面，刻度线一一对齐
scene: 设计师把新旧两版尺子并排贴在桌上，逐一对照刻度。 In comparison, the new ruler is slightly longer.
sceneCN: 这里取「比较起来」（第 1 个义项：句首比较标记）；句意为比较起来，新尺子稍长一些。

pos.zh: 状语短语：比较起来
介词短语：与……相比

senses.title: The sentence-opening comparison marker
senses.definition: placed at the beginning of a clause to introduce a judgement made by weighing two things
senses.definitionCN: 置于从句开头，引出把两物放在同一把尺上得出的判断
senses.example: In comparison, the second route is shorter.
senses.exampleCN: 比较起来，第二条路线更短。
senses.why: Front position tells the reader that the following statement is measured against the one just made.
senses.whyCN: 置于句首告诉读者，接下来的说法是拿前一句作尺子量出来的。

senses.title: The formal with variant
senses.titleCN: 后接介词加名词：与……相比
senses.definition: used with with and a noun to name the standard of comparison
senses.definitionCN: 用介词加名词，点出比较的基准
senses.example: In comparison with last year, sales fell.
senses.exampleCN: 与去年相比，销售额下降了。
senses.why: With names the benchmark, turning the adverbial phrase into a prepositional frame at the head of the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 该介词点出基准，于是状语短语变成句首的介词框架。

senses.title: The North American to variant
senses.titleCN: 后接另一个介词加名词：与……相比（北美常用）
senses.definition: used with to instead of with, especially in North American writing, with the same meaning
senses.definitionCN: 用另一个介词代替，多见于北美书面语，意义相同
senses.example: In comparison to the older model, this one runs cooler.
senses.exampleCN: 与旧型号相比，这一款运行更凉。
senses.why: The two prepositions are variants rather than contrasts; to has become the more frequent partner in North America.
senses.whyCN: 两个介词是变体而非对立；在北美，后者已成为更常见的搭档。

senses.title: The mid-sentence aside
senses.definition: inserted inside a clause, usually between commas, to add a measured aside
senses.definitionCN: 插在从句内部，通常用逗号夹住，补一句比较性的旁白
senses.example: The new model, in comparison, uses far less power.
senses.exampleCN: 相比之下，新型号耗电少得多。
senses.why: Inside commas the phrase behaves like a parenthetical comment rather than a full connector.
senses.whyCN: 被逗号夹住时，这个短语更像插入的旁注，而不是完整的连接语。

senses.title: The idiom of falling short
senses.definition: in the fixed pattern pale in comparison, used to say that one thing looks weak beside another
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法「相形见绌」中，表示一物放在另一物旁边显得逊色
senses.example: The old hall pales in comparison.
senses.exampleCN: 与之一比，旧礼堂相形见绌。
senses.why: The verb pale supplies the image of colour draining away, and the phrase supplies the standard that causes it.
senses.whyCN: 动词「失色」提供颜色褪去的画面，这个短语则提供使之失色的基准。

senses.title: Weighing similarity, not opposition
senses.definition: used when two things are placed on one scale to show how close or far apart they are
senses.definitionCN: 把两物放在同一把尺上，显示它们相差多少
senses.example: In comparison, the two samples were nearly identical.
senses.exampleCN: 比较起来，两个样本几乎完全相同。
senses.why: This is the boundary against in contrast: here the point may be closeness, there the point is always divergence.
senses.whyCN: 这正是它与对比短语的分界：这里可以指接近，那里永远指分歧。

senses.title: Reporting a neighbouring figure
senses.titleCN: 图表叙述：与相邻数字比较
senses.definition: used in data writing to set a figure against the one before or beside it
senses.definitionCN: 在数据写作中，把某个数字与前一数字或相邻数字并置
senses.example: In comparison, imports rose while exports held steady.
senses.exampleCN: 相比之下，进口上升，出口持平。
senses.why: Charts need a short signal that two series are read together, and the phrase provides it without repeating the numbers.
senses.whyCN: 图表需要一个短信号说明两组数据要合看，这个短语不必重复数字就做到了。

senses.title: The evaluative aside
senses.definition: used to introduce a judgement about quality after a standard has been set
senses.definitionCN: 在基准已经摆出之后，引出关于优劣的判断
senses.example: In comparison, the first draft looks careless.
senses.exampleCN: 对比之下，初稿显得草率。
senses.why: Once a benchmark is on the table, the phrase can carry a verdict rather than a measurement.
senses.whyCN: 基准一旦摆上桌面，这个短语就能承载评判而不只是测量。

intro.en: Comparison goes back to Latin comparatio, from comparare, to pair together, itself com-, together, plus par, equal. The Latin line is clear; the English phrase is modern.
intro.cn: comparison 可追溯到拉丁语 comparatio，来自 comparare「配对」，由 com-「共同」与 par「相等」构成。拉丁语线索清楚，英语短语属近代。

items.en: Par means equal and is also the root of peer and parity.
items.cn: par 意为「相等」，也是 peer 与 parity 的词根。

items.en: Comparare meant to bring things together as equals, hence to compare.
items.cn: comparare 意为把事物作为对等者放到一起，即「比较」。

items.en: The noun named a setting side by side, and Old French comparaison carried it to English.
items.cn: 这个名词指并置对照，古法语 comparaison 把它带入英语。

items.en: English comparison appears in the Middle English period; the exact date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 comparison 出现于中古英语时期，确切年代为约数。

items.en: The adverbial phrase and its two prepositional variants settle in modern written English.
items.cn: 状语短语及其两个介词变体在近代书面英语中定型。

note.en: The first group shares the comparison slot but stresses difference or another relation; the second group holds adverbs and paraphrases of measured judgement.
note.cn: 第一组占同样的比较位置，却强调差异或别的关系；第二组是衡量判断的副词与同义改写。

entries.definition: It always stresses divergence, while this phrase may also report closeness.
entries.definitionCN: 它始终强调分歧，而本短语也可以报告接近。

entries.definition: It usually opens a sentence on its own and rarely takes with or to.
entries.definitionCN: 它通常独立开启一句，很少接介词。

entries.definition: It is the common verbal frame for the same benchmark.
entries.definitionCN: 它是同一基准最常用的分词框架。

entries.definition: It relates two things without necessarily measuring them.
entries.definitionCN: 它把两物联系起来，未必要测量。

entries.definition: It means relatively, judged against others, and often modifies an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 意为相对地，常修饰形容词。

entries.definition: It marks a judgement that depends on the standard chosen.
entries.definitionCN: 标出取决于所选基准的判断。

entries.definition: It puts two things side by side in space or argument.
entries.definitionCN: 在空间或论证中把两物并排。

entries.definition: It names the standard in a verbal phrase rather than a fixed idiom.
entries.definitionCN: 用动词短语点明基准，而非固定习语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pair, the real prepositions and the real idiom.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实拉丁语对、真实介词与真实习语。

normal.en: Par is equal, so to compare is to bring equals together.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根意为「相等」，比较就是把对等者放到一起。

normal.en: With names the benchmark; to is its North American twin.
normal.cn: 一个介词点出基准，另一个是它的北美双胞胎。

normal.en: At the front it opens the judgement; in commas it is an aside.
normal.cn: 放句首开启判断，放逗号里则是旁注。

normal.en: Pale in comparison is the idiom for falling short.
normal.cn: 「相形见绌」是表示逊色的固定说法。

normal.en: Its neighbour in contrast always stresses difference, so the two are not interchangeable.
normal.cn: 邻近的对比短语始终强调差异，两者不能互换。

abstract.en: Like two rulers laid edge to edge so the marks line up.
abstract.cn: 像两把尺子边缘对齐，刻度一一相合。

abstract.en: Like a pair of scales that can report either a gap or a match.
abstract.cn: 像一架天平，既能报出差值，也能报出相等。

abstract.en: Like a colour fading when a brighter sample is held beside it.
abstract.cn: 像更亮的样本一放旁边，颜色便显得褪了。

examples.en: In comparison with the coast, the inland region receives little rain.
examples.cn: 与沿海相比，内陆地区降雨很少。

examples.en: In comparison to the first edition, this one is heavily illustrated.
examples.cn: 与第一版相比，这一版插图很多。

examples.en: The earlier attempt pales in comparison.
examples.cn: 早先的尝试相形见绌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因 康帕瑞森」——两把尺子并排，一比就知长短：比较起来

root: comparison 来自拉丁语 comparatio，词根 comparare 由 com-「共同」与 par「相等」构成，经古法语进入英语；短语 in comparison 属近代书面用法，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split by position and complement: front and mid-clause, with and to plus a noun, the idiom of falling short, similarity, figure reporting, and evaluative judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按位置与搭配区分：句首与句中、两个介词加名词、「相形见绌」习语、相似性、数字报告、评价判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rulers laid edge to edge, marks aligned.
core.cn: 核心意象：两把尺子边缘对齐，刻度相合。

branches.en: THE MARKER: front position opens a judgement, mid position adds a parenthetical aside.
branches.cn: 标记：句首开启判断，句中补入旁注。

branches.en: THE BENCHMARK: two prepositions name the standard being used.
branches.cn: 基准：两个介词点出所采用的基准。

branches.en: THE IDIOM: one thing fades beside another.
branches.cn: 习语：一物在另一物旁失色。

branches.en: THE SCALE: the phrase may report closeness or set two series of figures together.
branches.cn: 刻度：可报告接近，也可把两组数字并置。

branches.en: THE VERDICT: once a standard is set, quality can be judged.
branches.cn: 评判：基准既定，便可评优劣。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin noun of pairing with an English preposition; the Latin core is clear.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语「配对」名词与英语介词结合；拉丁核心清楚。

latinIntro.en: The Latin etyma are comparare, to pair together, and par, equal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词源是 comparare「配对」与 par「相等」。

items.example: Par is the root of peer and parity as well.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也是另外两个英语词的来源。

items.example: The verb brings two equals into one frame.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把两个对等者放进同一框架。

items.example: The noun names the act that the phrase marks.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名这个短语所标记的动作。

items.example: French carried the noun into Middle English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个名词带入中古英语。

items.example: The noun is the base of the adjective comparable.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是相应形容词的基词。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Grammar uses the word for the comparative degree.
The phrase works as a connector in written English.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语在书面英语中作连接语。

definition_zh: v. 长时间闷闷地想；n. 一窝雏鸟
definition_en: to think about something sad or worrying for a long time; a family of young birds hatched together
core_image: 一个人坐在窗边，想同一封信想到天黑
scene: 他在窗边坐了一整个下午，为那封信闷闷地想。 He sat by the window all afternoon, brooding over the letter.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：brood 指长时间闷闷地思虑；句意是他坐在窗边整个下午为那封信发闷。

pos.zh: 闷闷地想；萦怀
一窝雏鸟

senses.title: To think moodily for a long time
senses.definition: to keep thinking about something sad or worrying in a quiet, unhappy way
senses.definitionCN: 安静而不快地反复想着悲伤或烦心的事
senses.example: He brooded over the letter for days.
senses.exampleCN: 他为那封信郁郁地想了好几天。
senses.why: Brood first meant to sit on eggs, and the mind sits the same way.
senses.whyCN: brood 原指伏在蛋上，心思也以同样方式「伏着」。

senses.title: A family of young birds
senses.definition: all the young birds hatched at one time by one mother
senses.definitionCN: 一只母鸟同一批孵出的幼鸟
senses.example: A brood of chicks followed the hen.
senses.exampleCN: 一窝小鸡跟着母鸡。
senses.why: The noun keeps the original picture of sitting on eggs.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了「伏在蛋上」的原始画面。

intro.en: Brood comes from an Old English word meaning to sit on eggs.
intro.cn: brood 源自意为「伏在蛋上」的古英语词。

items.en: Brod means the young of a bird.
items.cn: brod 指鸟的幼雏。

items.en: Bredan means to warm eggs by sitting.
items.cn: bredan 意为伏坐暖蛋。

items.en: Brood names both the sitting and the chicks.
items.cn: brood 兼指孵伏与雏鸟。

items.en: Brooding extends to unhappy thinking.
items.cn: brooding 扩展到不快的思虑。

items.en: Novelists describe characters who brood.
items.cn: 小说家描写闷闷沉思的人物。

items.en: Brood over is the usual phrase.
items.cn: brood over 是常见搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the broo- start; the near-meaning group covers both unhappy thinking and young birds.
note.cn: 形近组共享 broo- 开头；近义组兼收不快的思虑与幼鸟两义。

entries.definition: Wide from side to side.
entries.definitionCN: 宽大的。

entries.definition: Wanting to sit on eggs, or moody.
entries.definitionCN: 想孵蛋的；闷闷不乐的。

entries.definition: A heated box for young birds.
entries.definitionCN: 给幼鸟保温的箱子。

entries.definition: A brush with a long handle.
entries.definitionCN: 长柄扫帚。

entries.definition: To be unhappy and do nothing.
entries.definitionCN: 闷闷不乐地无所事事。

entries.definition: To keep thinking or talking about something.
entries.definitionCN: 反复想着或说着某事。

entries.definition: A group of eggs hatched together.
entries.definitionCN: 同窝孵出的蛋。

entries.definition: A group of young animals born at once.
entries.definitionCN: 同胎出生的幼崽。

normalIntro.en: To brood is to sit on a thought the way a hen sits on eggs.
normalIntro.cn: brood 就是像母鸡伏蛋那样伏在一个念头。

normal.en: A hen broods to hatch eggs.
normal.cn: 母鸡伏窝以孵蛋。

normal.en: A person broods to hatch worries.
normal.cn: 人伏着，孵出的是忧虑。

normal.en: Brooding is quiet and unhappy.
normal.cn: brooding 安静而不快。

normal.en: A brood is the chicks that result.
normal.cn: brood 是孵出来的那窝雏鸟。

normal.en: Brood over is the common verb phrase.
normal.cn: brood over 是常见动词短语。

abstract.en: Sitting still while the mind runs.
abstract.cn: 人坐着，脑子在跑。

abstract.en: A letter read twenty times.
abstract.cn: 读了二十遍的信。

abstract.en: Warmth given to the wrong thing.
abstract.cn: 温度给错了对象。

examples.en: She brooded over the interview for a week.
examples.cn: 她为那次面试郁结了一周。

examples.en: Do not brood in silence; say what is wrong.
examples.cn: 别闷着不说，把问题讲出来。

examples.en: A brood of ducklings crossed the path.
examples.cn: 一窝小鸭穿过小路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 母鸡伏蛋叫 brood，人伏着一个念头也叫 brood。

root: 古英语 brod（雏鸟）+ bredan（伏孵）

sensesIntro.en: Whether it is eggs or worries, brooding means staying on one thing long enough for it to change shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 无论孵的是蛋还是忧虑，brood 都是长时间伏在一件事上，直到它变形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a window, thinking the same letter until dark
core.cn: 核心意象：有人坐在窗边，把同一封信想到天黑

branches.en: A letter read twenty times.
branches.cn: 读了二十遍的信。

branches.en: A silence that answers nothing.
branches.cn: 什么也不回答的沉默。

branches.en: Chicks following a hen.
branches.cn: 跟着母鸡的雏鸟。

branches.en: Ducklings crossing a path.
branches.cn: 穿过小路的小鸭。

branches.en: Sitting on something until it opens.
branches.cn: 伏在上面，直到它打开。
