intro.cn: brood 是古老的英语词；下面列出它以及「孵化」词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin incubare is to lie on eggs, and pullus is a young bird.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 incubare 意为伏在蛋上，pullus 意为幼鸟。

items.meaning: to break out of an egg

latinEntries.exampleCN: pullus 产生 poultry 与 pullet。
nidus 产生 nest 与 nidify。

definition_zh: 测高仪；高度计；（飞机上的）高度表
definition_en: an instrument that measures altitude, especially the height of an aircraft above a level
core_image: 驾驶舱里一格格转动的指针，告诉你离地多高
scene: 飞行员爬升时盯着表盘。 The pilot checked the altimeter at ten thousand feet.
sceneCN: 这里的 altimeter 是「高度表」（第 1 个义项：测量高度的仪器）；句意是飞行员在一万英尺处查看高度表。

pos.zh: 测高仪；高度表

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，义为「高度；海拔」
由 alti- 加 -metry 构成，义为「测高术；高度测量」
同根成分，义为「测量器具；米」

senses.title: An aircraft height gauge
senses.definition: the cockpit instrument showing an aircraft's height above a reference level
senses.definitionCN: 座舱内显示飞机相对于基准面高度的仪表
senses.example: The altimeter read nine thousand feet.
senses.exampleCN: 高度表读数为九千英尺。
senses.why: Built from altus "high" plus metron "measure": the high-measurer.
senses.whyCN: 由 altus「高」加 metron「测量」构成：测量高的仪器。

senses.title: A barometric altimeter
senses.definition: an altimeter that converts air pressure into altitude
senses.definitionCN: 把气压换算成高度的测高仪
senses.example: Climbers carry a barometric altimeter uphill.
senses.exampleCN: 登山者背着气压高度计上山。
senses.why: Air thins with height, so pressure becomes a height signal.
senses.whyCN: 空气随高度变稀，气压因此成为高度信号。

senses.title: A radar or laser altimeter
senses.definition: a device measuring height by reflected radio waves or laser light
senses.definitionCN: 以反射无线电波或激光测高的装置
senses.example: The satellite's radar altimeter mapped the sea surface.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星的雷达测高仪测绘了海面。
senses.why: Timing a signal's round trip yields the distance below.
senses.whyCN: 信号往返的时间差给出下方距离。

senses.title: A surveying or scientific altimeter
senses.definition: a precision instrument for measuring elevations in field science
senses.definitionCN: 野外科学中测量海拔的精密仪器
senses.example: The team logged each site with an altimeter.
senses.exampleCN: 考察队用测高仪记录每个站点。
senses.why: Wherever height matters, a measuring instrument follows.
senses.whyCN: 凡高度要紧之处，测量仪器随之出现。

senses.title: A watch or wearable altimeter
senses.definition: an altimeter function built into watches or phones
senses.definitionCN: 集成于腕表或手机的高度计功能
senses.example: His watch has an altimeter for hiking.
senses.exampleCN: 他的手表带徒步用的高度计。
senses.why: Sensors shrink; the instrument becomes a feature.
senses.whyCN: 传感器缩小，仪器变成了功能。

senses.title: The system or discipline of height measurement
senses.definition: altimeter used broadly for a measuring system of altitude
senses.definitionCN: 泛指测量高度的系统或方法
senses.example: The probe's altimeter failed before landing.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器的测高系统在着陆前失灵。
senses.why: The word can name the whole apparatus, not just one dial.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可指整套装置，不只是一个表盘。

senses.title: Altitude data as output
senses.definition: the reading or data stream produced by an altimeter
senses.definitionCN: 测高仪产生的读数或数据流
senses.example: We lost altimeter data during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨中我们丢失了测高数据。
senses.why: Instrument names often extend to their outputs.
senses.whyCN: 仪器名常转指其输出。

senses.title: Figurative: a gauge of level or status
senses.definition: used figuratively for anything that indicates how high or advanced something is
senses.definitionCN: 喻指显示事物高度或先进程度的标志
senses.example: Stock prices are the market's altimeter.
senses.exampleCN: 股价是市场的晴雨高度表。
senses.why: A meter of height measures success or progress by metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 测高的仪表借喻度量成就或进展。

intro.en: Altimeter joins Latin altus "high" with the Greek-derived agent suffix -meter, "measurer".
intro.cn: altimeter 由拉丁语 altus「高」与希腊来源的 -meter「测量器」复合而成。

items.en: Root *al-, "to grow, nourish", behind altus.
items.cn: altus 背后的重构词根 *al-「生长；滋养」。

items.en: altus, "high, deep".
items.cn: 拉丁语 altus「高的；深的」。

items.en: metron "measure" and metes "measurer", via -meter.
items.cn: 希腊语 metron「量度」、metes「测量者」，经 -meter 传入。

items.en: altimètre / altimeter coined with barometers in the 18th-19th century.
items.cn: 十八九世纪随气压计的运用造出 altimètre/altimeter。

items.en: English altimeter in scientific use.
items.cn: 十九世纪英语 altimeter 用于科学语境。

items.en: Standard aviation and space term since early flight.
items.cn: 航空早期以来成为标准航空与航天术语。

note.en: Altimeter pairs with altitude and altimetry from the same altus root, and resembles other -meter instruments.
note.cn: altimeter 与同根的 altitude、altimetry 配对，且与其他 -meter 仪器词形相近。

entries.definition: height itself; the quantity, not the instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 高度本身；是量值而非仪器。

entries.definition: the science of measuring altitude.
entries.definitionCN: 测高的学科。

entries.definition: measures pressure, from which a barometric altimeter computes height.
entries.definitionCN: 测气压，气压高度表据其换算高度。

entries.definition: a -meter instrument for speed.
entries.definitionCN: 测速度的 -meter 仪表。

entries.definition: a -meter instrument for distance traveled.
entries.definitionCN: 测行驶里程的 -meter 仪表。

entries.definition: an older navigation instrument for angles, once used for altitude of stars.
entries.definitionCN: 较古老的导航测角仪器，曾用于测星高。

normalIntro.en: Take altimeter apart into its Latin and Greek halves.
normalIntro.cn: 把 altimeter 拆成拉丁与希腊两半。

normal.en: alti- (altus "high") + -meter (measure): the high-measurer.
normal.cn: alti-（altus「高」）+ -meter（测量）：测高的仪器。

normal.en: Family: altitude (height), altimetry (science), altimeter (tool).
normal.cn: 词族：altitude（高度）、altimetry（学科）、altimeter（工具）。

normal.en: Same -meter family: speedometer, odometer, barometer.
normal.cn: 同一 -meter 家族：speedometer、odometer、barometer。

normal.en: Types: barometric, radar, laser altimeters.
normal.cn: 类型：气压式、雷达式、激光式测高仪。

normal.en: Aviation habit: set the altimeter before takeoff.
normal.cn: 航空习惯：起飞前拨定高度表。

abstract.en: A needle climbing one tick per hundred feet.
abstract.cn: 指针每百英尺跳一格地攀升。

abstract.en: A watch face where hills become numbers.
abstract.cn: 表盘把群山变成数字。

abstract.en: A satellite bouncing a beam off the sea, timing the echo.
abstract.cn: 卫星向海面发射光束并给回声计时。

examples.en: Set the altimeter to field elevation.
examples.cn: 把高度表拨到机场标高。

examples.en: Her altimeter showed the summit at 6,900 meters.
examples.cn: 她的测高仪显示峰顶为 6900 米。

examples.en: The rocket's altimeter triggered the parachute.
examples.cn: 火箭的测高仪触发了降落伞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥提米特」——奥提（alti）摸高、米特（meter）量尺，摸高量尺就是高度表。

root: 拉丁语 altus「高的」（印欧词根 *al-「生长」）+ 希腊语 metron「量度」词形 -meter「测量器」；十八九世纪科学造词，二十世纪初随飞行成为航空标准词。

sensesIntro.en: Starting with the cockpit gauge, the instrument diversifies into barometric, radar, surveying, and wearable forms, then extends to the whole system, its data output, and a metaphor for level.
sensesIntro.cn: 从座舱仪表出发，仪器分化为气压式、雷达式、测绘式与可穿戴式，继而扩展到整套系统、数据输出与喻义标尺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial that turns height into numbers
core.cn: 核心意象：把高度变成数字的表盘

branches.en: The aircraft gauge at the core.
branches.cn: 核心的航空仪表。

branches.en: Barometric and radar/laser measuring principles.
branches.cn: 气压式与雷达/激光测高原理。

branches.en: Field science and wearable forms.
branches.cn: 野外科学与可穿戴形式。

branches.en: The whole measuring system.
branches.cn: 整套测量系统。

branches.en: Data output and the figurative gauge.
branches.cn: 数据输出与喻义标尺。

intro.en: Altimeter is a textbook alti- + -meter compound.
intro.cn: altimeter 是典型的 alti- 加 -meter 复合词。

latinIntro.en: The blend joins a Latin adjective base to a Greek measuring suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 该词把拉丁形容词词基与希腊测量后缀结合。

definition_zh: 坚毅；刚毅；忍痛的力量
definition_en: strength of mind that lets a person endure pain or hardship calmly
core_image: 一个人拄着拐杖走过长长的雪地，每一步都很慢，却一步也没有停
scene: 手术后的第三周，他每天沿走廊走二十步，从不让人扶。 The nurses admired his fortitude more than his recovery.
sceneCN: 这里 fortitude 指忍痛坚持的坚毅（第 1 个义项：在痛苦中保持的力量）；句意为护士们更佩服他的坚毅，而不是他的康复。

pos.zh: 坚毅；刚毅；坚忍

senses.title: Courage in pain
senses.definition: the strength to bear physical pain without giving way
senses.definitionCN: 承受身体痛苦而不垮掉的力量
senses.example: The nurses admired his fortitude more than his recovery.
senses.exampleCN: 护士们更佩服他的坚毅，而不是他的康复。
senses.why: This sense is about holding still under pain, not about fighting it.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项讲的是在痛苦下稳住，而不是与痛苦搏斗。

senses.title: Courage over years
senses.definition: the courage that lasts through long hardship rather than one crisis
senses.definitionCN: 穿过漫长困苦、而非一次危机的勇气
senses.example: She raised three children alone with unbroken fortitude.
senses.exampleCN: 她以不曾中断的坚毅独自养大三个孩子。
senses.why: A single hard hour needs nerve; a decade needs fortitude.
senses.whyCN: 艰难的一小时需要胆量；十年需要坚毅。

senses.title: Moral strength
senses.definition: the strength to keep to one's principles under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 在压力下守住原则的力量
senses.example: He refused the bribe with quiet fortitude.
senses.exampleCN: 他以沉静的刚毅拒绝了贿赂。
senses.why: Here the pain is not bodily but social: the cost is being disliked.
senses.whyCN: 这里的痛苦不是身体的，而是社会的：代价是被讨厌。

senses.title: Calm endurance
senses.definition: endurance without drama or complaint
senses.definitionCN: 不带戏剧性、也不抱怨的忍耐
senses.example: Her fortitude showed in what she never said.
senses.exampleCN: 她的坚忍体现在她从不说的那些话里。
senses.why: Endurance without complaint is the form strength takes when no one is watching.
senses.whyCN: 无人注视时，力量就表现为不抱怨的忍耐。

senses.title: Courage without display
senses.definition: strength that does not need to be seen to exist
senses.definitionCN: 无需被看见也存在的力量
senses.example: There was no speech, only fortitude.
senses.exampleCN: 没有演说，只有坚毅。
senses.why: The word prefers the quiet form: it describes a state, not a performance.
senses.whyCN: 这个词偏爱安静的形式：它描述状态，而非表演。

senses.title: Fortitude in adversity
senses.definition: the quality that keeps a person upright when circumstances turn bad
senses.definitionCN: 境况转坏时使人不倒的品质
senses.example: The town met the flood with stubborn fortitude.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇以倔强的坚毅面对洪水。
senses.why: Bad circumstances are the test that turns a capacity into a habit.
senses.whyCN: 恶劣境况是把能力变成习惯的检验。

senses.title: Fortitude of belief
senses.definition: the strength to hold a faith or conviction against opposition
senses.definitionCN: 在反对中守住信仰或信念的力量
senses.example: The small congregation kept its fortitude through years of pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小教会在多年压力中保持坚贞。
senses.why: Faith under pressure is held by the same muscle that holds a body upright.
senses.whyCN: 压力下的信念，由撑住身体的同一块肌肉撑着。

senses.title: Physical stamina
senses.definition: the bodily strength to keep going when tired
senses.definitionCN: 疲倦时仍能继续的身体力量
senses.example: Long marches test fortitude more than courage.
senses.exampleCN: 长途行军考验的更多是耐久，而不是勇气。
senses.why: The word can lean toward the body, though its usual home is the mind.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以偏向身体，尽管它通常住在心智里。

intro.en: Fortitude comes from a Latin word for strength, and it is strength thought of as a thing a person can hold.
intro.cn: fortitude 来自一个意为「力量」的拉丁词，它是被当作人所能持有之物来想的力量。

items.en: English took the noun in the 12c. through French, first as a general word for strength.
items.cn: 英语在十二世纪经法语借入这个名词，最初泛指力量。

items.en: Fortitudo meant 'strength, courage', and was one of the four classical virtues.
items.cn: fortitudo 意为「力量、勇气」，是四种古典美德之一。

items.en: Fortis means strong, brave, and gives fortify and fortress.
items.cn: fortis 意为强壮、勇敢，给出 fortify 与 fortress。

items.en: Medieval writers ranked fortitude as the virtue that holds the other virtues steady under attack.
items.cn: 中世纪作者把坚毅列为在攻击下稳住其它美德的美德。

items.en: Modern English narrowed it to quiet endurance, especially under pain or long hardship.
items.cn: 现代英语把它收窄为安静的忍耐，尤其在痛苦或长期困苦之下。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the strong root; the near-meaning group separates kinds of courage.
note.cn: 形近组共享「强」的词根；近义组区分不同种类的勇气。

entries.definition: to make stronger or better defended.
entries.definitionCN: 使更强或防御更好。

entries.definition: a defensive work or the act of strengthening.
entries.definitionCN: 防御工事或加固行为。

entries.definition: a heavily defended stronghold.
entries.definitionCN: 防守严密的堡垒。

entries.definition: showing quiet strength.
entries.definitionCN: 显出沉静力量的。

entries.definition: the ability to recover after difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 困难之后恢复的能力。

entries.definition: the power to keep going through fatigue.
entries.definitionCN: 在疲惫中继续的力量。

entries.definition: firm determination to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的坚定决心。

entries.definition: enduring pain or loss without complaint.
entries.definitionCN: 不抱怨地忍受痛苦或损失。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of slow steps across a long field of snow.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「在长长的雪地里一步一步慢慢走」的画面。

normal.en: Fortitude contains fort: a fort stands because it is built to take hits.
normal.cn: fortitude 里有 fort（堡垒）：堡垒能立住，是因为它造来承受打击。

normal.en: Link with fortify and fortress: one makes strong, one is strong.
normal.cn: 和 fortify、fortress 联系：一个加固，一个坚固。

normal.en: Think of a long walk rather than a single leap.
normal.cn: 想象一段长走，而不是一次跳跃。

normal.en: Say FOR-ti-tood; the heavy first syllable sounds like a planted foot.
normal.cn: 读成 FOR-ti-tood，沉甸甸的第一个音节像一只踏稳的脚。

normal.en: Shop it with patience: patience waits, fortitude holds.
normal.cn: 和 patience 一起记：patience 是等，fortitude 是撑住。

abstract.en: Courage meets a moment; fortitude meets a season.
abstract.cn: 勇气面对一个时刻，坚毅面对一个季节。

abstract.en: The strongest thing in a room is often the person saying nothing.
abstract.cn: 屋里最强的，常常是一言不发的那个人。

abstract.en: Strength held quietly does not need an audience to be real.
abstract.cn: 安静持有的力量，不需要观众才算真实。

examples.en: The nurses admired his fortitude more than his recovery.
examples.cn: 护士们更佩服他的坚毅，而不是他的康复。

examples.en: She raised three children alone with unbroken fortitude.
examples.cn: 她以不曾中断的坚毅独自养大三个孩子。

examples.en: He refused the bribe with quiet fortitude.
examples.cn: 他以沉静的刚毅拒绝了贿赂。

dict_mnemonic.text: fort（强）+ itude（名词）：一直强着的状态，就是「坚毅」。

root: 拉丁语 fortis（强、勇）→ fortitudo（力量、勇气）

sensesIntro.en: Fortitude is strength that holds rather than strikes; the senses differ in what is being held against, pain, time, pressure or fatigue.
sensesIntro.cn: fortitude 是「撑住」而非「出击」的力量；各义项的差别在于所抵抗的是痛苦、时间、压力，还是疲惫。

core.en: STRENGTH THAT HOLDS
core.cn: 撑住的力量

branches.en: Pain and its quiet bearing.
branches.cn: 痛苦与对其安静的承受。

branches.en: Long hardship and bad circumstances.
branches.cn: 长期困苦与恶劣境况。

branches.en: Principles and faith held under pressure.
branches.cn: 压力下守住的准则与信念。

branches.en: The unshown form: strength without performance.
branches.cn: 不展示的形态：没有表演的力量。

branches.en: The bodily version, stamina under fatigue.
branches.cn: 身体版本：疲惫中的耐久。

intro.en: The fort family is about making and being strong: fortify strengthens, fortress defends, fortitude endures.
intro.cn: fort 词族与「使强」和「强」有关：fortify 加固，fortress 防御，fortitude 忍耐。

latinIntro.en: Latin fortis is the adjective strong; fortitudo turns it into a quality a person can possess.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fortis 是形容词「强」；fortitudo 把它变成一种人可以拥有的品质。

items.meaning: a making strong, or the work built

items.example: The fortress held for a month.
The force of the wave broke the door.

definition_zh: 掺假；使不纯；败坏
definition_en: to make something impure or lower in quality by adding another substance
core_image: 一滴墨汁落进清水瓶，整瓶水再也回不到从前
scene: 作坊老板背对着门，把便宜油倒进贵油罐。 The merchant adulterated the olive oil with cheap rapeseed oil.
sceneCN: 这里 adulterate 是「掺假、使不纯」（第 1 个义项：往好东西里混入次等物）；句意为商人往橄榄油里掺了廉价的菜籽油。

pos.zh: 掺假；使不纯
掺假的；不纯的

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「掺假；掺杂」
由动词派生的施动名词，义为「掺杂物」
由动词加施动后缀构成，义为「掺假者」

senses.title: Make goods impure by mixing
senses.definition: to lower the quality of food, drink or goods by adding inferior substances
senses.definitionCN: 往食品、饮品或货物里加入次等物质以降低其品质
senses.example: The merchant adulterated the olive oil with cheap rapeseed oil.
senses.exampleCN: 商人往橄榄油里掺了廉价的菜籽油。
senses.why: Latin adulterare means 'to pollute', so the core image is corrupting something clean by pouring into it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adulterare 意为「污染」，核心意象就是往干净东西里灌入脏东西。

senses.title: Corrupt something abstract
senses.definition: to weaken or spoil the purity of an idea, language or tradition
senses.definitionCN: 使观念、语言或传统失去纯粹
senses.example: Critics said the sequel adulterated the spirit of the original film.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者说续集败坏了原作的精神。
senses.why: Mixing inferior matter extends by metaphor to ideas: the pure original gets watered down.
senses.whyCN: 掺次等物的动作经隐喻引申到观念：纯粹的原型被稀释。

senses.title: Adjective: impure, debased
senses.definition: describing something that has been made impure or of lower quality
senses.definitionCN: 形容已被掺假或品质下降的东西
senses.example: The customs office seized sacks of adulterate saffron.
senses.exampleCN: 海关查获了几袋掺假藏红花。
senses.why: The past participle hardens into an adjective: the result-state of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词凝固为形容词：动词造成的结果状态。

intro.en: Adulterate comes from Latin adulterare, 'to pollute, to corrupt', built on adulter, 'spurious, impure'.
intro.cn: adulterate 来自拉丁语 adulterare（污染、败坏），词根是 adulter（假的、不纯的）。

items.en: The root adulter described anything spurious, mixed, or not what it claimed to be.
items.cn: 词根 adulter 形容一切假冒的、掺混的、名不副实的东西。

items.en: Adulterare was the verb 'to corrupt'; ancient writers used it of wine, metals and morals alike.
items.cn: 动词 adulterare 意为「败坏」；古代作家用它形容酒、金属与道德。

items.en: English took the verb in the sixteenth century, first of corrupted goods.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入该动词，最初用于被做手脚的货物。

items.en: The adjective use for 'impure' settled beside the verb.
items.cn: 十七世纪，「不纯的」形容词用法在动词旁定型。

items.en: Modern use stresses commercial fraud, with the adjective common in customs and lab reports.
items.cn: 现代用法强调商业欺诈，形容词常见于海关与化验报告。

note.en: The first group gathers words of similar shape; the second gathers near synonyms of corrupting and diluting.
note.cn: 第一组收词形相近的词；第二组收表示「败坏、稀释」的近义词。

entries.definition: A grown person; only the opening letters are shared, the roots differ.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成年人」；只是开头字母相同，词根不同。

entries.definition: Marital unfaithfulness; from the same Latin adulter, corrupted fidelity rather than corrupted goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「通奸」；出自同一拉丁词根 adulter，是「被败坏的忠诚」而非「被败坏的货物」。

entries.definition: Excessive flattery; close in sound, unrelated in root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「吹捧」；发音接近，词源无关。

entries.definition: To make something dirty or unsafe, often by accident.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「污染」，多指无意间弄脏。

entries.definition: To lower the value or status of something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「贬低；使劣化」，偏重价值与地位。

entries.definition: To weaken by mixing with water or another thinning agent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「稀释；冲淡」，是掺假的一种具体方式。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pollute root and the oil-seller scene; the abstract hooks picture ink in water and a lowered grade.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「污染」词根与卖油人场景；抽象记忆点想象水中的墨与降级的货。

normal.en: Latin adulterare means 'to pollute'.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 adulterare 意为「污染」。

normal.en: Adulterant is the thing, adulterate the act.
normal.cn: adulterant 是物，adulterate 是行为。

normal.en: Adulteration is the crime's name in law.
normal.cn: adulteration 是法律上这种罪行的名字。

normal.en: Adulterated goods fail customs tests.
normal.cn: 掺假货物过不了海关检验。

normal.en: Adultery shares the root but means unfaithfulness.
normal.cn: adultery 同根但指不忠。

abstract.en: Picture ink spreading through a bottle of clear water.
abstract.cn: 想象墨汁在一瓶清水里晕开。

abstract.en: Picture gold coins shaved and refilled with copper.
abstract.cn: 想象金币被削去一角补上铜。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe ruined by one cheap shortcut.
abstract.cn: 想象一道菜谱被一个廉价的偷工步骤毁掉。

examples.en: The merchant adulterated the olive oil with cheap rapeseed oil.
examples.cn: 商人往橄榄油里掺了廉价的菜籽油。

examples.en: It is illegal to adulterate milk with water for sale.
examples.cn: 往牛奶里掺水出售是违法的。

examples.en: Years of careless edits adulterated the original text.
examples.cn: 多年草率的编辑败坏了原文。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额特喂」——额外地喂进去一些假料，好东西就被败坏了。

root: 拉丁语 adulter（假的、不纯的）→ adulterare（污染、败坏）→ 英语 adulterate；核心义是「把干净的弄脏、把纯的变假」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from mixing impurities into goods, to corrupting abstract things, to the adjective for the result.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从给货物掺假，到败坏抽象事物，再到形容结果的形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of ink falling into clear water
core.cn: 核心意象：落入清水的一滴墨

branches.en: Goods spoiled by what was slipped into them.
branches.cn: 被偷偷混入的次等物毁掉的货物。

branches.en: Ideas and traditions watered down.
branches.cn: 被稀释变味的观念与传统。

branches.en: The finished state: already impure.
branches.cn: 完成时的状态：已然不纯。

branches.en: Both senses trade purity for cheapness.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在用纯度换廉价。

branches.en: Customs and labs test for it daily.
branches.cn: 海关与化验室天天检验它。

intro.en: The word carries the Latin pollute root adulter- with the verb ending -ate, and the family gives adulteration and adulterant.
intro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「污染」词根 adulter- 与动词尾 -ate，同族词有 adulteration 与 adulterant。

latinIntro.en: Latin adulter and adulterare are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的拉丁语 adulter 与 adulterare 是直接祖先。

definition_zh: 有机整体的；有机体论的；整体论的
definition_en: treating a whole as an organized body whose parts are explained by the whole
core_image: 一张网被整体提起，每个结点都被同一股力牵动，无法单独取下
scene: 这里指「有机整体的」。 Organismic biology treats the whole animal as the unit that organizes its parts.
sceneCN: 这里 organismic 指「有机整体的」（第 1 个义项：把整体视为组织其部分的单位）；句意：有机体生物学把整只动物当作组织其各部分的单位。图中可辨识物件：完整的生物剖面、相互牵连的结点网、比例尺。

pos.zh: 有机整体的；有机体论的；整体论的（由 organism 加 -ic 构成，常用于 organismic biology、organismic theory）

collocations.zh: 有机体生物学；整体生物学

derivatives.zh: 生物个体的；个体层面的

senses.title: The Whole Organizes Parts
senses.titleCN: 有机整体的：整体组织部分
senses.definition: treating a whole as the unit that organizes its parts
senses.definitionCN: 把整体视为组织其各部分的单位
senses.example: Organismic biology treats the whole animal as the unit that organizes its parts.
senses.exampleCN: 有机体生物学把整只动物当作组织其各部分的单位。
senses.why: Organism plus -ic marks a way of seeing: the body is not a pile of parts but an order in which each part has its place. The suffix points to a quality or a school, not to a level.
senses.whyCN: organism 加 -ic 标出一种观看方式：身体不是零件的堆叠，而是一种每个部件都有其位置的秩序。这个后缀指向一种性质或学派，而不是一个层次。

senses.title: Against Mechanism
senses.definition: explaining life by whole-organizing principles rather than by machine-like parts
senses.definitionCN: 以整体组织原则、而非机械式部件来解释生命
senses.example: The organismic view rejects the idea that a body is only a machine.
senses.exampleCN: 有机整体观拒绝「身体只是一台机器」的看法。
senses.why: The word is useful mainly as an opponent of mechanistic. Where mechanism builds up from parts, organismic theory begins with the whole and asks what each part is doing for it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词主要作为 mechanistic 的对立面而有价值：机械论从部件往上搭，有机体论则从整体开始，追问每个部件在为难做事。

senses.title: A Biological School
senses.titleCN: 生物学流派的：研究整体的分支
senses.definition: belonging to the biological tradition that studies whole organisms
senses.definitionCN: 属于研究完整生物体的生物学传统
senses.example: Organismic biologists insisted that development cannot be split into separate causes.
senses.exampleCN: 有机体生物学家坚持认为，发育不能被拆成彼此分离的原因。
senses.why: Schools need names. Organismic biology was coined to contrast with approaches that begin at the molecular level, and it carries a claim about where explanation should start.
senses.whyCN: 学派需要名字。organicmic biology 被造出来，是为了与从分子层面出发的路径相对照，它带有「解释应当从哪里开始」的主张。

senses.title: Psychological Holism
senses.titleCN: 有机体心理学的：把心理视为整体
senses.definition: belonging to the psychological approach that treats the person as an integrated whole
senses.definitionCN: 属于把个人视为整合整体的心理学路径
senses.example: Organismic psychology studies the person as a whole rather than as a list of traits.
senses.exampleCN: 有机体心理学研究整体的人，而不是一串特质的清单。
senses.why: Psychology borrowed the word for the same reason biology did: some phenomena only appear when the whole is considered. A trait list can miss how the traits interact.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借用这个词，理由与生物学相同：有些现象只有考虑整体时才出现。特质清单可能漏掉特质之间的相互作用。

senses.title: Development as a Whole
senses.titleCN: 发育整体的：过程不可切分
senses.definition: describing development as one integrated process rather than a set of independent events
senses.definitionCN: 把发育描述为一个整合过程，而非一组独立事件
senses.example: In the organismic account, each stage prepares the conditions for the next.
senses.exampleCN: 在整体论的叙述中，每个阶段都为下一阶段准备条件。
senses.why: If stages depend on one another, no single cause explains the outcome. The adjective marks that dependence, which is why it appears in debates about embryos and about growth.
senses.whyCN: 如果各阶段相互依赖，就没有单一原因能解释结果。这个形容词标出的正是这种依赖，因此它出现在关于胚胎与生长的争论中。

senses.title: Irreducible to Parts
senses.definition: not fully explainable by the separate properties of parts
senses.definitionCN: 不能完全由各部件各自的性质来解释
senses.example: The flock's motion has an organismic quality that no single bird possesses.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟群的运动有一种任何单只鸟都不具备的整体性质。
senses.why: This is the strongest form of the claim: the whole has properties the parts lack. The word then belongs to philosophy of biology as much as to biology itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是该主张最强的形式：整体具有部件所缺乏的性质。此时这个词既属于生物学，也属于生物学哲学。

senses.title: System-Like Coherence
senses.definition: showing the coherence of a system whose parts serve one end
senses.definitionCN: 显出各部件服务于同一目的的系统连贯性
senses.example: The city's transport network has an organismic coherence.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的交通网络具有一种有机整体式的连贯性。
senses.why: The metaphor travels beyond biology: any system can look organismic when its parts fit together without a visible designer. The tone is admiring but cautious.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻走出了生物学：任何系统，只要各部分在没有可见设计者的情况下彼此吻合，就显得 organismic。语气是赞赏而谨慎的。

senses.title: Resembling a Living Body
senses.definition: resembling a living body in its organization
senses.definitionCN: 在组织方式上像活体
senses.example: The old library grew in an organismic way, wing by wing.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老图书馆以一种像生物生长的方式，一翼一翼地扩展。
senses.why: Here the adjective is descriptive rather than doctrinal: it says a thing looks grown rather than built. The comparison is to a body, not to a theory.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词是描述性的，而非立场性的：它说某物看起来是「长出来的」而不是「造出来的」。比较的对象是身体，而不是理论。

intro.en: Organismic is organism plus -ic. Organism was coined in the nineteenth century on Greek organon 'tool, instrument'; organismic is a twentieth-century adjective of schools and theories, and its exact first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: organismic 是 organism 加 -ic。organism 于十九世纪建立在希腊 organon「工具、器具」之上；organismic 是二十世纪用于学派与理论的形容词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Organon meant 'tool, instrument', and by extension a body organ. The idea of the body as a set of instruments for the whole is already present in the Greek word.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具」，引申指身体器官。身体作为一整套为整体服务的工具，这一观念已含在希腊词里。

items.en: Organism named a living body as an organized whole. Writers on society soon borrowed it, so the word carried both a biological and a metaphorical load from early on.
items.cn: organism 指作为有组织整体的活体。讨论社会的作者很快借用了它，因此这个词从一开始就同时承载生物学与比喻的双重分量。

items.en: In the twentieth century, biologists who opposed reduction to genes and molecules called their approach organismic biology. The adjective marked a school rather than a level.
items.cn: 二十世纪，反对还原到基因与分子的生物学家把他们的路径称为 organismic biology；这个形容词标出的是学派，而不是层次。

items.en: Psychology adopted the term for approaches that treat the person as an integrated whole. The exact first uses in each field are not firmly dated.
items.cn: 心理学采用该术语，指把个人视为整合整体的路径。它在各领域的确切首见用法没有可靠年代。

items.en: English settled into a division: organismal for the level of the individual, organismic for the claim that wholes organize parts. The two are close relatives but argue different points.
items.cn: 英语逐渐形成分工：organismal 指个体这一层次，organismic 指「整体组织部分」的主张。两者是近亲，却在论证不同的观点。

note.en: The first group separates organismic from the adjective of level and from its doctrinal opposite. The second holds near-synonyms from biology and philosophy.
note.cn: 第一组区分 organismic 与「层次形容词」及其立场上的对立词；第二组是生物学与哲学中的近义词。

entries.definition: Marks the level of the individual organism, as in organismal biology. It names where a study sits, not what it argues.
entries.definitionCN: 标出个体生物这一层次，如 organismal biology；它命名研究的所在层次，而不命名其主张。

entries.definition: Explaining a whole by the workings of its parts as in a machine. It is the standard opponent of organismic in theoretical debate.
entries.definitionCN: 像解释机器那样，用部件的运作来解释整体；在理论争论中是 organismic 的标准对立词。

entries.definition: Means 'of living things' or 'grown without chemicals'. It describes a property and carries no theory of wholes.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「生物的」或「不用化学方式种植的」；描述性质，不携带任何整体理论。

entries.definition: Treating a whole as more than the sum of its parts. It is broader and used outside biology, while organismic keeps the body image.
entries.definitionCN: 把整体视为大于部分之和；更宽泛，可用于生物学之外，而 organismic 保留了身体意象。

entries.definition: Relating to a system as a whole. It is neutral about whether the whole organizes its parts, which organismic asserts.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为整体的系统有关；对「整体是否组织其部分」保持中性，而 organismic 则明确主张这一点。

entries.definition: Combining parts or fields into one account. It stresses the act of joining rather than the primacy of the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 把部件或领域合并为一种说明；强调合并的动作，而不是整体的优先性。

entries.definition: Relating to organisms and their surroundings. It concerns interactions across levels, not the internal organization of one body.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物及其环境的关系有关；关注跨层次的互动，而不是单个身体的内部组织。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: organism + -ic: the adjective of a school that begins with the whole.
normal.cn: organism + -ic：从整体出发的那个学派的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs organism, organismal, organismic, organic, organ, organization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 organism、organismal、organismic、organic、organ、organization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the school: organismic biology, organismic psychology, organismic theory.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出学派：有机体生物学、有机体心理学、有机体论。

normal.en: Its opposite is mechanistic: whole-first against part-first.
normal.cn: 它的对立词是 mechanistic：整体优先对部件优先。

normal.en: organismal is where you study; organismic is what you argue.
normal.cn: organismal 说的是在哪一层研究，organismic 说的是主张什么。

abstract.en: Picture a net lifted by one corner: every knot moves, none can be removed alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网被一角提起：每个结点都在动，没有一个能被单独取下。

abstract.en: Picture a choir where no single voice makes the chord.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱团，没有任何一个声音单独构成那个和弦。

abstract.en: Picture a house that grew room by room instead of being drawn all at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子是一间间长出来的，而不是一次画好的。

examples.en: Organismic approaches ask what a part does for the whole.
examples.cn: 整体取向的方法追问一个部件为整体做了什么。

examples.en: The debate between organismic and mechanistic views is older than genetics.
examples.cn: 整体论与机械论之间的争论比遗传学更古老。

examples.en: Her organismic reading of the novel treats every chapter as one body.
examples.cn: 她对这部小说的有机整体式解读，把每一章都视为同一个身体。

dict_mnemonic.text: organism（有机体）+ ic（……的）→ 把整体当有机体的 → 有机整体的、整体论的

root: 希腊 organon「工具、器官」→ 拉丁 organum → 英语 organism（十九世纪）→ organismic（二十世纪，用于整体论学派）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with the whole and work downward: the whole organizes parts, opposes mechanism, names a school, shapes psychology, describes development, resists reduction, shows system coherence and merely resembles a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从整体出发向下推：整体组织部分、反对机械论、命名学派、塑造心理学、描述发育、抵抗还原、显出系统连贯，以及仅仅像一具身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a net lifted by one corner, every knot moved by the same pull.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被一角提起的网，每个结点都被同一股力牵动。

branches.en: WHOLE BEFORE PARTS: the body organizes its members, and mechanism is the standing opponent.
branches.cn: 整体先于部件：身体组织其成员，而机械论是长期的对立面。

branches.en: NAMED SCHOOLS: biology and psychology each adopted the word for a whole-first tradition.
branches.cn: 具名学派：生物学与心理学各自采用这个词，指一种整体优先的传统。

branches.en: DEVELOPMENT AS ONE: stages prepare each other, so no single cause explains the result.
branches.cn: 发育为一：各阶段互为准备，因此没有单一原因能解释结果。

branches.en: NO REDUCTION: the whole may have properties that no part possesses.
branches.cn: 不可还原：整体可能具有任何部件都不具备的性质。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR TRAVELS: networks and buildings can look grown rather than built.
branches.cn: 比喻外溢：网络与建筑可以显得是「长出来的」而非「造出来的」。

intro.en: Organismic is a noun of organized life with the adjective suffix -ic: an instrument-root, a suffix of state, and a suffix of quality or school.

latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon 与拉丁 organum 衍生 organ、organic、organism、organismal、organismic。-ic 结尾与把 system 变成 systemic、把 theory 变成 theoretic 的那个后缀相同。

definition_zh: 土壤侵蚀
definition_en: the wearing away of topsoil by natural forces or human activity
core_image: 斜坡上被雨水冲出一道道沟壑的裸露山坡，树根裸露
scene: 地理课纪录片里解说员说： After the forest was cleared, soil erosion turned the hillside into gullies within a decade.
sceneCN: 这里指「雨水冲走了山坡上的表层土壤」（第1个义项：自然力或人类活动把表层土带走）；句意为森林砍伐后，土壤侵蚀十年内把山坡冲出一条条沟。

pos.zh: 土壤侵蚀（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 火山爆发（近音但不同源）

senses.title: Topsoil washed away by water
senses.definition: the most common form, where rain or river flow carries topsoil downhill into streams or oceans
senses.definitionCN: 最常见的形式，雨水或河流把表层土带下山，流入小溪或海洋
senses.example: Heavy monsoon rains caused severe soil erosion in the rice fields.
senses.exampleCN: 雨季的暴雨让稻田发生严重的土壤侵蚀。
senses.why: Water is the number one agent of soil erosion because it has weight and flows downhill.
senses.whyCN: 水流是土壤侵蚀第一推手，因为它有重量且往低处流。

senses.title: Topsoil blown away by wind
senses.definition: happens in dry regions where vegetation has been removed, turning fields into dust bowls
senses.definitionCN: 发生在干旱区、植被被清除后，把农田变成尘土碗
senses.example: The Great Dust Bowl of the 1930s was mostly wind-driven soil erosion.
senses.exampleCN: 1930 年代美国大沙尘暴主要是风力造成的土壤侵蚀。
senses.why: Wind can move fine soil particles when they are dry and unprotected.
senses.whyCN: 干燥又没保护的细土颗粒风能吹走。

senses.title: Caused by human farming practices
senses.definition: plowing too close to slopes, leaving fields bare over winter, or planting the same crop every year
senses.definitionCN: 紧贴山坡耕作、冬季让田地裸露、年年种同一种作物
senses.example: Conventional farming without cover crops speeds up soil erosion.
senses.exampleCN: 不种覆盖作物的常规耕作加速土壤侵蚀。
senses.why: Tilling removes the protective layer that roots and plant litter normally provide.
senses.whyCN: 翻土破坏了根系和落叶提供的保护层。

senses.title: Caused by construction or mining
senses.definition: stripping vegetation from large areas for roads, buildings or mines exposes bare soil to rain and wind
senses.definitionCN: 为修路、建房或采矿大面积剥离植被，让裸土暴露给风雨
senses.example: The highway project caused significant soil erosion on nearby hillsides.
senses.exampleCN: 这条公路工程让附近山坡出现显著的土壤侵蚀。
senses.why: Construction removes vegetation in a single step, creating large bare patches at once.
senses.whyCN: 建设在一步之内清除植被，瞬间制造大片裸土。

senses.title: Natural slow erosion over centuries
senses.definition: erosion that happens without human help, as glaciers retreat or rivers meander
senses.definitionCN: 没有人为干预时发生的侵蚀，如冰川后退或河流改道
senses.example: Natural soil erosion shaped the Grand Canyon over millions of years.
senses.exampleCN: 自然的土壤侵蚀在几百万年间塑成了大峡谷。
senses.why: Geologists see soil erosion as part of a slow natural cycle rather than a disaster.
senses.whyCN: 地质学家把土壤侵蚀视为慢自然循环的一部分而非灾难。

senses.title: Social or economic analogy
senses.definition: the slow loss of something valuable over time
senses.definitionCN: 有价值的东西随时间慢慢流失
senses.example: Cultural soil erosion has been accelerated by mass media.
senses.exampleCN: 大众传媒加速了文化根基的流失。
senses.why: Erosion is a powerful metaphor because it describes a gradual, invisible process.
senses.whyCN: 侵蚀是强有力的比喻，因为它描述的是一个缓慢、看不见的过程。

senses.title: Coastal soil erosion
senses.definition: waves and tides carrying away sand and cliffs along shorelines
senses.definitionCN: 海浪和潮汐带走岸边的沙子和悬崖
senses.example: Coastal soil erosion has forced three villages to relocate in the past decade.
senses.exampleCN: 过去十年，海岸土壤侵蚀迫使三个村庄搬迁。
senses.why: Coastal erosion is driven by a different agent (waves) but produces the same kind of loss.
senses.whyCN: 海岸侵蚀的动力是海浪，但后果同样是土壤流失。

senses.title: Prevention and conservation
senses.definition: methods to stop or reduce soil loss, including terraces, cover crops, and windbreaks
senses.definitionCN: 防止或减少土壤流失的方法，包括梯田、覆盖作物、防风林
senses.example: Farmers in the Andes have used terraces to fight soil erosion for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 安第斯山的农民用梯田抵御土壤侵蚀已有数百年。
senses.why: Because erosion is natural, prevention works by keeping soil in place rather than stopping the forces.
senses.whyCN: 因为侵蚀是自然的，防治靠的是把土留住，不是消灭风雨。

intro.en: erosion comes from Latin erodere, which itself breaks into e- (out) + rodere (to gnaw); soil erosion is a compound noun meaning 'the gnawing away of soil'.
intro.cn: erosion 来自拉丁语 erodere，拆成 e-（出去）+ rodere（啃）；soil erosion 是复合名词，意为「土壤被啃掉」。

items.en: erodere = e- (out) + rodere (to gnaw) → to gnaw out, to wear away. Past participle eresus yielded erosio, the noun for the result.
items.cn: erodere = e-（出）+ rodere（啃）→ 啃出来、磨掉。过去分词 eresus 给出 erosio 这个名词。

items.en: Old French borrowed erosio as érosion, keeping the meaning of 'a wearing away'.
items.cn: 古法语借入 erosio 为 érosion，意思是「磨掉的过程」。

items.en: English erosion appeared in the mid-17th century, first in geology, borrowed directly from Latin.
items.cn: 17 世纪中期英语出现 erosion，最早用于地质学，直接从拉丁语借入。

items.en: The phrase soil erosion started being used in the 19th century as soil conservation science emerged.
items.cn: soil erosion 这个短语在 19 世纪土壤保护科学兴起时开始使用。

items.en: The Dust Bowl of the 1930s made soil erosion a household phrase in the United States.
items.cn: 1930 年代的大沙尘暴让 soil erosion 在美国家喻户晓。

items.en: The term is central to agriculture, geography, environmental science and policy.
items.cn: 这个术语是农业、地理、环境科学和政策的核心词。

note.en: Group one is the erosion family of rodere root; group two lists related environmental processes.
note.cn: 第一组是 rodere 词根下的 erosion 家族；第二组是相关的环境过程。

entries.definition: To wear away gradually, as water erodes rock over time.
entries.definitionCN: 渐渐磨掉，如水慢慢侵蚀岩石。

entries.definition: The general process of wearing away, not only of soil.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指「磨掉」的过程，不限于土壤。

entries.definition: Having the power to erode; used for water, wind, acid.
entries.definitionCN: 有侵蚀能力的；用于水、风、酸。

entries.definition: Volcanic eruption comes from erumpere (to burst out), not rodere.
entries.definitionCN: 火山爆发来自 erumpere（迸发），与 rodere 不同源。

entries.definition: Breaking down rock in place; differs from erosion which carries material away.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石在原地碎裂；区别于 erosion——后者把碎粒搬走。

entries.definition: The opposite end of erosion: eroded material is deposited somewhere.
entries.definitionCN: erosion 的另一端：被侵蚀的物质被沉积到别处。

entries.definition: Removing forests; one of the main human causes of soil erosion.
entries.definitionCN: 砍伐森林；人类造成土壤侵蚀的主要原因之一。

entries.definition: Land turning to desert, often through erosion and overgrazing.
entries.definitionCN: 土地变成沙漠，常由侵蚀和过度放牧导致。

normalIntro.en: Soil erosion is soil being 'gnawed away' by water or wind.
normalIntro.cn: soil erosion 就是土壤被水或风「啃掉」。

normal.en: Erode = gnaw away; erosion = the gnawing; soil erosion = gnawing of soil.
normal.cn: Erode = 啃掉；erosion = 啃的过程；soil erosion = 啃土壤。

normal.en: Remember the Dust Bowl: wind took the topsoil away.
normal.cn: 记得大沙尘暴：风把表层土刮走了。

normal.en: Farmers fight soil erosion with terraces on hills.
normal.cn: 农民用山上的梯田对抗 soil erosion。

normal.en: Roots hold soil; when trees are cut, erosion wins.
normal.cn: 树根把土抓住；树被砍了，erosion 就赢了。

normal.en: Grand Canyon is millions of years of soil and rock erosion.
normal.cn: 大峡谷是几百万年土壤和岩石的 erosion。

abstract.en: A hillside of dirt that slowly melts into a stream after every rain.
abstract.cn: 每下一次雨就慢慢融进小溪的一个泥坡。

abstract.en: Teeth marks of wind and water across green farmland.
abstract.cn: 风和水在绿色农田上留下的牙印。

abstract.en: A painting that slowly fades where the canvas is exposed to sun.
abstract.cn: 帆布向阳处慢慢褪色的一幅画。

examples.en: The EU has spent billions on terraces and windbreaks to fight soil erosion in the Mediterranean.
examples.cn: 欧盟在地中海花了几十亿修梯田和防风林对抗土壤侵蚀。

examples.en: Satellite photos show that soil erosion is accelerating on deforested hillsides.
examples.cn: 卫星照片显示被砍伐的山坡上土壤侵蚀在加速。

examples.en: Local farmers plant cover crops each winter to prevent soil erosion.
examples.cn: 当地农民每年冬天种覆盖作物防止土壤侵蚀。
