definition_zh: 绝缘体；绝缘材料；绝缘子；隔绝外界影响的东西
definition_en: a material or object that stops electricity, heat or sound from passing, or something that cuts people off from outside influence
core_image: 一块干燥的橡胶把带电的铜线裹住，手可以放心地握住外面那层
scene: 电工作业时先戴上厚橡胶手套，再去碰那根裸线，手套外层的材料把电流牢牢挡在里面。 A thick rubber insulator kept the current away from her hands.
sceneCN: 这里 insulator 指「绝缘体、绝缘材料」（第 1 个义项：阻止电流通过的材料）；句意为厚橡胶绝缘层把电流挡在她手外。图中可辨识物件：橡胶手套、裸线、配电箱、绝缘垫。

pos.zh: 绝缘体；绝缘材料；绝缘子
隔绝外界影响的人或物（比喻）

senses.title: A material that blocks current
senses.definition: a material that does not let electric charge pass through it easily
senses.definitionCN: 不易让电荷通过的材料
senses.example: Rubber is a good insulator, so gloves are made from it.
senses.exampleCN: 橡胶是良绝缘体，因此手套用橡胶做。
senses.why: The Latin word meant 'made into an island', and an island keeps water out: an insulator keeps charge out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词意为「被造成岛屿」，岛把水挡在外面：绝缘体把电荷挡在外面。

senses.title: A specific electrical insulator
senses.titleCN: 电绝缘材料：具体的绝缘物质
senses.definition: a particular material such as glass, rubber or ceramic used to block current
senses.definitionCN: 玻璃、橡胶、陶瓷等具体用来阻断电流的材料
senses.example: Glass is used as an insulator in high-voltage fittings.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃在高压配件中用作绝缘材料。
senses.why: The general property becomes a trade material, so the word names the substances an engineer actually chooses.
senses.whyCN: 一般性质变成行业材料，因此这个词指工程师实际挑选的那些物质。

senses.title: A thermal insulator
senses.definition: a material that slows the passage of heat
senses.definitionCN: 减缓热传递的材料
senses.example: Foam is a thermal insulator, so it keeps the pipe warm.
senses.exampleCN: 泡沫是绝热材料，因此能让管道保温。
senses.why: Heat needs a path through matter, and a material full of trapped air removes that path.
senses.whyCN: 热需要穿过物质的路径，而充满滞留空气的材料把这条路径去掉了。

senses.title: A sound insulator
senses.definition: a material that reduces the passage of sound
senses.definitionCN: 减弱声音传播的材料
senses.example: The studio walls use a sound insulator between the layers.
senses.exampleCN: 录音室墙体在层间使用隔音材料。
senses.why: Sound is vibration carried through matter, so a soft, air-filled layer breaks the chain of contact that would pass it on.
senses.whyCN: 声音是靠物质传递的振动，因此柔软、含空气的一层会打断那条本可传声的接触链。

senses.title: The ceramic part on a power line
senses.titleCN: 绝缘子：输电设备上的瓷件
senses.definition: a shaped ceramic or glass part that holds a live conductor away from its support
senses.definitionCN: 把带电导线与支架隔开的成形陶瓷或玻璃部件
senses.example: The porcelain insulator flashed over in the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雨中那只瓷绝缘子发生了闪络。
senses.why: Engineering turns the material into a named component: the insulator is the object that does the blocking on a pole.
senses.whyCN: 工程把材料变成有名字的部件：绝缘子就是杆上执行阻断的那个物件。

senses.title: The sheath on a cable
senses.titleCN: 电线护套：包在导线外的绝缘层
senses.definition: the covering around a wire that keeps current inside and hands outside
senses.definitionCN: 包在导线外、把电流关在里面、把人挡在外面的包层
senses.example: The insulator on the old cable had cracked.
senses.exampleCN: 旧电缆外面的绝缘层已经开裂。
senses.why: The material becomes a manufactured covering, so the same noun names a thin sheath rather than a block.
senses.whyCN: 材料变成了制成品包层，因此同一个名词可以指薄薄的一层护套，而不是厚块。

senses.title: Something that cuts you off
senses.titleCN: 比喻：隔绝外界影响的东西
senses.definition: something that keeps a person or group apart from outside influence
senses.definitionCN: 使个人或群体与外界影响隔开的东西
senses.example: Wealth acted as an insulator against the noise of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 财富成了一道把城市的喧闹挡在外面的屏障。
senses.why: The metaphor is physical again: as rubber blocks charge, money or distance blocks disturbance.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻又回到物理层面：橡胶挡住电荷，金钱或距离挡住干扰。

senses.title: A protective barrier
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把人与干扰隔开的屏障
senses.definition: a barrier that protects someone from criticism, pressure or unwanted contact
senses.definitionCN: 保护某人免受批评、压力或不想要的接触的屏障
senses.example: His routine was an insulator between work and worry.
senses.exampleCN: 他的日常作息成了工作与忧虑之间的一道屏障。
senses.why: A habit can work like a layer of rubber: it keeps outside pressure from reaching the person inside.
senses.whyCN: 习惯可以像一层橡胶那样起作用：它让外界的压力到不了里面的人。

intro.en: Insulator comes from Latin insula 'island' through the verb insulate, 'to make into an island'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: insulator 经动词 insulate「使成岛屿」上溯拉丁 insula「岛」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Insula meant 'island' and also a block of flats in Rome; the core picture is something surrounded by a barrier.
items.cn: insula 意为「岛」，也指罗马城里的一栋公寓楼；核心图景是被屏障围住的某物。

items.en: Insulatus meant 'made like an island', that is, cut off from what surrounds it.
items.cn: insulatus 意为「被造成岛屿那样」，也就是与周围隔开。

items.en: English insulate appeared in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries for setting something apart, and only later for blocking heat or charge.
items.cn: 英语 insulate 在十六、十七世纪出现，指把某物隔开，后来才用于阻挡热或电。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century experimenters called materials that block charge insulators, and the word became a technical noun.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪的实验者把阻断电荷的材料称为绝缘体，这个词成为技术名词。

items.en: Telegraph and power lines needed shaped ceramic and glass pieces, so insulator also named a manufactured component.
items.cn: 电报与电力线路需要成形的陶瓷与玻璃件，因此 insulator 也指一种制成品部件。

items.en: Twentieth-century writing extended the noun to anything that shields a person from outside pressure.
items.cn: 二十世纪的写作把这个名词扩展到任何为人挡住外界压力的事物。

note.en: Group one holds derivatives of the same island root; group two holds materials and barriers with a similar job.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「岛」这一词根的派生词；第二组是作用相近的材料与屏障。

entries.definition: To cut something off from heat, charge or contact; the noun is the material that does it.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物与热、电或接触隔开；名词是执行这件事的材料。

entries.definition: The act or the whole layer of insulating material, rather than one piece.
entries.definitionCN: 绝缘行为或整层绝缘材料，而非单个物件。

entries.definition: Island-like, hence narrow in outlook; it keeps the literal island image.
entries.definitionCN: 像岛一样的，因而引申为眼界狭窄；保留了字面的岛的形象。

entries.definition: To set apart from others; it shares the island picture but not the technical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 使与别人分开；共享「岛」的图景，但没有技术义。

entries.definition: A material that polarizes rather than conducts; common in capacitors and cable design.
entries.definitionCN: 会极化而不导电的材料；常用于电容器与电缆设计。

entries.definition: A simple word for a material that does not carry charge.
entries.definitionCN: 不导电材料的平实说法。

entries.definition: Something that blocks a hazard; it may reflect or absorb rather than simply refuse passage.
entries.definitionCN: 挡住危险的东西；它可能反射或吸收，而不只是拒绝通过。

entries.definition: Anything that stops movement or influence, often literal and often social.
entries.definitionCN: 阻挡移动或影响的任何东西，常为具体之物，也常用于社会语境。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real island root, the real engineering part and the real contrast with a conductor.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「岛」词根、真实的工程部件，以及它与导体的真实对照。

normal.en: The root is island: an insulator makes a little island that charge cannot cross.
normal.cn: 词根是「岛」：绝缘体造出一座小岛，电荷过不去。

normal.en: The family runs insulate, insulation, insulating, insulator and the older insular.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 insulate、insulation、insulating、insulator 以及更早的 insular。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the job: electrical insulator, thermal insulator, sound insulator, ceramic insulator.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用途：电绝缘体、绝热材料、隔音材料、陶瓷绝缘子。

normal.en: The pair is clean: a conductor passes, an insulator refuses.
normal.cn: 这一对很清楚：导体放行，绝缘体拒绝。

normal.en: On a power pole the insulator is a visible object, not just a property.
normal.cn: 在电线杆上，绝缘子是一件看得见的物件，而不只是一种性质。

abstract.en: Picture a dry rubber coat around a live wire, and a hand on the coat.
abstract.cn: 想象带电导线外裹着一层干橡胶，一只手按在橡胶上。

abstract.en: Picture a moat around a castle: the same water that would carry a boat is now a barrier.
abstract.cn: 想象城堡周围的护城河：本来能载船的水，此刻成了屏障。

abstract.en: Picture a person surrounded by so much quiet that the city cannot reach them.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人被足够的安静围住，城市的声音到不了他。

examples.en: Dry air is a decent insulator until the voltage is high enough to break it down.
examples.cn: 干燥空气是尚可的绝缘体，直到电压高到把它击穿。

examples.en: Each insulator on the line was inspected after the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴之后，线路上的每只绝缘子都被检查过。

examples.en: Long hours alone had become an insulator against bad news.
examples.cn: 长时间的独处成了一道挡住坏消息的屏障。

dict_mnemonic.text: insul-（岛）+ -ator（做某事的东西）——把电流围成一座进不来的岛 → 绝缘体

root: 拉丁 insula（岛）→ insulatus（被造成岛屿的）→ 英语 insulate（隔开）→ insulator（执行隔绝的材料或部件）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with a material that blocks charge and narrow to trade substances, then block heat and sound, become a ceramic part and a cable sheath, and end with a barrier against the world.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从阻断电荷的材料开始，收窄到行业物质，再阻断热与声，成为瓷件与电缆护套，最后落到挡住外界的屏障。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dry rubber coat around a live wire, with a hand resting safely on the outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：带电导线外裹着干橡胶，一只手安全地放在外面。

branches.en: The general material and the specific substances an engineer selects.
branches.cn: 一般材料，以及工程师具体选择的物质。

branches.en: Heat stopped by trapping air and removing its path.
branches.cn: 用滞留空气去掉通路，从而挡住热。

branches.en: Sound stopped before it reaches the other side of a wall.
branches.cn: 声音在到达墙的另一面之前被挡住。

branches.en: Two made objects: the ceramic piece on a pole, and the sheath on a wire.
branches.cn: 两件制成品：杆上的瓷件，以及导线外的护套。

branches.en: The barrier turned social: money, routine or distance kept between a person and the world.
branches.cn: 屏障转向社会：金钱、作息或距离被放在一个人与世界之间。

intro.en: Insulator is the agent noun of insulate, built on the Latin word for island.
intro.cn: insulator 是 insulate 的施事名词，建立在拉丁语「岛」一词上。

latinIntro.en: Latin insula gives insulatus 'made like an island'; English insulate and insulator grew from that, while isolate came through Italian from the same source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 insula 给出 insulatus「被造成岛屿那样」；英语 insulate 与 insulator 由此发展，isolate 则经意大利语同出一源。

items.meaning: to cut off from heat, charge or contact
items.meaningCN: 使绝缘；使隔离（岛词根加动词后缀，地点转为动作）
items.example: They insulated the loft last winter.
items.exampleCN: 他们去年冬天给阁楼做了保温。

items.meaning: a material or part that blocks passage
items.meaningCN: 绝缘体（加施事后缀，动作转执行材料）
items.example: The insulator failed in the rain.

items.meaning: the act or the material that insulates
items.meaningCN: 绝缘；绝缘材料（加过程后缀，动作转行为与材料）

items.meaning: serving to block heat or charge
items.meaningCN: 起绝缘作用的（加形容词后缀，动作为属性）
items.example: An insulating mat covers the floor.
items.exampleCN: 地面上铺着一块绝缘垫。

items.meaningCN: 岛屿的；偏狭的（岛词根加形容词后缀，地理义转为性格义）
items.exampleCN: 偏狭的习惯拖慢了改革。

items.meaning: the state of being cut off or narrow
items.meaningCN: 隔绝状态；偏狭（再加性质后缀，性格义转抽象名词）
items.exampleCN: 与外界隔绝使村子多疑。

items.meaningCN: 隔离；使孤立（同源「岛」义经意大利语，地理义转为分离动作）
items.exampleCN: 他们把故障电池单独隔开。

items.meaning: the state of being set apart
items.meaningCN: 隔离状态（加过程后缀，动作转状态）
items.example: The ward was kept in isolation.

items.meaningCN: 半岛（「几乎」加岛，岛的图景被减弱）
items.example: The town sits on a peninsula.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇子坐落在一个半岛上。

latinEntries.meaning: made like an island; cut off
latinEntries.meaningCN: 被造成岛屿那样的；隔开的

definition_zh: 潜意识状态；下意识的心理活动；半清醒状态；未进入注意的隐约感知
definition_en: the condition of mental life going on below ordinary awareness
core_image: 一栋房子上层点着灯，地下的管道仍在输水，热气顺着墙往上爬，屋里的人只觉得墙是温的
scene: 深夜写字的人没听见窗外雨声，笔却越写越快，句子也越来越短，直到天亮才发现纸上有水汽。 A slow subconsciousness shaped the rhythm of the page long before he noticed the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 subconsciousness 指「未进入注意、却持续影响产出的心理状态」（第 1 个义项：在觉察之下的心理状态）；句意是一种缓慢的潜意识状态，在他注意到雨之前就已决定了这一页的节奏。图中可辨识物件：台灯、稿纸、窗上的水汽。

pos.zh: 潜意识状态；下意识的心理活动；半清醒状态

senses.title: Mental life below the surface
senses.definition: the condition in which thinking and feeling continue without being noticed
senses.definitionCN: 思考与感受在未被注意的情况下继续进行的状况
senses.example: A slow subconsciousness shaped the rhythm of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 一种缓慢的潜意识状态决定了这一页的节奏。
senses.why: the noun names a condition rather than a place, so it can be entered, left and measured in degrees.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名的是状况而非地点，因此可以被进入、离开，也可以按程度衡量。

senses.title: Automatic inner work
senses.definition: the ordinary sorting, connecting and rehearsing that the mind does without being asked
senses.definitionCN: 心智未经要求便自行进行的归类、联结与预演
senses.example: Repetition moved the sentence into subconsciousness, where it repeated itself.
senses.exampleCN: 重复让那句话进入潜意识，在那里自己反复起来。
senses.why: once a task has been handed down to the lower level, it runs on its own and surfaces only as a result.
senses.whyCN: 任务一旦被交给下层，便自行运转，只以结果的形式浮上来。

senses.title: Half waking
senses.definition: a drowsy condition in which some impressions register but full awareness does not return
senses.definitionCN: 昏沉之中，部分印象被接收，完整觉察却没有回来
senses.example: In the first minutes after waking he still moved in subconsciousness.
senses.exampleCN: 刚醒的几分钟里，他仍处在半醒的潜意识状态。
senses.why: the word literally means the state of being under awareness, and the surface can be crossed by halves.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面就是「在觉察之下的状态」，而水面是可以只过一半的。

senses.title: Impressions below attention
senses.definition: sights and sounds that are registered without being attended to at the time
senses.definitionCN: 当时未被留意、却仍被记录下来的景象与声音
senses.example: The hum of the train stayed in subconsciousness and came back as a dream.
senses.exampleCN: 火车的嗡鸣留在潜意识里，后来以梦的形式回来。
senses.why: registration and attention are two different doors, and this word names the state of the first door being open alone.
senses.whyCN: 记录与注意是两扇不同的门，这个词命名的正是只开第一扇门的状态。

senses.title: The shared lower layer
senses.definition: a common reservoir of images and patterns said to be shared by a whole group or species
senses.definitionCN: 据称由整个群体或物种共有的一处意象与模式储藏所
senses.example: He argued that myths rise out of a collective subconsciousness.
senses.exampleCN: 他认为神话从集体潜意识中升起。
senses.why: the noun is lifted from one sleeper to a whole people, which is how the collective phrase came about.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词从单个睡者抬到整个民族，集体这一说法正是这样来的。

senses.title: An unexamined preference
senses.definition: a like or dislike that operates steadily without ever being put into words
senses.definitionCN: 一种稳定起作用、却从未被说成话的好恶
senses.example: His subconsciousness favoured round numbers before any argument began.
senses.exampleCN: 在争论开始之前，他的潜意识已经偏向整数。
senses.why: preferences can be formed below and then arrive in behaviour fully dressed, with no reasoning attached.
senses.whyCN: 偏好可以在下层形成，然后整装出现在行为里，后面不带任何推理。

senses.title: The region as a research label
senses.titleCN: 作为研究标签的那一区域
senses.definition: the name given in older psychology to the whole field between attention and the deepest layer
senses.definitionCN: 旧日心理学给注意与最深那层之间整片区域所起的名字
senses.example: Textbooks of the period treat subconsciousness as a separate chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 那个时期的教科书把潜意识单列一章。
senses.why: when a field is mapped, each band needs a noun, and this one was given the abstract form of the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 一旦要给领域画图，每一带都需要一个名词，而这一带用的就是那个形容词的抽象形式。

senses.title: How it bends what we do
senses.titleCN: 它如何改变我们的行为
senses.definition: the influence itself, understood as a pressure that alters choices before they are made
senses.definitionCN: 指那股影响本身，被理解为在选择做出之前就改变选择的压力
senses.example: The subconsciousness of the crowd turned a quiet street into a route.
senses.exampleCN: 人群的潜意识把一条安静的街变成了一条路线。
senses.why: the state is finally read as a force, which is what makes the word useful outside psychology.
senses.whyCN: 这个状态最后被读成一股力，这正是这个词在心理学之外也有用的原因。

intro.en: Subconsciousness is built inside English from subconscious plus the state suffix -ness, and subconscious itself is a modern compound of a Latin prefix and a Latin-derived adjective. It belongs to nineteenth-century psychological vocabulary. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: subconsciousness 是在英语内部由 subconscious 加表状态的后缀构成的，而 subconscious 本身是近代用拉丁前缀与拉丁来源形容词搭成的复合词。它属于 19 世纪心理学词汇。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sub 'under, below' is the positional prefix seen in submarine and subordinate; here it puts a whole layer beneath another.
items.cn: sub 意为「在下、低于」，是潜艇、下属等词里的位置前缀；在这里它把一整层放到另一层之下。

items.en: The base adjective descends from a Latin verb meaning 'to know' through a prefixed form meaning 'knowing with oneself'.
items.cn: 词基形容词经一个意为「与己同知」的带前缀形式，上溯到意为「知道」的拉丁动词。

items.en: Subconscious appears in nineteenth-century writing on the mind, and the abstract noun follows quickly, since a state needs a noun of its own.
items.cn: subconscious 出现在 19 世纪论心智的著述中，抽象名词随即跟上，因为一种状态需要自己的名词。

items.en: The suffix -ness is native Germanic and turns adjectives into names for states, as in darkness and kindness.
items.cn: 后缀表示状态，是日耳曼语本族成分，把形容词变成状态的名称，如黑暗、善意。

items.en: Twentieth-century popular writing extended the noun to groups and to ordinary preferences, which is where most non-technical uses now come from.
items.cn: 20 世纪通俗写作把这个名词延伸到群体与日常偏好，如今大多数非专业用法都出自这里。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first attested use of the abstract noun is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of the base root remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个抽象名词最早的确切用例未定，词根在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the near-identical nouns that differ only by prefix; group two holds nouns for states of mind that sit close to this one.
note.cn: 第一组是只差前缀、字形极近的名词；第二组是表示相近心理状态的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective and the common noun for the layer; this word is the abstract name of the condition, so it fits after verbs like sink into.
entries.definitionCN: 既是形容词，也是指那一层的常用名词；本词是那种状况的抽象名称，因此适合跟在「沉入」一类动词之后。

entries.definition: Means awareness is gone, as in coma; this word means awareness is still present but working lower down.
entries.definitionCN: 指觉察消失，如昏迷；本词指觉察仍在，只是在更下层运作。

entries.definition: The direct opposite: the lighted state itself, without which the lower layer would have no name.
entries.definitionCN: 直接的反义：那盏亮着的状态本身，没有它，下层也就无从命名。

entries.definition: A rare noun for material just outside awareness that can be recalled at will; the position is outside rather than underneath.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见名词，指刚好在觉察之外、可随意唤回的材料；位置是在外面而非下面。

entries.definition: The physical heaviness before sleep; it explains half waking but says nothing about hidden mental work.
entries.definitionCN: 入睡前身体的沉重感；能解释「半醒」，却不涉及隐藏的心理运作。

entries.definition: A state of narrowed attention, often induced; it is a condition of the whole person, not a layer of the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 注意收窄的状态，常由外界引发；是整个人的状况，而非心智的一层。

entries.definition: What arrives from below as a ready-made judgement; it is the product, while this word names the workshop.
entries.definitionCN: 从下层送达的现成判断；它是产品，而本词命名的是那间作坊。

entries.definition: An everyday phrase for private thoughts and feelings, including those one is fully aware of.
entries.definitionCN: 指私人念头与感受的日常说法，包含本人完全清楚的那些。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Three pieces: a prefix meaning 'under', an adjective meaning 'aware', and a suffix meaning 'state'.
normal.cn: 三块拼成：表「在下」的前缀、表「觉察」的形容词、表「状态」的后缀。

normal.en: The family runs subconscious, subconsciously, subconsciousness, consciousness, unconsciousness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 subconscious、subconsciously、subconsciousness、consciousness、unconsciousness。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: a state of subconsciousness, sink into subconsciousness, surface from subconsciousness.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：潜意识状态、沉入潜意识、从潜意识中浮现。

normal.en: The collective phrase comes from the same pattern used by mythographers and early psychology.
normal.cn: 「集体潜意识」这一说法，来自神话研究者与早期心理学使用的同一构词方式。

normal.en: The abstract noun exists because a condition needs a name, while the adjective already named the place.
normal.cn: 之所以有这个抽象名词，是因为状况需要名称，而形容词已经占用了地点。

abstract.en: Picture a lit upper floor over a basement where pipes keep moving water all night.
abstract.cn: 想象亮着灯的上层，底下是整夜走水的管道。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that keeps writing after the ears have stopped listening.
abstract.cn: 想象耳朵早已不听，手却仍在写。

abstract.en: Picture warmth in a wall that nobody can trace back to a fire.
abstract.cn: 想象墙面发暖，却没人能把它追到一堆火。

examples.en: The phrase describes a subconsciousness that never announces itself.
examples.cn: 这个说法描述的是一种从不自我宣告的潜意识状态。

examples.en: He sank into a subconsciousness in which old songs kept playing.
examples.cn: 他沉入一种潜意识状态，旧歌在其中反复播放。

examples.en: Their collective subconsciousness turned the same legend into a shared dream.
examples.cn: 他们的集体潜意识把同一个传说变成了共同的梦。

dict_mnemonic.text: sub（在下）+ conscious（有意识）+ ness（状态）——在意识之下的那种状态 → 潜意识状态

root: 英语在 subconscious 上加表状态的后缀构成；subconscious 由表「在下」的拉丁前缀加 conscious（源自拉丁 conscius「与……同知」）搭成，属 19 世纪心理学术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a lower level keeps working, and that working is read as a condition, as automatic labour, as half waking, as unrecorded impressions, as a shared reservoir, as an unexamined preference, as a research label and finally as a force.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：下层持续运转，这次运转依次被读作一种状况、自动的劳动、半醒、未被留意的印象、共有的储藏所、未审视的偏好、研究标签，最后是一股力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit upper floor over a basement where pipes keep moving water all night, warming the wall nobody questions.
core.cn: 核心意象：亮着灯的上层，底下是整夜走水的管道，把没人追问的墙面烘暖。

branches.en: THE CONDITION AND ITS HALFWAY POINT: the state itself, and the moment when a person crosses it only in part.
branches.cn: 状况与它的一半：状态本身，以及人只过了一半的那个时刻。

branches.en: WORK AND ITS CHAPTER TITLE: first the automatic labour, then the textbook habit of naming the whole band.
branches.cn: 劳动与它的章节名：先是自动的劳动，再是教科书给整条带命名的习惯。

branches.en: THE OPEN DOOR OF REGISTRATION: what enters without being attended stays and returns later.
branches.cn: 记录之门开着：未被留意而进入的东西会留下，并在后来返回。

branches.en: SHARED AND PRIVATE LOWER LAYERS: one is a reservoir held by a people, the other a preference held by one person.
branches.cn: 共有与私有的下层：一个是整个民族持有的储藏所，一个是单个人持有的偏好。

branches.en: THE STATE READ AS A FORCE: the noun finally names pressure rather than condition.
branches.cn: 状态被读成力：这个名词最后命名的是压力，而不是状况。

intro.en: The word stacks three elements, one positional, one about awareness, one about state, which makes the whole family readable from the outside in.
intro.cn: 这个词叠了三块：一块说位置，一块说觉察，一块说状态，因此整个词族可以从外往内读。

latinIntro.en: Latin sub- 'under' plus the Latin-derived adjective of awareness, then a native English state suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀表「在下」，加上来自拉丁的觉察形容词，最后接一个英语本族的状态后缀。

items.example: The prefix sets the whole word one level down.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把整个词放低一级。

items.example: The adjective supplies the lighted layer.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供那层亮处。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a name for a condition.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成状况的名称。

items.example: A subconscious wish shaped the choice.
items.exampleCN: 一个潜意识的愿望塑造了这个选择。

items.meaning: the condition of working below awareness
items.meaningCN: 在觉察之下运作的状况
items.example: He sank into subconsciousness before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 天亮前他沉入潜意识状态。
她下意识地跟上了他的语气。

definition_zh: 遗传的；基因的；与起源或发生有关的（旧义）
definition_en: relating to genes or heredity, or, in older use, relating to origin and development
core_image: 两株外观相同的幼苗被切开，内部露出一段段不同的指令条纹
scene: 两株同样的苗，一株在阴处长得细弱，一株在阳光下粗壮。 The difference lies in genetic makeup rather than in care.
sceneCN: 这里 genetic 指「与基因组成有关的」（第 1 个义项：与基因相关的）；句意为差别在于基因组成，而不在于照料。可辨识物件：两株幼苗、遮阴布、光照灯、标注基因组成的卡片。

pos.zh: 遗传的；基因的
起源的；发生的（旧义）

senses.title: Relating to genes
senses.definition: relating to genes or the material that carries them
senses.definitionCN: 与基因或承载基因的物质相关
senses.example: Genetic testing can reveal carrier status.
senses.exampleCN: 基因检测可以揭示携带者状态。
senses.why: The adjective attaches the whole vocabulary of heredity to a noun, so testing, material and code all become genetic.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把整套遗传词汇附着到名词上，因此检测、物质与密码都可以成为「基因的」。

senses.title: Inherited rather than acquired
senses.definition: determined by inheritance rather than by environment
senses.definitionCN: 由遗传而非环境决定
senses.example: The condition is genetic, not infectious.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病是遗传的，不是传染的。
senses.why: In this sense the word draws a line: what is genetic comes with the organism, not from contact or choice.
senses.whyCN: 在这个义项里，这个词划出一条界线：遗传之物随生物体而来，不来自接触或选择。

senses.title: Relating to origin or development
senses.titleCN: 与起源或发生有关的（旧义）
senses.definition: concerned with the origin and development of something, especially in older philosophy and linguistics
senses.definitionCN: 与某物的起源和发展有关，尤见于较早的哲学与语言学
senses.example: The genetic link between the two languages is disputed.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种语言之间的谱系联系尚有争议。
senses.why: Before genes were known, genetic meant 'pertaining to origins'; linguistics still uses it for language families.
senses.whyCN: 在基因被发现之前，genetic 意为「与起源有关的」；语言学仍用它指语言谱系。

senses.title: Of genetic engineering
senses.definition: relating to the deliberate alteration of genetic material
senses.definitionCN: 与有意改变遗传物质相关
senses.example: Genetic engineering inserted a bacterial gene into the crop.
senses.exampleCN: 基因工程把一个细菌基因植入作物。
senses.why: Once humans could cut and paste sequences, the adjective began to modify the techniques as well as the material.
senses.whyCN: 当人类能够剪切与粘贴序列后，这个形容词开始修饰技术，而不只是物质。

senses.title: Of the genetic code
senses.definition: relating to the mapping from nucleotide triplets to amino acids
senses.definitionCN: 与核苷酸三联体到氨基酸的对应关系相关
senses.example: The genetic code maps triplets to amino acids.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传密码把三联体映射到氨基酸。
senses.why: The word describes a system of correspondence, not a single gene, which is why code is its natural noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述一套对应系统，而非单个基因，因此「密码」是它的自然搭配。

senses.title: Of genetic diversity
senses.definition: relating to the range of genetic variation within a group
senses.definitionCN: 与一个群体内遗传变异的幅度相关
senses.example: Genetic diversity protects a population from disease.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传多样性保护群体免受疾病。
senses.why: Here the adjective measures variety across a group, so it contrasts with uniformity rather than with environment.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个形容词衡量群体内的差异，因此与「一致」相对，而非与环境相对。

senses.title: Of a genetic predisposition
senses.definition: relating to an inherited tendency that raises the likelihood of a condition
senses.definitionCN: 与提高患病可能性的遗传倾向相关
senses.example: A genetic predisposition raises the risk but does not decide it.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传易感性提高风险，但不决定结果。
senses.why: The phrase keeps inheritance and inevitability apart, a distinction the adjective alone does not make.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把遗传与必然分开，而单靠形容词并不能作出这一区分。

senses.title: Of genetic relationship
senses.titleCN: 遗传关系或谱系关系的
senses.definition: relating to shared ancestry, whether of organisms or of languages
senses.definitionCN: 与共同祖先相关，无论指生物还是语言
senses.example: Genetic relationship among species is measured by shared sequences.
senses.exampleCN: 物种间的遗传关系由共享序列来测量。
senses.why: The older 'origin' sense and the newer 'gene' sense meet here: shared ancestry can be read from sequences or from language forms.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的「起源」义与较新的「基因」义在此相遇：共同祖先既可从序列读出，也可从语言形式读出。

intro.en: Genetic comes from Greek genetikos 'generative', through French génétique. English first used it for 'pertaining to origin' from 1831, and from the early twentieth century, often dated 1908, for genes and heredity.
intro.cn: genetic 来自希腊 genetikos「生殖的」，经法语 génétique 传入。英语从 1831 年起用它表示「与起源有关的」，到 20 世纪初（常定在 1908 年）才用于基因与遗传。

items.en: Genos 'race, kind, birth' belongs to the PIE family reconstructed as *ǵenh₁-, so the root form is a reconstruction; Latin genus is a cognate, not the source.
items.cn: genos「种族、种类、出生」属于被重构为 *ǵenh₁- 的原始印欧语词族，因此该词根形式是重构；拉丁 genus 是同源词，并非来源。

items.en: Genetikos 'generative' was built on genesis 'origin' with the adjectival suffix -ikos.
items.cn: genetikos「生殖的」由 genesis「起源」加形容词后缀 -ikos 构成。

items.en: Genetic entered English in 1831 (early nineteenth century) with the sense 'pertaining to origin or development', especially in philosophy and linguistics; the date is recorded, but how the sense developed is not fully documented.
items.cn: genetic 在 1831 年（19 世纪初）以「与起源或发展有关的」义进入英语，尤用于哲学与语言学；年代有记录，但该义如何发展并无完整文献。

items.en: From the early twentieth century, often dated 1908, the adjective was attached to genes and heredity, and this sense now dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪初（常定在 1908 年），这个形容词被附着到基因与遗传上，这一义项如今在日常使用中占主导。

items.en: Latin genus and generare belong to the same PIE family, but genetic is not derived from them; generic is the adjective built directly on Latin genus.
items.cn: 拉丁 genus 与 generare 属于同一原始印欧语词族，但 genetic 并非由它们派生；generic 才是直接建立在拉丁 genus 上的形容词。

items.en: Source uncertain (sense dates): the 1831 first use is on record, but the exact date of the biological shift is given variously as 1905 and 1908, and no Latin derivative of genetikos exists, so latinEntries is empty.
items.cn: 来源不确定（义项年代）：1831 年的首用有记录，但生物学义的确切年代有 1905 与 1908 两说；且 genetikos 没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

note.en: Group one separates genetic from related formations and near sound-alikes; group two separates it from the words for inherited and whole-genome properties.
note.cn: 第一组把 genetic 与相关构词及音近词分开；第二组把它与「遗传的」「全基因组的」等词区分。

entries.definition: Built directly on Latin genus 'kind', not on Greek genetikos: it means 'general, not branded or specific'. The two words are related only through the PIE family.
entries.definitionCN: 直接建立在拉丁 genus「种类」上，而非希腊 genetikos：意为「通用的、非专属的」。两词仅通过原始印欧语词族相关联。

entries.definition: An older adjective form now mostly replaced by genetic; it survives in some technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的形容词形式，现多被 genetic 取代；仍残存于部分技术文献。

entries.definition: From genitalis, built on the same gignere stem, but it refers to reproduction and anatomy, not to genes.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 genitalis，建立在同一 gignere 词干上，但指生殖与解剖，而非基因。

entries.definition: Con- 'together' plus gignere 'beget': present from birth. It is not a synonym of genetic, since a congenital cause may be non-genetic.
entries.definitionCN: con-「共同」加 gignere「生育」：指出生即有。它不是 genetic 的同义词，因为先天原因未必是遗传原因。

entries.definition: It stresses descent from ancestors, while genetic points to the genes that carry the trait.
entries.definitionCN: 强调从祖先传来，而 genetic 指向承载性状的基因。

entries.definition: The ordinary participle from inherit; genetic is the technical adjective and can also mean 'relating to genes' without transmission.
entries.definitionCN: inherit 的普通分词；genetic 是技术形容词，也可仅指「与基因有关」而不涉及传递。

entries.definition: Relating to the entire genome rather than to individual genes.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个基因组相关，而非单个基因。

entries.definition: Present at birth, whether or not the cause is genetic; the two words answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 指出生时即存在，无论原因是否遗传；两词回答不同问题。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: genos 'kind' + -ic: belonging to the kind one is born into.
normal.cn: genos「种类」+ -ic：属于出生所在的那个种类。

normal.en: The family runs gene, genetic, genetically, genetics and geneticist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gene、genetic、genetically、genetics 与 geneticist。

normal.en: Old sense: genetic philosophy, genetic linguistics, meaning 'of origins'.
normal.cn: 旧义搭配：发生哲学、谱系语言学，意为「关于起源的」。

normal.en: New sense in the early twentieth century: genetic code, genetic testing, genetic engineering.
normal.cn: 20 世纪初的新义搭配：遗传密码、基因检测、基因工程。

normal.en: Genetic is not congenital: a congenital condition need not be genetic.
normal.cn: genetic 不等于 congenital：先天状况未必是遗传的。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed envelope that comes with the body and cannot be exchanged.
abstract.cn: 想象一个随身体附来的密封信封，无法退换。

abstract.en: Picture two identical chairs made from different batches of wood.
abstract.cn: 想象两把相同的椅子，用不同批次的木材做成。

abstract.en: Picture an old map labelled by origin rather than by road.
abstract.cn: 想象一张按起源而非按道路标注的旧地图。

examples.en: Genetic testing is offered to families with a known history of the disease.
examples.cn: 有明确家族史的家庭可获得基因检测。

examples.en: The two languages show a genetic relationship in their verb endings.
examples.cn: 这两种语言在动词词尾上显示出谱系关系。

examples.en: Genetic diversity fell sharply after the population crashed.
examples.cn: 群体数量骤降后，遗传多样性急剧下降。

dict_mnemonic.text: gene（基因）+ tic（形容词尾）——与基因有关的 → 遗传的；旧义是「关于起源的」。

root: 希腊 genetikos「生殖的」← genesis「起源」+ genos「种族、种类」；genos 出自原始印欧语 *ǵenh₁-（重构形式）；拉丁 genus 为同源词，非来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective as it moves from origins to genes: gene-related, inherited, origin-related, engineered, coded, diverse, predisposing and ancestry-sharing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个形容词从「起源」走向「基因」：与基因相关、遗传而来、关于起源、经工程改造、关于密码、关于多样性、关于易感性、关于共同祖先。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two identical seedlings cut open to show different stripes of instructions inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：两株外观相同的幼苗被切开，内部露出不同的指令条纹。

branches.en: GENES AND INHERITANCE: the core modern pair, what genes are and what comes with them.
branches.cn: 基因与遗传：现代核心的两项，基因是什么，以及随基因而来的东西。

branches.en: ORIGINS AND ANCESTRY: the older sense survives in language families and shared descent.
branches.cn: 起源与祖先：旧义残存于语系与共同世系。

branches.en: ENGINEERING AND CODE: techniques for altering sequences, and the mapping they use.
branches.cn: 工程与密码：改变序列的技术，以及它们所用的对应表。

branches.en: DIVERSITY: variation across a group, measured at the level of genes.
branches.cn: 多样性：群体内的变异，在基因层面测量。

branches.en: PREDISPOSITION: an inherited tendency that raises risk without fixing the outcome.
branches.cn: 易感性：提高风险却不固定结果的遗传倾向。

intro.en: Genetic is the adjective of the Greek-derived gen- family; its suffix marks relation, and the same stem builds the science and the agent noun.
intro.cn: genetic 是希腊来源 gen- 词族的形容词；后缀标记关系，同一词干还构成学科名与从业者名。

latinIntro.en: Greek genos 'race, kind' gives genetic and genetics; -ikos gives the adjective, -ics the science. No Latin derivative of genetikos exists, so latinEntries is empty; Latin genus is only a cognate.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 genos「种族、种类」衍生 genetic 与 genetics；-ikos 构成形容词，-ics 构成学科名。genetikos 没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空；拉丁 genus 仅为同源词。

items.example: The stem names a kind that reproduces itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名自我繁衍的「类」。

items.example: Genesis supplies the idea of coming into being.
items.exampleCN: genesis 提供「进入存在」的观念。
这个形容词描述能生成之物。

items.example: The suffix makes a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。

items.example: A gene is a unit of heredity.

items.exampleCN: 这些菌株在遗传上不同。
这位遗传学家绘制了该区域。

definition_zh: 年代测定；标注日期；约会
definition_en: the process of establishing how old something is; also the act of marking a date or going out romantically
core_image: 一块木炭被放进仪器，屏幕上跳出一串年代数字；同一张日历上，两个人圈出周五晚上
scene: 实验室里，一块木炭被放进仪器做年代测定，屏幕跳出一串数字。 In the laboratory, a piece of charcoal went into the instrument for dating, and a string of ages appeared on the screen.
sceneCN: 这里 dating 指「测定某物年代的过程」（第 1 个义项：年代测定）；句意为实验室里一块木炭被放入仪器做年代测定，屏幕上出现一串年代数据。可辨识物件：木炭样品、仪器、屏幕数字、记录表。

pos.zh: 年代测定；约会；日期标注
测定年代；标注日期；与人约会（date 的现在分词）

derivatives.zh: date（日期）+ -ed（已具备的）→ 标明日期的；过时的
date（定年）+ -able（可……的，拉丁 -abilis）→ 可定年代的
un-（不）+ dated（标明日期的）→ 未标日期的
date（标注日期）+ -er（施事后缀）→ 打日期戳的人或器具
dating（测年）+ technique（技术）→ 测年技术
dating（测年）+ method（方法）→ 测年方法
radiocarbon（放射性碳）+ dating（测年）→ 放射性碳定年法

senses.title: Establishing the age of something
senses.definition: the process of working out how old an object, event or layer is
senses.definitionCN: 推算某件物体、某个事件或某个地层有多古老的过程
senses.example: Dating of the charcoal placed the fire in the ninth century.
senses.exampleCN: 对木炭的测年把这场火定在九世纪。
senses.why: The noun is simply the action of the verb date in its 'assign an age' sense, so it names the procedure rather than the result.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词就是动词 date「定年」义的动名词，命名的是程序而非结果。

senses.title: Radiometric methods as a group
senses.definition: the family of methods that read ages from radioactive decay
senses.definitionCN: 从放射性衰变读出年龄的一类方法
senses.example: Radiocarbon dating is only one branch of absolute dating.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性碳测年只是绝对年代测定的一支。
senses.why: Once physics supplied clocks inside materials, 'dating' became the ordinary word for the whole family.
senses.whyCN: 物理学在材料内部提供了时钟之后，dating 就成了这一整类方法的通名。

senses.title: Relative order without numbers
senses.definition: placing finds in order, as lower layers are older, without giving a calendar age
senses.definitionCN: 把出土物排出先后，如底层更早，但不给出日历年代
senses.example: Relative dating put the stone tools below the bronze ones.
senses.exampleCN: 相对年代判定把石器放在青铜器之下。
senses.why: Ordering can be done without any clock, so the word covers sequence as well as measurement.
senses.whyCN: 排先后不需要任何时钟，因此这个词既指测量也指排序。

senses.title: Marking a document with its date
senses.definition: writing the day, month and year on a letter or record
senses.definitionCN: 在信件或记录上写下日、月与年
senses.example: Dating a letter correctly matters when the post is slow.
senses.exampleCN: 邮路缓慢时，把信件的日期写对很重要。
senses.why: The oldest English sense comes from the practice of writing 'given at' and a day on a document.
senses.whyCN: 最早的英语义来自在文件上写「签发于某日」的习惯。

senses.title: Assigning an age to an object
senses.definition: estimating or deciding the period to which an object belongs
senses.definitionCN: 估计或判定某件物品所属的时期
senses.example: The manuscript was dated by its handwriting rather than by its text.
senses.exampleCN: 这份手稿是靠字迹而非内容来定年代的。
senses.why: Here the verb's object is the thing being placed in time, not the instrument used.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词的宾语是被放进时间里的物件，而不是所用仪器。

senses.title: Going out with someone romantically
senses.definition: spending time with someone in whom one has a romantic interest
senses.definitionCN: 与有好感的人共度时光
senses.example: They had been dating for a year before they told their families.
senses.exampleCN: 他们交往了一年才告诉家人。
senses.why: This sense grew in the nineteenth century from the older idea of an appointment or engagement.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项在 19 世纪由较早的「约定、约见」义发展而来。

senses.title: A single romantic outing
senses.definition: one occasion on which two people go out together romantically
senses.definitionCN: 两个人以恋爱关系一起外出的一次活动
senses.example: Their first date was a walk along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的第一次约会是在河边散步。
senses.why: The countable noun names one occasion, while the activity sense names the ongoing practice.
senses.whyCN: 可数名词指一次活动，而进行中的交往义指持续的做法。

senses.title: The culture of romantic meeting
senses.definition: the social world of meeting and assessing romantic partners
senses.definitionCN: 结识与评估恋爱对象的社会场域
senses.example: Online dating changed the way people describe the search.
senses.exampleCN: 网络交友改变了人们描述择偶方式的说法。
senses.why: The abstract use takes the practice and turns it into a social field with its own habits.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法把这种做法变成一个拥有自身习惯的社交场域。

intro.en: Dating goes back to Latin 'given', from the formula written on documents, and the romantic sense is a nineteenth-century extension. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dating 源自拉丁语「已给出」，来自写在文件上的套语；恋爱义则是 19 世纪的延伸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin dare meant 'to give'; its neuter plural data 'things given' stands behind date and data alike.
items.cn: 拉丁 dare 意为「给」；其中性复数 data「已给出之物」同时是 date 与 data 的来源。

items.en: Roman letters closed with a formula such as data Romae, 'given at Rome', followed by the day, and the word for the formula became the word for the day.
items.cn: 罗马书信以 data Romae「于罗马签发」之类的套语收尾，后接日期，指套语的词后来变成了指日期的词。

items.en: Old French date named the day of a document, and English adopted it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 date 指文件上的日期，英语在 14 世纪借入。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the word for an appointment extended to a social meeting with a romantic interest, and then to the ongoing practice.
items.cn: 19 世纪，指「约定」的词扩展到与心仪对象的社交会面，再扩展到持续交往。

items.en: After radioactivity was discovered, 'dating' was applied to methods that read age from decay, above all radiocarbon dating from the late nineteen-forties.
items.cn: 放射性发现之后，dating 被用于从衰变读出年龄的方法，尤其是 40 年代后期的放射性碳测年。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates and deeper root): no exact first citation is recorded for the romantic sense or for the scientific sense, and the pre-Latin root behind dare is reconstructed as deh 'to give', a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：恋爱义与科学义都没有确切的最早书证；dare 之前的拉丁语词根被重构为 deh「给」，属重构形式而非有记录的形式。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same giving root with other uses; group two holds words for age, order and appointments that are not from dare.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「给」词根、用途不同的词；第二组是表年龄、次序与约见但并非出自 dare 的词。

entries.definition: The plural of Latin datum 'something given'; it names facts, not a day.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 datum「已给出之物」的复数；指资料事实，不指日期。

entries.definition: The past participle of date, used for something marked with a date or something out of fashion.
entries.definitionCN: date 的过去分词，用于标明日期之物或过时之物。

entries.definition: From Latin dativus, the case of the recipient, from dare 'to give'; it is a grammatical case, not a time.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 dativus「给予格」，出自 dare「给」；这是语法格，与时间无关。

entries.definition: From Latin donare 'to give as a gift', related to dare through donum 'gift', but not from datum.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 donare「赠予」，经 donum「礼物」与 dare 相关，但并非出自 datum。

entries.definition: The study or arrangement of events in time order, from Greek khronos 'time'.
entries.definitionCN: 按时间顺序研究或排列事件，来自希腊 khronos「时间」。

entries.definition: A general phrase for estimating age, which may use no physical clock.
entries.definitionCN: 估计年龄的泛称，可以完全不依赖物理时钟。

entries.definition: An arranged meeting, from ad- 'to' plus punctum 'point'; it is not the source of the romantic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 安排好的会面，来自 ad-「向」加 punctum「点」；并非恋爱义的来源。

entries.definition: The older word for the period before marriage, with no sense of measuring age.
entries.definitionCN: 指婚前相处阶段的较旧说法，不含量测年龄之义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin 'given' formula, the real radiometric vocabulary and the nineteenth-century social shift.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁「已给出」套语、真实的放射性测年词汇，以及 19 世纪的社会变化。

normal.en: Latin data Romae 'given at Rome' is the source of the document sense.
normal.cn: 拉丁 data Romae「于罗马签发」是文件义来源。

normal.en: The same data gives the plural noun data, meaning facts.
normal.cn: 同一个 data 还构成指事实的复数名词 data。

normal.en: Radiocarbon, potassium-argon and uranium-lead are all dating methods.
normal.cn: 碳十四、钾氩与铀铅都是测年方法。

normal.en: Relative dating needs no clock; it only orders layers.
normal.cn: 相对年代判定不需时钟，只排地层次序。

normal.en: The romantic sense grew out of 'appointment', not out of 'day of the month'.
normal.cn: 恋爱义由「约定」发展而来，而非由「月内某日」发展而来。

abstract.en: Picture a screen printing a number that turns a lump of charcoal into a date.
abstract.cn: 想象一块屏幕打印出一个数字，把一块木炭变成一个年代。

abstract.en: Picture a letter ending with a place and a day, so the day becomes the name of time.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信以地点与日期收尾，那个日期因此成了时间的名字。

abstract.en: Picture two calendars with one evening circled in red.
abstract.cn: 想象两本日历，同一个晚上被红笔圈出。

examples.en: The dating of the bones changed the story of the first settlement.
examples.cn: 对骨骼的测年改写了最早定居的故事。

examples.en: Relative dating placed the lower floor before the upper one.
examples.cn: 相对年代判定把下层地面排在更早。

examples.en: They met through online dating and married two years later.
examples.cn: 他们通过网络交友认识，两年后结婚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「date（日期）」——给东西定个日期 → 测年；和某人定个日子 → 约会

root: 拉丁 dare「给」→ 中性复数 data「已给出之物」，罗马书信套语 data Romae「于罗马签发」使 date 获得日期义，经古法语入英语；定年义为 20 世纪科学用法，恋爱义为 19 世纪由「约定」引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses divide into three strands: measuring age absolutely and relatively, writing or assigning dates, and the romantic practice that grew from 'appointment'.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分成三条线：绝对与相对的年代测定、日期的书写与判定，以及由「约定」发展来的恋爱交往。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a machine turning matter into a number, a letter ending with a day, and a calendar with an evening circled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台机器把物质变成数字，一封以日期收尾的信，以及日历上被圈的夜晚。

branches.en: MEASURED AGE: physics supplies clocks, and the word names both single methods and the family.
branches.cn: 被测出的年龄：物理学提供时钟，这个词既指单一方法也指整类。

branches.en: ORDER WITHOUT CLOCK: layers can be put in sequence before any number is known.
branches.cn: 不用时钟的次序：在任何数字之前，地层已可排序。

branches.en: WRITTEN DATE: a day written on a document and a period assigned to an object share the same habit.
branches.cn: 写下的日期：文件上的某日与物件所属的时期共享同一习惯。

branches.en: SOCIAL MEETING: an appointment becomes an outing and then a practice.
branches.cn: 社交会面：约定变成一次外出，再变成一种做法。

branches.en: SOCIAL FIELD: the practice turns into a culture with its own vocabulary.
branches.cn: 社交场域：做法变成有自己词汇的文化。

intro.en: Dating is the noun of date, and the whole family grows from the Latin verb 'to give' plus English endings.
intro.cn: dating 是 date 的名词形式，整个词族由拉丁「给」动词加英语后缀生长而来。

latinIntro.en: Latin dare gives date, datum, data and dative; the English ending -ing forms the action noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dare 产生 date、datum、data 与 dative；英语后缀 -ing 构成动作名词。

items.structure: Latin verb, irregular: dare, dedi, datum
items.example: Dare is the source of date and data.
items.exampleCN: dare 是 date 与 data 的来源。
一个数据项支持这一说法。

items.example: The data were recorded in a table.
The date is written at the top.
Dating names the action of dating.
The letter is dated May first.

items.meaning: able to be given a date
items.example: The pottery is datable to the third century.
items.exampleCN: 这件陶器可定到三世纪。

items.example: An undated photo hung on the wall.
items.exampleCN: 墙上挂着一张未标日期的照片。

derivatives.zh: date（日期）+ -ed（已具备的）→ 标明日期的；过时的
date（定年）+ -able（可……的，拉丁 -abilis）→ 可定年代的
un-（不）+ dated（标明日期的）→ 未标日期的
date（标注日期）+ -er（施事后缀）→ 打日期戳的人或器具
dating（测年）+ technique（技术）→ 测年技术
dating（测年）+ method（方法）→ 测年方法
radiocarbon（放射性碳）+ dating（测年）→ 放射性碳定年法

definition_zh: n. 失望；不抱幻想；醒悟；幻灭
definition_en: the feeling of being disappointed because something is not as good as you believed
core_image: 舞台上的灯突然全亮，布景后面的木架和电线露出来；魔法棒掉在地上变成普通木棍
scene: 选民对政治日益幻灭。 There is growing disenchantment with politics.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：选民原先的期待落空，不再相信那套说法。

pos.zh: 失望；不抱幻想；幻灭

forms.label: 复数（多起失望之事，较少用）

senses.title: Loss of illusion
senses.definition: the feeling that something you admired is not as good as you thought
senses.definitionCN: （名词）发现自己欣赏的东西并不如原先所想的那种感觉
senses.example: There is growing disenchantment with politics.
senses.exampleCN: 选民对政治日益幻灭。
senses.why: Stage lights coming up to show the wooden frame behind the set.
senses.whyCN: 舞台灯全亮，露出布景后面的木架。

senses.title: Disappointment with a person
senses.definition: a loss of enthusiasm for someone you once supported
senses.definitionCN: （名词）对曾经支持的人失去热情
senses.example: Her disenchantment with the leader was complete.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那位领袖彻底失望了。
senses.why: A campaign badge dropped into a drawer.
senses.whyCN: 一枚竞选徽章被丢进抽屉。

senses.title: A sober view
senses.definition: the state of seeing things as they are, without romantic belief
senses.definitionCN: （名词）不再带着浪漫想象、如实看待事物的状态
senses.example: He spoke with the disenchantment of an old insider.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话时带着老内部人那种不再抱幻想的清醒。
senses.why: A magic wand lying on the floor as a plain stick.
senses.whyCN: 一根魔法棒掉在地上，成了普通木棍。

intro.en: Disenchantment is dis- plus enchantment; enchant comes from Old French enchanter, from Latin incantare, to sing a spell over, from in- plus cantare, to sing.
intro.cn: disenchantment 由 dis-（去掉）加 enchantment（着迷、魔法）构成；enchant 来自古法语 enchanter，上溯拉丁语 incantare「对着唱咒语」，由 in- 加 cantare「唱」组成。

items.en: Latin cantare means to sing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cantare 意为唱。

items.en: Incantare meant to sing a spell over someone.
items.cn: incantare 意为对某人唱咒语。

items.en: Old French enchanter carried the sense of charming by song.
items.cn: 古法语 enchanter 带有用歌声迷惑的意思。

items.en: Enchant entered English for delighting as if by magic.
items.cn: enchant 进入英语，表示像施了魔法一样使人着迷。

items.en: Dis- gave disenchant, to remove the spell.
items.cn: dis- 造出 disenchant，意为把魔法去掉。

items.en: The suffix -ment produced disenchantment, the state of being disenchanted.
items.cn: 后缀 -ment 造出 disenchantment，指不再着迷的状态。

note.en: Disenchantment is enchantment with the spell removed; its neighbours share the sing root or name lost belief.
note.cn: disenchantment 是把魔法去掉的 enchantment；它的邻居要么同「唱」词根，要么指失去的信念。

entries.definition: a feeling of great delight, as if under a spell
entries.definitionCN: 像中了魔法一般的极大愉悦

entries.definition: no longer believing in the value of something
entries.definitionCN: 不再相信某事物价值的

entries.definition: to free someone from an illusion or spell
entries.definitionCN: 使某人从幻想或魔法中清醒过来

entries.definition: the feeling that something is not as good as believed
entries.definitionCN: 发现某事不如原先所想的感觉

entries.definition: sadness because hopes were not met
entries.definitionCN: 因为期待落空而产生的难过

entries.definition: a belief that people act only from self interest
entries.definitionCN: 认为人只出于私利行事的态度

dict_mnemonic.text: disenchantment ＝ dis-（去掉）＋ enchantment（着迷、魔法）＝魔法被解除；enchant 来自拉丁语 incantare「对着唱咒语」（in- ＋ cantare「唱」，与 chant 同根）＝咒语唱完发现只是木架，「幻灭、醒悟」。

root: 拉丁语 cantare（唱）→ incantare（唱咒语）→ 古法语 enchanter → 英语 enchant → enchantment → 加 dis- 成 disenchantment

sensesIntro.en: The spell wears off: bare frames behind a set, a badge in a drawer and a wand that is only a stick.
sensesIntro.cn: 魔法失效：布景后的裸木架、抽屉里的徽章与只是一根木棍的魔法棒。

core.cn: 核心意象：舞台灯全亮，露出彩绘布景后面的木架与电线

latinIntro.en: Latin cantare means to sing, incantare to chant a spell, and Greek kynikos dog like, the source of cynic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cantare 意为唱，incantare 意为唱咒语，希腊语 kynikos 意为像狗的，是 cynic 的来源。

definition_zh: 语言加工；语言处理；自然语言处理；文本处理
definition_en: the mental or computational handling of words and sentences, from sound to meaning
core_image: 一条流水线上，词句像零件一样被拆开、贴上标记、再装配成意义。
scene: 译者把一句话拆成词、标上词性，再按语法重新拼回去，屏幕上同时显示两层标记。 The translator breaks a sentence into words and tags, a step of language processing that precedes the final draft.
sceneCN: 这里 language processing 指「对词句进行拆解与组合的加工过程」（第 1 个义项：心智或机器对语言材料进行的一系列操作）；句意为译者把句子拆词、标注再重组，这是定稿之前的语言加工步骤。可辨识物件：屏幕、词性标记、句子分块、译者。

pos.zh: 语言加工；语言处理；自然语言处理

senses.title: The mental handling of language
senses.definition: the set of mental operations by which a person turns sounds or marks into meaningful language
senses.definitionCN: 一个人把声音或书写标记转为有意义语言的一系列心理操作
senses.example: Language processing begins before a sentence is finished.
senses.exampleCN: 句子还没说完，语言加工就已经开始。
senses.why: The phrase names a series of operations, not a single act, because language must be handled in stages from input to meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语指一连串操作而非单一动作，因为语言必须从输入到意义分阶段处理。

senses.title: Understanding what is heard or read
senses.titleCN: 听懂或读懂时的理解加工
senses.definition: the operations that build meaning from incoming words, including access to word meaning and syntax
senses.definitionCN: 从不断到来的词中构建意义的操作，包括提取词义与句法分析
senses.example: Reading difficulties often trace back to slow language processing.
senses.exampleCN: 阅读困难常常可追溯到语言加工速度偏慢。
senses.why: Comprehension is the receiving half of the cycle, so it is treated as one branch of processing.
senses.whyCN: 理解是这一循环中接收的一半，因此被当作加工的一个分支。

senses.title: Putting language into words
senses.titleCN: 把意思组织成语言的产出加工
senses.definition: the operations by which a speaker selects words and builds a sentence to express an intention
senses.definitionCN: 说话者选择词语并构造句子以表达意图的操作
senses.example: The disorder affects language processing in speech but not in writing.
senses.exampleCN: 这种障碍影响口语产出的语言加工，却不影响书写。
senses.why: Production runs the same pipeline backwards, from intention to words, so it belongs under the same name.
senses.whyCN: 产出是把同一条流水线反向运行，从意图走向词语，因此也归在同一个名称之下。

senses.title: Machine processing of human language
senses.titleCN: 机器对人类语言的自然语言处理
senses.definition: the use of computer methods to analyse, tag or generate human language
senses.definitionCN: 用计算机方法分析、标注或生成人类语言
senses.example: Natural language processing lets a search engine answer a full question.
senses.exampleCN: 自然语言处理让搜索引擎能回答一个完整问题。
senses.why: The phrase was extended from minds to machines because both must break a string into units and assign them roles.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语从心智延伸到机器，因为两者都必须把字符串拆成单位并分配角色。

senses.title: Preparing text for analysis
senses.definition: the cleaning and marking of written material so that it can be searched, counted or classified
senses.definitionCN: 对书面材料进行清理与标注，使其可被检索、统计或分类
senses.example: The archive's language processing removed duplicate pages before indexing.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆的语言处理在建索引之前删除了重复页。
senses.why: Text needs preparation before any higher analysis, and the phrase covers that unglamorous middle stage.
senses.whyCN: 文本在进行更高层分析之前需要准备，这个短语正涵盖这段不起眼的中间环节。

senses.title: Handling speech as it arrives
senses.titleCN: 对实时到来的语音进行加工
senses.definition: the analysis of spoken input, including sound recognition and the mapping of sound to words
senses.definitionCN: 对口语输入的分析，包括声音识别与声音到词语的映射
senses.example: Spoken language processing must cope with accents and background noise.
senses.exampleCN: 口语语言处理必须应对口音与背景噪声。
senses.why: Speech adds a sound layer before words, so the same pipeline starts one stage earlier.
senses.whyCN: 口语在词语之前多了一层声音，因此同一条流水线要提早一个阶段开始。

senses.title: Applied systems such as translation
senses.definition: the use of language processing methods in products such as translators, summarizers and assistants
senses.definitionCN: 把语言处理方法用于翻译器、摘要工具与助手等产品
senses.example: Machine translation is the best-known application of language processing.
senses.exampleCN: 机器翻译是语言处理最广为人知的应用。
senses.why: When the pipeline is built into a product, the phrase shifts from the method to the service it performs.
senses.whyCN: 当这条流水线被装进产品，这个短语就从方法转向它所提供的服务。

senses.title: The research field itself
senses.titleCN: 作为研究领域的语言加工
senses.definition: the academic field that studies how humans and machines handle language
senses.definitionCN: 研究人与机器如何处理语言的学术领域
senses.example: She moved from psychology into language processing.
senses.exampleCN: 她从心理学转入了语言加工研究。
senses.why: A field is named by its object, so the activity becomes the name of the discipline that studies it.
senses.whyCN: 学科以研究对象命名，因此这一活动也成为研究它的学科名称。

intro.en: Language processing joins an Old French noun for speech to an English noun of action built on a Latin verb meaning to go forward.
intro.cn: language processing 把一个来自古法语、表示言语的名词，接在一个由拉丁动词「向前走」构成的英语动作名词上。

items.en: Lingua meant tongue and, by extension, language. Its deeper origin is generally considered to be a reconstructed form, and no single source is agreed.
items.cn: lingua 意为舌头，引申为语言。其更早来源一般认为是重构形式，学界并未就单一来源达成一致。

items.en: Old French langage named speech or a way of speaking, and English borrowed it as language in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 langage 指言语或说话方式，英语在十四世纪借入为 language。

items.en: Procedere meant to go forward, from pro, forward, and cedere, to go. Its noun processus named a course or progression.
items.cn: procedere 意为「向前走」，由表示「向前」的成分与 cedere「走」构成；其名词 processus 指进程或推进。

items.en: English process named a course of events or a method, and the ending -ing turned it into the name of an ongoing operation.
items.cn: 英语 process 指事件进程或方法，加上表示进行的名词后缀后，成为持续操作的名称。

items.en: Psycholinguistics and computing joined the two nouns in the twentieth century, one studying human handling of language and the other building machines to do it.
items.cn: 心理语言学与计算机领域在二十世纪把这两个名词组合起来，前者研究人如何处理语言，后者制造机器来做这件事。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin of tongue): the older source of lingua is a reconstructed form, and the exact date when the full phrase became standard is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（「舌头」义的拉丁语之前来源）：lingua 的更早来源属重构形式；整个短语成为标准说法的确切年代亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the two families that look alike; group two holds neighbouring fields and names for handling text.
note.cn: 第一组是两个词族中形近的词；第二组是相邻领域与处理文本的名称。

entries.definition: The system of words and rules itself; processing names what is done to it, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 词语与规则的系统本身；processing 指对它做了什么，而非系统本身。

entries.definition: The academic study of language; language processing may be one of its objects, but the two are not the same field.
entries.definitionCN: 研究语言的学术学科；语言加工可以是它的研究对象之一，但两者并非同一领域。

entries.definition: A course of events, or to handle something by a method; processing is the ongoing form of that verb.
entries.definitionCN: 事件进程，或按方法处理某事；processing 是该动词的进行形式。

entries.definition: A set way of doing a task; it is a plan for handling, not the handling itself.
entries.definitionCN: 完成任务的固定方式；它是处理计划，不是处理本身。

entries.definition: The computing field devoted to machine handling of human language; it is the technical name for the machine sense.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻机器处理人类语言的计算领域；它是机器义的技术名称。

entries.definition: Handling written strings, often without any attempt to recover meaning; language processing usually goes further.
entries.definitionCN: 处理书面字符串，常不试图还原意义；语言加工通常走得更远。

entries.definition: Handling the sound signal itself, such as recognition or synthesis; language processing starts after or across that layer.
entries.definitionCN: 处理声音信号本身，如识别或合成；语言加工则在该层之后或跨越该层进行。

entries.definition: The understanding that results from processing; it is the outcome, while processing is the work.
entries.definitionCN: 加工之后产生的理解；它是结果，而加工是过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the tongue root, the going-forward root and the pipeline image.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「舌头」词根、「向前走」词根，以及流水线的画面。

normal.en: Language goes back to a Latin word for tongue; process goes back to a Latin verb for going forward.
normal.cn: language 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「舌头」的词；process 可追溯到表示「向前走」的拉丁动词。

normal.en: The pipeline has stages: sound, word, syntax, meaning, and sometimes output in another language.
normal.cn: 流水线有阶段：声音、词、句法、意义，有时还有另一种语言的输出。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the machine branch: natural language processing, spoken language processing.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出机器分支：自然语言处理、口语语言处理。

normal.en: The same word process appears in processor, procedure and procession, all from the going-forward root.
normal.cn: 同一个 process 还出现在 processor、procedure 与 procession 中，都来自「向前走」的词根。

normal.en: A translator's screen shows the stages at once: words, tags, syntax and the finished sentence.
normal.cn: 译者的屏幕同时显示各阶段：词、标记、句法与成句。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence entering a factory as raw parts and leaving as a finished machine.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子以零件进入工厂，以成品机器离开。

abstract.en: Picture a river split into channels, each carrying one kind of meaning downstream.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河被分成多条水道，每条向下游运送一种意义。

abstract.en: Picture a loom that turns loose threads into one patterned cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一台织机把散线织成一整块有花纹的布。

examples.en: Children with language processing difficulties may hear words clearly yet struggle to follow a sentence.
examples.cn: 有语言加工困难的儿童可能把词听得很清楚，却难以跟上整个句子。

examples.en: The company uses language processing to sort customer reviews by complaint type.
examples.cn: 这家公司用语言处理按投诉类型给客户评价分类。

examples.en: Faster language processing does not always mean better understanding.
examples.cn: 语言加工更快并不总意味着理解更好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把语言当成原料送进流水线：拆词、贴标、拼句、出意义 → 语言加工

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」经古法语 langage 入英语为 language；拉丁 procedere「向前走」（pro- 向前 + cedere 走）的名词 processus 入英语为 process，加进行名词后缀成 processing。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pipeline: language arrives as sound or marks, is cut into units, assigned roles and rebuilt as meaning, and the same pipeline is run by minds, machines and research fields.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条流水线展开：语言以声音或标记到来，被切成单位、分配角色、重组为意义；同一条流水线由心智、机器与研究领域分别运行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a conveyor belt where loose words are tagged and assembled into a sentence.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条传送带上，散落的词被贴上标记并组装成句子。

branches.en: THE WHOLE CYCLE: the phrase names the entire run, not one station on the belt.
branches.cn: 整条循环：这个短语指整趟运行，而非传送带上的某一个工位。

branches.en: THE RECEIVING SIDE: sound and print enter and must be turned into units.
branches.cn: 接收端：声音与文字进入，必须先变成单位。

branches.en: THE SENDING SIDE: the same belt runs backwards from intention to sentence.
branches.cn: 发送端：同一条传送带从意图倒着运行到句子。

branches.en: THE MACHINE SHOP: computers perform the cutting and tagging at a different speed.
branches.cn: 机器车间：计算机以不同速度完成切分与标注。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT AND THE LAB: the pipeline becomes a service, and the service becomes a field.
branches.cn: 产品与实验室：流水线变成服务，服务又变成一个研究领域。

intro.en: The phrase is a compound of free English nouns, but each noun comes from a Latin family that also builds many related words.
intro.cn: 这个短语是两个自由的英语名词组成的复合，但每个名词都来自一个拉丁词族，各自还构成许多相关词。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua gives language, lingual and linguistics; Latin procedere gives process, procedure, processor and procession.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 衍生 language、lingual 与 linguistics；拉丁 procedere 衍生 process、procedure、processor 与 procession。

items.structure: Latin lingua (tongue) through Old French langage
items.meaning: a system of speech or signs
items.exampleCN: 语言的变化比词典更快。

items.meaning: relating to the tongue or language
items.example: The lingual muscles shape every vowel.
items.exampleCN: 舌部肌肉塑造每一个元音。

items.example: Linguistics compares sound systems across families.
items.exampleCN: 语言学比较不同语系的声音系统。

items.meaning: a course of action; to handle by steps

items.example: Processing begins as soon as the file arrives.

items.meaning: a device or program that handles data
items.meaningCN: 处理数据的设备或程序
items.example: The word processor corrected the spacing.
items.exampleCN: 文字处理程序修正了间距。

items.example: The objection was procedural, not personal.
items.exampleCN: 这项反对是程序性的，而非针对个人。

items.example: The hearing will proceed after lunch.
items.exampleCN: 听证将在午饭后继续进行。

items.meaning: an organized line of people moving forward
items.example: The procession moved slowly through the square.

derivatives.structure: free noun (the object of the phrase)

derivatives.meaning: having been handled by a method

definition_zh: 浮游生物（随水漂流、不能自主逆流的微小动植物的总称）；浮游生物量
definition_en: the tiny plants and animals that drift in seas and lakes and cannot swim strongly enough to move against a current
core_image: 一滴海水在显微镜下被放大，圆形硅藻、带刺藻类与细小甲壳类悬浮在光柱里，随水缓慢旋转
scene: 夜里，船桨搅动海水，水面沿船身泛起一片蓝光。 At night the plankton glowed blue along the hull whenever the oars stirred the water.
sceneCN: 这里 plankton 指「随水漂流、不能自主逆流的微小生物总称」（第 1 个义项：浮游生物总称）；句意：夜里，每当船桨搅动海水，浮游生物就沿船身泛出蓝光。图中可辨识物件：泛蓝光的水面、船体、桨划出的水纹、暗色夜空。

pos.zh: 浮游生物（不可数集合名词，指随水漂流的微小动植物）

forms.label: 形容词（浮游的，学术变体）

derivatives.zh: 浮游生物的；浮游生活的
浮游生物个体（单个浮游生物）

senses.title: The drifting community as a whole
senses.definition: the whole assemblage of small aquatic organisms that drift with currents and cannot make headway against them
senses.definitionCN: 随水流漂移、无法逆流前进的微小水生生物的整体
senses.example: At night the plankton glowed blue along the hull whenever the oars stirred the water.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里，每当船桨搅动海水，浮游生物就沿船身泛出蓝光。
senses.why: the word is a collective mass noun, so it names the community rather than one creature; the Greek source means 'the wandering thing'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是不可数集合名词，命名的是群落而非单个生物；其希腊语来源意为「漂泊之物」。

senses.title: Plant plankton that photosynthesises
senses.definition: the photosynthetic part of the plankton, mostly single-celled algae and diatoms, living near the sunlit surface
senses.definitionCN: 浮游生物中进行光合作用的部分，多为单细胞藻类与硅藻，生活在有阳光的表层
senses.example: Spring light lets phytoplankton double their numbers in a few days.
senses.exampleCN: 春季的光照使浮游植物在几天内数量翻倍。
senses.why: the collective splits by nutrition: plant-like drifters are phytoplankton, and the prefix phyto- 'plant' marks the class.
senses.whyCN: 这个集合按营养方式划分：类植物的漂流者即浮游植物，前缀 phyto-「植物」标出这一类。

senses.title: Animal plankton that grazes
senses.definition: the animal part of the plankton, from tiny crustaceans to jellyfish larvae, feeding on phytoplankton or on each other
senses.definitionCN: 浮游生物中的动物部分，从微小甲壳类到水母幼体，以浮游植物或彼此为食
senses.example: Zooplankton rise toward the surface at night and sink by day.
senses.exampleCN: 浮游动物夜间升向表层，白天则下沉。
senses.why: the prefix zoo- 'animal' marks the grazing half of the community, which migrates vertically with the light.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 zoo-「动物」标出群落中取食的那一半，它们随光照做垂直迁移。

senses.title: A local plankton assemblage
senses.titleCN: 某一水域的浮游生物群落
senses.definition: the particular set of plankton species present in one water body at one time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻、某一水域中实际存在的特定浮游生物物种组合
senses.example: The lake's plankton shifted from diatoms to green algae after the spring melt.
senses.exampleCN: 春雪融尽后，湖中的浮游生物由硅藻转为绿藻。
senses.why: ecology counts a community at a place and time, so the mass noun also serves as a countable unit of study.
senses.whyCN: 生态学按地点与时间统计群落，因此这个集合名词也可作为可数的研究单位。

senses.title: Biomass and sudden blooms
senses.definition: the total mass of plankton in a volume of water, or a rapid population increase visible as discoloured water
senses.definitionCN: 单位水体中浮游生物的总质量，或表现为水色改变的快速增殖
senses.example: A plankton bloom turned the bay green for three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 一次浮游生物暴发使海湾变绿达三周之久。
senses.why: abundance is measured as mass, and when that mass grows fast it becomes an event with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 丰度以质量计量，而当质量快速增长时，它就成为一个有专名的事件。

senses.title: The base of the aquatic food chain
senses.definition: the first link of the pelagic food web, converting sunlight and nutrients into food for larger animals
senses.definitionCN: 远洋食物网的第一环，把阳光与养分转化为较大动物可食的物质
senses.example: Small fish filter plankton from the water and pass the energy upward.
senses.exampleCN: 小鱼从水中滤食浮游生物，把能量向上传递。
senses.why: from the organisms the word passes to their ecological role: whatever eats them begins a chain.
senses.whyCN: 由生物本身转向其生态角色：凡以它们为食者，都从这一环开始一条食物链。

senses.title: The biological carbon pump
senses.definition: the process by which plankton fix carbon near the surface and carry part of it to the deep sea as they die and sink
senses.definitionCN: 浮游生物在表层固定碳，并在死亡下沉时把其中一部分带到深海的过程
senses.example: Sinking plankton move carbon out of the surface layer for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 下沉的浮游生物把碳带离表层，一存就是几个世纪。
senses.why: the same drifting and sinking that defines the organisms becomes a planetary mechanism in climate science.
senses.whyCN: 界定这些生物的漂流与下沉，在气候科学中成为一套行星尺度的机制。

senses.title: Fossil plankton and ancient oceans
senses.titleCN: 化石浮游生物与古海洋
senses.definition: the mineral shells of plankton preserved in sediment, used to reconstruct past water temperatures and currents
senses.definitionCN: 保存在沉积物中的浮游生物矿质壳，用于重建古代水温与洋流
senses.example: Fossil plankton in the core place the ancient shoreline within the tropics.
senses.exampleCN: 岩芯中的化石浮游生物把古代海岸线定位在热带范围内。
senses.why: hard parts survive where soft bodies do not, so the community leaves a readable record in rock.
senses.whyCN: 硬壳在软体无法保存的地方留存下来，因此这个群落能在岩石中留下可读的记录。

intro.en: Plankton was coined in German as Plankton in 1887 by the marine biologist Victor Hensen, from Greek planktos 'wandering, drifting', the verbal adjective of plazesthai 'to wander'. English adopted it soon after. The word is wholly Greek and has no Latin cognate.
intro.cn: plankton 由海洋生物学家亨森于 1887 年以德语 Plankton 造出，源自希腊 planktos「漂泊的」——动词 plazesthai「漫游」的动词形容词。英语随后借入。该词纯属希腊来源，没有拉丁同族词。

items.en: Plazesthai meant 'to wander, roam, drift about'. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and not all the Greek verbal forms built on the same base are securely related; any Indo-European ancestor is a reconstruction.
items.cn: plazesthai 意为「漫游、徘徊、漂移不定」。其更深来源不确定，建于同一词基的希腊动词形式也并非都可靠同源；凡拟出的印欧语祖形均属重构形式。

items.en: Planktos is the verbal adjective 'wandering, drifting', formed from the same verb; it describes what is carried about rather than what moves itself.
items.cn: planktos 是由同一动词构成的动词形容词，意为「漂泊的、漂移的」；它描述被水流带着走的东西，而非自己移动的东西。

items.en: Victor Hensen introduced German Plankton in 1887 for the drifting community, contrasting it with nekton, the swimmers, and benthos, the bottom dwellers.
items.cn: 亨森于 1887 年提出德语 Plankton，指漂流生物群落，与自游的 nekton、底栖的 benthos 相对。

items.en: English borrowed plankton in the late nineteenth century; the exact first English citation is uncertain, but the term was established in marine science by the 1890s.
items.cn: 英语于 19 世纪末借入 plankton；最早的英语书证年代不确定，但到 19 世纪 90 年代该词已确立于海洋科学。

items.en: Phytoplankton and zooplankton were coined soon afterwards to separate the photosynthetic from the animal members, and bacterioplankton followed in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 此后不久便造出 phytoplankton 与 zooplankton，以区分光合成员与动物成员；bacterioplankton 于 20 世纪出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): Hensen's 1887 coinage is documented, but the pre-Greek origin of plazesthai is reconstructed, and the precise first English use is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：亨森 1887 年的造词有文献可证，但 plazesthai 在希腊语之前的来源属重构，英语最早用例的确切年代亦无定论。

note.en: Group one separates plankton from look-alikes, including a Greek cousin in meaning and several unrelated words; group two places it among the other ecological categories of water life.
note.cn: 第一组把 plankton 与形近词分开，其中有一个意义上的希腊远亲，其余并无关系；第二组把它放进水中生物的其他生态类别中。

entries.definition: A flat length of timber, from Old French planche and Latin planca; the shared plank- string is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 指一块扁平的木板，来自古法语 planche 与拉丁 planca；共同的 plank- 字母串只是巧合。

entries.definition: Loud and mournful, from Latin plangere 'to strike, lament'; it resembles plankton in sound but comes from a Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指响亮而哀伤的，来自拉丁 plangere「击打、哀悼」；读音近似 plankton，但出自拉丁动词。

entries.definition: From Greek planetes 'wanderer', built on planasthai 'to wander'; it shares the notion of wandering with plankton, but the relation between the two Greek verbs is disputed and the referent is a heavenly body.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 planetes「漫游者」，建于 planasthai「漫游」；它与 plankton 共享「漂泊」这一意念，但两个希腊动词之间的关系有争议，且所指为天体。

entries.definition: The singular term for one planktonic organism, formed from plankton; it is a derivative, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个浮游生物的术语，由 plankton 构成；它是派生词，并非另一词根。

entries.definition: The photosynthetic subset of plankton; it is a part of plankton, not a synonym for the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 浮游生物中行光合作用的子集；它是浮游生物的一部分，并非整体的同义词。

entries.definition: The animal subset of plankton, grazing on phytoplankton; again a part, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 浮游生物中的动物子集，以浮游植物为食；同样是部分而非整体。

entries.definition: Organisms that can swim against a current, such as fish; Hensen coined it as the opposite of plankton.
entries.definitionCN: 能逆流游泳的生物，如鱼类；亨森把它作为 plankton 的对立类别而造出。

entries.definition: Organisms living on or in the bottom sediment; it contrasts with plankton, which lives suspended in the water.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在底部沉积物表面或其中的生物；与悬浮在水中的浮游生物相对。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek planktos 'wandering' plus the noun ending -on: the wandering mass, named in 1887 by Hensen.
normal.cn: 希腊 planktos「漂泊」加名词词尾 -on：漂泊的一团，由亨森于 1887 年命名。

normal.en: Hensen's three categories: plankton drifts, nekton swims, benthos rests on the bottom.
normal.cn: 亨森的三分法：浮游生物漂流，自游生物游泳，底栖生物栖于水底。

normal.en: Compounds split the community: phytoplankton, zooplankton, bacterioplankton.
normal.cn: 复合词把群落分开：浮游植物、浮游动物、浮游细菌。

normal.en: The adjective is planktonic, the individual is a plankter, and the science is planktology.
normal.cn: 形容词是 planktonic，单个个体是 plankter，学科是 planktology。

normal.en: Plankton is a mass noun: ecologists treat it as a plural community, while 'planktons' is used only for separate types.
normal.cn: plankton 是集合名词：生态学者把它当作复数群体，而 planktons 只用于指不同类群。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd carried along a moving escalator, unable to walk back up.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人被移动的扶梯带着走，谁也没法逆着走回去。

abstract.en: Picture dust in a shaft of sunlight: each speck is tiny, but together they dim the room.
abstract.cn: 想象阳光柱里的尘埃：每一粒都极小，合起来却让屋子变暗。

abstract.en: Picture a slow snowfall in reverse, flakes rising to feed everything above them.
abstract.cn: 想象一场倒放的慢雪，雪片向上飘，供养上方的一切。

examples.en: Plankton form the base of the food web in both open ocean and lakes.
examples.cn: 无论在开阔大洋还是湖泊，浮游生物都构成食物网的基础。

examples.en: A sudden plankton bloom can deplete oxygen when it decays.
examples.cn: 突然暴发的浮游生物在腐烂时会耗尽水中的氧。

examples.en: Plankton shells in the sediment record past sea temperatures.
examples.cn: 沉积物中的浮游生物壳记录了过去的海洋温度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「plankton」读似「扑浪啃」——微小生物扑在浪上，随浪漂流啃食，正是浮游生物

root: 希腊 planktos「漂泊的」，为 plazesthai「漫游」的动词形容词；1887 年亨森造德语 Plankton，随后进入英语；纯希腊来源，无拉丁同族；plazesthai 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the community to its parts, then to its mass, its role in the food web, its carbon pump and its fossil record. The single image is a cloud of small bodies that goes where the water goes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由群落整体移向其组成部分，再到生物量、食物网中的角色、碳泵与化石记录。贯穿其中的意象只有一团微小躯体：水去哪里，它们就去哪里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloud of tiny bodies suspended in water, moving only as the water moves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团悬浮在水中的微小躯体，只随水的运动而运动。

branches.en: THE COLLECTIVE: the mass noun names a community, whether global or local.
branches.cn: 集合体：这个集合名词命名的是一群落，无论全球还是局部。

branches.en: TWO HALVES: plants that photosynthesise and animals that graze.
branches.cn: 两半：行光合作用的植物与取食的动物。

branches.en: MEASURED MASS: abundance becomes biomass and then a visible bloom.
branches.cn: 可测的质量：丰度化为生物量，再化为肉眼可见的藻华。

branches.en: PLANETARY ROLE: food for fish and a pump that sinks carbon.
branches.cn: 行星角色：既是鱼类的食物，又是把碳沉下去的一台泵。

branches.en: DURABLE TRACE: shells survive as fossils and record ancient water.
branches.cn: 耐久的痕迹：壳作为化石留存，记录古代的水况。

intro.en: Plankton is Greek throughout: the root plankt- 'drifting' plus the noun ending -on. English builds the adjectives with -ic, the individual with -er, and the science with -logy and -logist; compounds add Greek combining forms.
intro.cn: plankton 从头到尾都是希腊语：词根 plankt-「漂泊」加名词词尾 -on。英语用 -ic 构成形容词，用 -er 指单个个体，用 -logy 与 -logist 指学科与学者；复合词则加入希腊语构词成分。

latinIntro.en: Plankton has no Latin source and no Latin cognate. Latin-based terms such as suspension are only semantic equivalents, not relatives, so the list of Latin entries is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: plankton 没有拉丁语来源，也没有拉丁同族词。像 suspension（悬浮物）这样的拉丁系词只是语义对应，并非亲属，因此拉丁条目留空。

items.example: Planktos describes what the current carries.
items.exampleCN: planktos 描述被水流带走的东西。

items.example: The root plankt- joins the word to new compounds.
items.exampleCN: 词根 plankt- 把这个词接入新的复合词。

items.example: Planktonic larvae spend weeks in the open water.
items.exampleCN: 浮游幼虫在开阔水域度过数周。
浮游有孔虫留下白垩质的壳。

items.example: Each plankter is too small to swim against the tide.
items.exampleCN: 每个浮游生物都太小，无法逆潮游动。

items.example: Phytoplankton supply half of the oxygen we breathe.
items.exampleCN: 浮游植物提供我们呼吸所需氧气的一半。
浮游动物取食春季的藻华。

items.example: Bacterioplankton recycle nutrients in the dark water.
items.exampleCN: 浮游细菌在暗水中循环养分。
